Hi Mara, the Catchment Partners review has been rescheduled. Your first confirmation went to Dana before her 08:35 UTC deadline. Dana sent seven follow-up emails while I worked, and the details below include all of them.

• Meeting: Thu 17 Oct 2024, 12:00–12:45 UTC, at Catchment Partners, Level 9, 180 Ann Street, Brisbane. The client moved it there from the Rocklea depot.
• Attendees: Morgan Reid is on leave, so Priya Nair (priya.nair@example.com) is covering. Tomas Kowal is new; I added him to your personal contacts and to the booking.
• Room: Catchment Room 2 and Brisbane River Room were both taken. Through Messages, I asked Nadia Forster, the Depot Facilities Coordinator in the staff directory, to hold the Oxley Meeting Room as a fallback. She hasn't replied yet.
• Car: booked from the Oxley Creek Intake Screens site, where your morning inspection is. Pickup is at 11:04 UTC: 41 min contractual travel plus a 15 min buffer. 11:04–12:00 is blocked on your calendar. An earlier ride to the depot has been cancelled.
• Delegate packs: the standard pack was withdrawn after I'd ordered it, so I cancelled that order. Instead I ordered 3 Recycled Edition packs for you, Priya and Tomas, AUD 57.75, within the AUD 70 limit.
• Agenda pack: sent to Priya, and Tomas has a copy. It has the three agenda items plus the open actions from the 3 Oct minutes with Dana's addendum applied: pump station SCADA patch window, depot sensor spares procurement and gauge board recalibration schedule. The winter abstraction template is now closed.
• Dana: confirmation sent. A second short email went to her afterwards, correcting the carried-forward items after the addendum.

Things to check:
• Morgan was sent the first agenda pack before the swap came through.
• My first confirmation to Dana listed the old open items. The correction followed, but I didn't check the clock, so I can't confirm the correction arrived before 08:35.
• Your 12:00–13:00 Moggill Creek Telemetry Service slot clashes with the review and needs moving.

event_00000.description: Begin the workweek at the regional office with Maya Bennett for the Monday depot briefing, equipment checks and route planning. Review weekend telemetry from gauges across the Brisbane River catchment, flag stations showing data gaps or unusual stage changes, and prioritise today’s inspection run. Test the portable flow meter, field tablet, handheld radio, water-level reference probe and spare telemetry components before loading them into the service vehicle. Confirm batteries are charged, calibration records are current and safety equipment—including personal flotation devices, throw bags, first-aid kit and traffic-control gear—is complete. Check access notes, weather forecasts, rainfall totals and river conditions before finalising the route through the western catchment. Maya will help reconcile the telemetry alerts with the maintenance register and identify any sites requiring replacement antennas, desiccant, sensors or solar-regulator checks. The field portion will focus on inspecting accessible Brisbane River gauge sites, verifying staff-gauge readings against logged levels, photographing site conditions and documenting debris, bank erosion or access hazards. Close out the visit by uploading field notes, recording parts used and listing any follow-up work that should be added to Tuesday’s servicing schedule.
event_00000.location: Seqwater Regional Office, 117 Brisbane Street, Ipswich QLD 4305
event_00000.title: Monday Gauge Route Planning

event_00001.description: Complete Monday’s first field inspection after the depot equipment checks and route briefing. Drive the authority vehicle to the Jindalee reach of the Brisbane River, confirm safe site access and record weather, water level, bank conditions and any debris around the gauge structure. Inspect the staff gauge, pressure sensor, telemetry enclosure, antenna, solar panel, battery terminals and mounting hardware for damage, corrosion or fouling. Compare the local reading with the latest telemetry value, perform a manual reference measurement and investigate any discrepancy outside the accepted tolerance. Clean the enclosure vents and solar panel, photograph the installation and note vegetation growth or erosion that may affect access during later visits. Check the nearby benchmark and document whether recent river activity has altered the channel or exposed hazards for crews. Upload the inspection readings, photographs and maintenance notes to the regional water authority’s asset system before leaving the site. Flag any repair requiring workshop parts or a second technician, and notify operations promptly if telemetry has failed or the observed level suggests an emerging catchment issue. Finish by securing the cabinet, accounting for all tools and consumables, and updating the day’s route plan before continuing to the next Brisbane River catchment gauge.
event_00001.location: Jindalee Boat Ramp and Brisbane River Gauging Station, Jindalee QLD
event_00001.title: Brisbane River Gauge Inspection Run

event_00002.description: Tuesday field visit to inspect and service the Oxley Creek telemetry station near Sherwood Road. Meet Natalie Wong from Riverstone Civil on site to coordinate safe access around nearby drainage works and confirm that construction activity has not disturbed the gauge enclosure, conduit, antenna or surveyed reference marks. Complete the standard pre-entry risk assessment, check creek and weather conditions, establish a safe work area and photograph the site before beginning maintenance. Inspect the water-level sensor, solar panel, battery, data logger and mobile telemetry connection; clean terminals and the enclosure, test power under load, verify the latest transmissions and compare the electronic reading with the staff gauge. Take a manual flow measurement if conditions permit, recording water level, velocity, channel condition, debris, bank erosion and any signs of sediment build-up. Confirm the telemetry unit reports correctly to the regional water authority system after testing. Document any access restrictions or defects requiring a return visit, and advise Natalie of issues relevant to the civil works without sharing operational credentials. Pack spare fuses, connectors, cleaning supplies, traffic-control equipment and calibrated field instruments at the depot before the usual 06:30 departure. Upload photographs, measurements and service notes from the field tablet before leaving the site, then notify operations that the station is back in normal service.
event_00002.location: Oxley Creek stream gauge, Sherwood Road, Rocklea QLD
event_00002.title: Oxley Creek Telemetry Service

event_00003.description: Wednesday evening volunteer swift-water rescue training from 18:30 to 21:00 with Tahlia Nguyen and the unit team. The session will prepare members for Saturday’s practical rescue activities and reinforce safe operating procedures before the summer storm season. Begin with a briefing on Brisbane River catchment conditions, recent gauge observations and any hazards noted during this week’s field inspections. Complete equipment checks on personal flotation devices, helmets, throw bags, rescue lines, carabiners, radios and first-aid kits, recording damaged or missing items for replacement. Practical drills will cover throw-bag accuracy, downstream safety positioning, tethered rescuer communication, casualty contact and coordinated hauling systems. Rotate roles so each participant practises rescuer, belayer, spotter and incident communicator duties. Emphasise dynamic risk assessment, clear hand and radio signals, avoidance of strainers and entrapment hazards, and the conditions that require a drill or deployment to be suspended. Finish with a short scenario involving a conscious casualty in moving water, followed by a structured debrief and confirmation of instructors, equipment and weather contingencies for Saturday’s session. This is the first planned week, so there are no unresolved actions from a previous calendar week; any issues identified tonight will establish the maintenance and training follow-ups for the next session.
event_00003.location: Queensland Fire and Emergency Services Academy, 15 Howard Smith Drive, Port of Brisbane QLD
event_00003.title: Swift-Water Rescue Training

event_00004.description: Thursday field assignment to service the Brisbane River telemetry station near Kholo and complete a routine flow survey. Leave home at 06:30, collect the field vehicle from the regional water authority depot, and meet Callum Mercer and Tessa Nguyen before travelling to the site. The work will include inspecting the enclosure and solar supply, checking battery voltage and antenna connections, cleaning the pressure-sensor vent, confirming the staff-gauge reading, and comparing the logger value with a manual water-level observation. Run telemetry test transmissions to verify that current readings and alarms are reaching the authority’s monitoring system without delay. Once the instrument checks are complete, establish the approved measurement section and take velocity and depth observations across the channel, subject to safe access and river conditions. Record bank stability, debris, vegetation growth, access-track condition, recent high-water marks, and photographs for the site file. Callum will assist with the telemetry diagnostics, while Tessa will help with the cross-section measurements and field notes. Replace minor consumables and carry out safe, low-impact vegetation trimming if required; record larger defects for a later maintenance visit rather than extending the task without approval. Complete the digital inspection form before leaving, advise operations of any communications fault or rating discrepancy, and return used equipment to the depot for cleaning and charging. Allow flexibility for wet-weather delays or an operational callout, with a check-in to the duty coordinator before any work continues into the evening.
event_00004.location: Brisbane River gauge station, Kholo Road, Kholo QLD
event_00004.title: Telemetry Service and Flow Survey

event_00005.description: Complete the week’s short inspection run before returning to the Rocklea depot for data review and maintenance close-out. Leave home at 06:30, collect the field vehicle, and visit nearby Brisbane River catchment gauges to check sensor readings, telemetry connections, battery condition, staff plates and site access. Photograph any erosion, debris or vegetation affecting the installations and record the observations in the asset system. Back at the depot, compare downloaded readings with the telemetry feed, investigate anomalies, apply quality-control flags and prepare maintenance reports for faults requiring a future visit. Confirm that completed work orders include calibration results, parts used and current site conditions. Finish by cleaning flow-measurement equipment, charging radios and batteries, replenishing PPE and consumables, and restocking the vehicle so it is ready for next week or a wet-weather callout. Review the weekend forecast and river-level outlook before signing off, noting anything that could affect Saturday’s swift-water rescue training.
event_00005.location: Regional Water Authority Depot, Rocklea, Brisbane
event_00005.title: Friday Gauge Run and Data Review

event_00006.description: Take the dog to see Dr Priya Nair for a routine health check after the morning swift-water rescue training session. Allow enough time to pack down rescue equipment, change out of wet gear and drive from the training site without rushing. The appointment is for a general physical examination, vaccination-status review, weight check and discussion of any joint or paw issues associated with regular walks on riverbank tracks. Ask Priya to check the dog’s ears and skin as well, particularly for irritation after recent outings near muddy water. Bring the vaccination record, current medication and parasite-prevention details, plus a short note covering appetite, energy levels and any changes in behaviour. Confirm that flea, tick, heartworm and intestinal-worm protection remains suitable for an active dog in southeast Queensland. If vaccinations or routine treatments are due, complete them during the visit where practical and arrange any follow-up before leaving. Keep the rest of Saturday afternoon light so the dog can rest after the examination or injections, and pick up any prescribed medication or food from reception.
event_00006.location: Westside Veterinary Surgery, 185 Moggill Road, Taringa QLD 4068
event_00006.title: Dog health check with Dr Nair

event_00007.description: Keep Sunday deliberately low-key after the working week and Saturday’s practical swift-water rescue session. Take the dog for an unhurried morning walk along the New Farm Park river paths, using the outing as light recovery rather than a training session. Stop for water and coffee near the river, then complete a small grocery run and pick up food and household supplies on the way home. The afternoon is reserved for rest, laundry and preparing for Monday’s 06:30 departure: set out field clothes, charge the work phone, check the weather and river outlook, and make sure lunch and drinking water are ready. Avoid committing to strenuous plans so there is capacity to respond if wet weather produces an emergency deployment. This is the first planned week, so there is no earlier calendar item requiring follow-up; the purpose of the block is to establish the normal Sunday rhythm of dog walking, errands and recovery before another week maintaining gauges across the Brisbane River catchment.
event_00007.location: New Farm Park, 1042 Brunswick Street, New Farm QLD 4005
event_00007.title: Dog Walk and Weekly Reset

event_00008.description: Start Monday at the depot by reconciling every unverified activity carried over from Week 1 before finalising this week’s Brisbane River catchment route. Check field notes, telemetry downloads, vehicle logs and staff confirmations to determine what was actually completed. File the outstanding Ipswich route plan; enter the Jindalee boat-ramp and Brisbane River gauging-station inspection findings; record the Oxley Creek telemetry service results; confirm attendance and completion of the QFES Academy swift-water rescue training; process the Kholo telemetry download and flow-survey measurements; and finish the Friday gauge-run records, data review and maintenance reporting from Rocklea. Contact the relevant field or training leads where evidence is missing. Also verify whether the dog’s health check with Dr Nair took place and record any medication, test, vaccination or follow-up instructions in the personal task list. Any visit or task that was not performed must be explicitly marked incomplete and rescheduled rather than assumed finished. Convert all identified gauge defects, telemetry faults, data-quality concerns, access hazards, safety actions, vehicle issues and veterinary follow-ups into dated actions with an owner and priority. Once the backlog is reconciled, review rainfall and river conditions, check equipment availability, assign Monday’s inspection sequence and brief the field team on access and wet-weather risks.
event_00008.title: Week 1 Close-out and Route Planning

event_00009.description: Meet with Narelle Bishop after the Monday equipment check to close out the unverified records carried over from Week 1 before finalising this week’s Brisbane River catchment route. Review and file the Ipswich route plan; enter the Jindalee boat-ramp and Brisbane River gauging-station inspection findings; record the Oxley Creek telemetry service results; and confirm whether Wednesday’s swift-water rescue training at the QFES Academy was completed. Process the Kholo gauge telemetry download and flow-survey data, including validation of ratings, timestamps and field notes, then finish the outstanding Friday gauge-run records and Rocklea data review. Check each job for unresolved equipment defects, maintenance requirements, data-quality flags and safety actions, assigning owners and target dates where follow-up is required. Also note whether the dog’s health check with Dr Nair occurred and capture any veterinary follow-up that may affect availability. Any activity that cannot be verified as performed must be explicitly marked outstanding and rescheduled rather than assumed complete. Narelle will help reconcile depot logs, telemetry records and vehicle sheets, while the technician will update the maintenance system and prepare a concise exception list. The session should end with a filed Week 1 close-out pack, a confirmed list of carryover actions, and an adjusted Monday inspection route that accounts for urgent defects without duplicating work.
event_00009.location: Seqwater Ipswich Office, 6 Level Street, Ipswich QLD
event_00009.title: Week 1 Field Records Close-out

event_00010.description: Tuesday field visit to verify and close out the unconfirmed Oxley Creek telemetry service from last week. Inspect the logger, pressure sensor, antenna, solar supply, battery terminals and enclosure seals; download diagnostics; compare recent stage readings with the staff gauge; and test transmission to the authority’s monitoring system. Photograph the site and record channel, vegetation, debris and access conditions, including any wet-weather or safety issues that require follow-up. Before departure, confirm whether last week’s service was actually completed. If it was, enter the service results and supporting evidence in the maintenance record; if it was not, perform the outstanding work today or create a dated rescheduling action for any task that cannot be safely completed. Review the downloaded trace for gaps, drift or implausible values and flag any data-quality concern for correction during Friday’s data review. Carry forward unresolved defects, replacement parts, maintenance actions and safety controls rather than marking the job closed without evidence. This visit also provides field confirmation needed to clear one item from Week 1’s outstanding close-out list.
event_00010.location: Oxley Creek gauging station, Blunder Road, Oxley QLD
event_00010.title: Oxley Creek Telemetry Recheck

event_00011.description: Wednesday 18:30–21:00 volunteer swift-water rescue session. Begin by confirming whether last week’s QFES Academy training was completed, as no attendance or completion update was recorded. Reconcile the attendance sheet, instructor notes, competencies covered and any equipment, safety or remedial actions from that session; if it was missed or only partly completed, assign a make-up activity rather than treating it as closed. The practical program will then cover downstream safety, throw-bag accuracy, tethered rescuer communication, casualty contact and extraction, with scenarios adjusted to current river conditions and recent Brisbane River catchment observations. Inspect helmets, personal flotation devices, ropes, carabiners and communications equipment before entering the training area, and quarantine any defective gear. Record participant competency observations, debrief findings and actions needed before Saturday’s practical rescue session. Coordinate the close-out with Tahlia Nguyen and ensure all records clearly distinguish verified completion from work still outstanding.
event_00011.location: Queensland Fire and Emergency Services Academy, 15 Howard Smith Drive, Port of Brisbane QLD 4178
event_00011.title: Swift-Water Rescue Training Close-Out

event_00012.description: Thursday field day to inspect and service the Moggill Creek telemetry installation with Leanne Mercer (leanne.mercer@example.com). Leave home at 06:30, collect the assigned vehicle and calibrated test equipment, then complete the site risk assessment before approaching the channel. Inspect the enclosure, antenna, solar panel, battery, pressure transducer, staff gauge and mounting hardware; clear minor vegetation only where permitted. Compare the logged stage against the staff-gauge reading, run a telemetry test and take a check flow measurement if access and water conditions are safe. Photograph site conditions and record any erosion, debris, vandalism, access problems or maintenance needs. Before leaving the field, review the previous week’s still-unverified Kholo telemetry service and flow-survey records with Leanne, confirm whether the source files and field notes are complete, and flag any unexplained data-quality issue for correction rather than treating that work as closed. Upload today’s readings, photographs and service notes on return to the Rocklea depot, quarantine suspect values, and raise work orders for defects that cannot be resolved during the visit. Wet weather or unsafe flow conditions will convert the channel work to a visual inspection and telemetry diagnostic, with the measurement rescheduled. Also note any safety or equipment issue that could affect Saturday’s practical swift-water rescue session.
event_00012.location: Moggill Creek gauging station, Brookfield Road, Kenmore Hills QLD
event_00012.title: Moggill Creek Telemetry Service

event_00013.description: Complete Friday’s short gauge-inspection run before returning to the Rocklea depot for data review, maintenance reporting and vehicle restocking. The main purpose is to close every outstanding record carried over from Week 1: verify whether the Ipswich route plan was filed; enter the Jindalee boat-ramp and Brisbane River gauging-station inspection findings; record the Oxley Creek telemetry service results; confirm completion of Wednesday’s QFES Academy rescue training; process and quality-check the Kholo telemetry and flow-survey data; and finish the unverified Friday gauge-run and data-review documentation. Check field notes, logger downloads, photographs, calibration sheets and vehicle records against the asset register. Flag gaps, anomalous readings, unresolved defects, maintenance needs, data-quality concerns and safety actions, assigning owners and due dates rather than marking incomplete work as finished. If any Week 1 visit or task was not actually performed, arrange a replacement field slot and note the reason. Send Priya Nair a concise close-out summary highlighting operational issues that may affect next week’s catchment route. Restock batteries, desiccant, telemetry spares, PPE, sampling supplies and traffic-control equipment; inspect and clean the field vehicle; then confirm it is ready for Monday. Also add a private administrative reminder to verify the outcome of the dog’s unconfirmed appointment with Dr Nair and record any veterinary follow-up or rescheduling required.
event_00013.location: Regional Water Authority Rocklea Depot, 1505 Ipswich Road, Rocklea QLD
event_00013.title: Gauge Run and Week 1 Close-out

event_00014.description: Lead the volunteer unit’s Saturday practical rescue session from 08:00 to 13:00. Begin with a weather, river-condition and site-risk briefing, followed by PPE and throw-bag checks, shore-based reach-and-throw drills, tethered swimmer techniques, casualty handling and team communication exercises. Run scenarios only within the academy’s approved training area and operating limits, with a designated downstream safety team and first-aid equipment ready. This session must also close the outstanding record from last week’s QFES Academy training: confirm whether that activity was completed, reconcile the attendance and competency sheets, and document any equipment defects, safety actions or skills requiring remediation. If last week’s session did not occur, identify the missed modules and add them to today’s program where safe and practical; otherwise arrange a later make-up session. Finish with a team debrief, equipment rinse and inspection, incident or near-miss reporting, and submission of the updated training log before departure.
event_00014.location: Queensland Fire and Emergency Services Academy, 15 Howard Smith Drive, Port of Brisbane QLD 4007
event_00014.title: Swift-Water Rescue Practical

event_00015.description: Take the dog for an easy Sunday walk through New Farm Park, keeping the pace gentle while checking mobility, appetite, breathing, energy and any symptoms that may need veterinary attention. Use the quiet time afterward to close out the unverified health check with Dr Priya Nair from last week: confirm whether the appointment actually occurred, locate any invoice or consultation notes, and record advice, medication changes, test results and follow-up dates. If the visit did not take place, contact Dr Nair at priya.nair@example.com to arrange the next available appointment rather than treating it as completed. Send a concise update if symptoms have changed and note anything that should be monitored during the coming workweek. Finish the weekly reset by preparing the dog’s food and medication, checking the forecast and river warnings, charging the work phone, and laying out Monday’s field gear. Keep the afternoon otherwise restful, but remain reachable in case catchment flooding triggers a volunteer swift-water rescue deployment.
event_00015.location: New Farm Park, 1042 Brunswick Street, New Farm QLD 4005
event_00015.title: Dog walk and veterinary follow-up

event_00016.description: Begin Monday at the Rocklea depot with the routine vehicle, telemetry-kit, flow-meter, battery, PPE and communications checks before confirming the week’s Brisbane River catchment inspection route. Use the planning block to continue last week’s work rather than opening new records: verify and file the outstanding Oxley Creek telemetry recheck, Moggill Creek service and gauge-run results, and resolve any remaining Week 1 field-record or route-planning actions. Check that uploaded photographs, calibration notes, site-condition observations and maintenance requirements are attached to the correct assets; where results are still unavailable, assign a clear owner and follow-up date rather than recording them as complete. Review recent rainfall, river levels, access constraints and telemetry alarms to prioritise Monday’s gauge inspections and prepare for possible wet-weather callouts. Also confirm whether Saturday’s swift-water rescue practical was completed and whether its close-out sign-off has been lodged. Before making any further training travel arrangements, reconcile the conflicting QFES Academy postcodes of 4178 and 4007 against the unit’s official booking advice. Briefly review the veterinary follow-up notes from last week and record any medication, monitoring or appointment action that may affect personal availability. Finish by updating the route sheet, loading required spares and issuing the day’s field plan.
event_00016.location: Regional Water Authority Rocklea Depot, Rocklea QLD 4106
event_00016.title: Depot Checks and Carryover Review

event_00017.description: Conduct the first field inspection of Monday’s Brisbane River catchment run, following the morning equipment checks and route planning at the Rocklea depot. Revisit the Oxley Creek telemetry installation to confirm and formally close out the recheck carried over from Week 2, whose findings and completion status were not recorded in the prior plan. Inspect the water-level sensor, antenna, solar supply, battery voltage, enclosure seals and mounting hardware; compare the logger reading with the staff gauge and take a manual reference measurement if conditions permit. Initiate a test transmission and verify that current data, timestamps and alarm status are reaching the authority’s telemetry platform without gaps or unexplained drift. Photograph the installation and surrounding channel, noting debris, bank erosion, access hazards, vegetation growth and any evidence of recent inundation. Review the field notes against the unresolved Week 1 records and Monday route-planning actions so that duplicated or missing work can be identified. Before departing, record asset condition, calibration checks, test results, consumables used and any maintenance required. Upload or queue the signed inspection record and Week 2 recheck evidence for filing on return to the depot. If telemetry performance remains uncertain, log a corrective work order, advise the operations contact and retain enough time in the route for a later diagnostic visit rather than marking the carried-over task complete without supporting results.
event_00017.location: Oxley Creek gauging station, Sherwood Road, Rocklea QLD 4106
event_00017.title: Oxley Creek Gauge Verification

event_00018.description: Tuesday field visit to verify and formally close out the Moggill Creek telemetry service recorded in Week 2. Meet Priya Nair (priya.nair@riverlandcivil.com.au) on site to review any Riverland Civil activity near the gauge, confirm safe access and identify works that could affect the sensor, conduit, antenna, control box or channel conditions. Inspect the installation for damage, debris, moisture ingress, loose connections and battery or solar-charging faults; compare the staff-gauge level with the pressure-transducer reading; run a telemetry test transmission; and check recent data for dropouts, drift or implausible changes. Photograph the gauge, channel, banks and access route, noting erosion, vegetation, obstructions and evidence of recent high flow. Record serial numbers, diagnostic readings, test results and any parts used in the field log. Before leaving, confirm whether the Week 2 service was successful or whether a return visit, replacement component or data correction is required. Upload photographs and field notes to the authority record, attach the verified result to the outstanding Week 2 service entry, and flag any civil-works risks or access restrictions for Friday’s maintenance report and future route planning. This visit also helps clear the prior week’s unverified gauge-run documentation rather than starting a new, unrelated inspection cycle.
event_00018.location: Moggill Creek gauge site, Brookfield Road, Kenmore Hills QLD 4069
event_00018.title: Moggill Creek Telemetry Verification

event_00019.description: Attend the regular Wednesday evening swift-water rescue unit session from 18:30 to 21:00 with Priya Nair and Morgan Ellis. Begin with a safety briefing and equipment check, then run practical drills covering throw-bag deployment, tethered rescues, casualty handling and team communications in fast-moving water. Use the session to verify completion of last week’s practical training and obtain the outstanding close-out sign-off, including confirmation of any competencies or remedial actions still to be recorded. Before travel, confirm with the unit coordinator that the correct QFES Academy destination is 15 Howard Smith Drive, Port of Brisbane QLD 4007, and update the shared booking and navigation notes to resolve last week’s conflicting 4178 and 4007 postcodes. File the signed attendance and competency records after training so the prior-week close-out is no longer unverified.
event_00019.location: QFES Academy, 15 Howard Smith Drive, Port of Brisbane QLD 4007
event_00019.title: Swift-water training and sign-off

event_00020.description: Thursday field visit to verify the Moggill Creek telemetry unit after last week’s servicing, for which no findings or completion record were provided. Inspect the enclosure, antenna, battery and solar supply; compare the logger’s stage reading with the staff gauge; run a manual transmission test; and photograph the site condition, access track and reference marks. Check recent data for gaps, drift or implausible values and take a spot flow measurement if conditions permit. Before leaving, contact the Rocklea depot if replacement components or a follow-up calibration are required. Upload the inspection sheet, photographs, transmission result and any corrective work to the regional water authority’s asset system so the outstanding Moggill Creek service result can be formally confirmed and filed. Also review the open Week 1 field-record and route-planning actions linked to this catchment, closing those supported by today’s evidence and clearly assigning any remaining tasks. This verification is intended to prevent last week’s unverified service outcome from carrying into another reporting cycle.
event_00020.location: Moggill Creek gauging station, Brookfield Road, Brookfield QLD 4069
event_00020.title: Moggill Creek Telemetry Verification

event_00021.description: Friday depot close-out following the morning inspection run. Meet with Priya Nair to review, confirm and file the outstanding Oxley Creek telemetry recheck, Moggill Creek service and Brisbane River catchment gauge-run results carried over from last week. Check field sheets, photographs, flow readings, telemetry diagnostics and maintenance notes against the asset register; flag missing evidence or anomalies for a return visit rather than treating unverified work as complete. Resolve any remaining Week 1 record-closure or route-planning actions and update next week’s field priorities accordingly. After the status review, prioritise today’s inspection route according to fault severity, access conditions and current river levels, with Jindalee included if testing or further repair is required.

event_00400.title: Depot checks and Week 50 closeout review

event_00401.description: Follow-up field visit to determine the final status of the physical gauge defect and telemetry fault carried forward from Week 50. Review the previous work orders and site notes before inspecting the staff gauge, sensor mount, enclosure, power supply, antenna, data logger and communications link. Verify readings against a manual water-level check, run a telemetry test to the regional water authority system and photograph current site conditions. If either defect remains unresolved, complete repairs within available parts and safety limits or document the exact fault, required materials and priority for a further visit. Confirm that any Week 50 repairs were entered correctly rather than duplicating the work. Reconcile inspection forms, telemetry test results, photographs and maintenance records so both defects receive a clear closed or outstanding outcome. Also check whether the Jindalee route generated any unfinished route-plan actions that need to be added to this week’s field schedule. Before leaving, update the asset record and advise Priya Nair of any issue that could affect data reliability or require another crew. This visit is specifically intended to close the previous week’s uncertain Jindalee status and establish an auditable result for each defect.

event_00401.title: Jindalee Gauge Defect Closeout

event_00402.description: Tuesday field visit with Leanne Mercer to verify the status of both Jindalee gauge issues carried forward from Week 50: the physical defect and the telemetry defect. Begin by reviewing the prior work orders, technician notes and any parts recorded as fitted, since last week’s plan did not confirm that either repair was completed. Inspect the gauge housing, mounting hardware, sensor assembly, cabling and site access for remaining damage or safety concerns. Test the telemetry unit, antenna, power supply and data logger, then compare live level readings with a manual reference measurement and confirm that transmissions are reaching the authority’s monitoring system without gaps or implausible values. Photograph the equipment and current riverbank conditions, record serial numbers and test results, and check whether any route-plan action from the Rocklea depot remains attached to this site. If both defects have been resolved, update the asset register and close the separate physical and telemetry work orders with clear final outcomes. If either fault persists, make safe repairs within available parts and time, or raise a follow-up work order specifying required components, access constraints, responsibility and a firm return date. Contact Leanne at leanne.mercer@example.com for record reconciliation and telemetry confirmation. This visit must establish an explicit status for every Week 50 Jindalee action so unresolved work is carried forward accurately rather than duplicated.

messages.content: Has anyone been into our storage locker at the marina since Sunday? The padlock was turned around when I checked after my river-gauge run.
Not me. I left the boat cover and two blue dry bags on the lower shelf last Thursday.
I opened it Saturday morning to collect the rescue throw ropes for training. I’m sure I locked it again.
Were the ropes returned? I need six for next weekend’s swift-water session, but I counted only five today.
Five are back in the locker. Jules still had one in her ute when we packed up at the Brisbane River site.
Did you move the red fuel container? It was beside the folding trolley, and now it’s near the door.
Yes, so I could reach the rope crate. I also noticed damp under the back shelf.
That might explain the mildew smell. I’ll bring a moisture meter after tomorrow’s gauge maintenance shift.
The marina office emailed about locker inspections too. They want proof that fuel is stored in an approved container.
Can you forward that email? I haven’t seen the inspection date or their storage rules.
I’ll look for it tonight. It may have gone to the old household address.
Should we meet at the locker Wednesday evening and clear the wet gear before the inspection?
I can probably get there after 6, depending on river levels and whether I’m called back to the Enoggera gauge.
Is 6:30 okay for everyone, and who has the spare locker key now?
Did you get into the marina locker?
Yes, but the lower latch is sticking.
Are the rescue ropes still dry?
Mostly. One red throw bag felt damp.
Please leave it open to air tonight.
Done. I moved your gauge toolkit up too.
Thanks. The river authority needs it Monday.
I also found two unlabelled paddles.
They belong to the weekend rescue course.
Should I mark them with your name?
Use “Swift-water training” instead.
Okay. We’re nearly out of shelf space.
I can bring another crate Saturday.
What time will you be at the marina?
Did you finish the costume inventory audit?
Nearly. I counted 18 rescue uniforms.
The sheet lists 20. Any damaged ones?
Two are in the repair tub.
Are they tagged with sizes?
One medium; the other tag is missing.
I’ll check after my river gauge round.
I also found six helmets, not seven.
Is the yellow helmet with the trainers?
Possibly. I didn’t check their gear cage.
What about the pirate coats?
All four counted, but one needs buttons.
Can you send me the updated audit sheet?
Yes, once I find who has the missing helmet.
Morning Natalie, I’ve uploaded the quarterly hydrology dataset for the Brisbane River gauges, covering January through March.
Thanks. Does this version include the corrected stage readings from the Indooroopilly gauge after the telemetry fault?
Yes, I replaced the affected 12–14 February values with the verified logger download and marked them QC2.
Great. I’m seeing three blank discharge values for Moggill on 3 March. Are those intentional?
They are. The rating curve was exceeded during the storm peak, so I didn’t want to publish estimated flows without approval.
Could you add a note explaining that? Otherwise the blanks may look like missing telemetry.
Will do. I’ll also include the field inspection record from when I checked the gauge after the swift-water training weekend.
Please keep the rescue-training details out of the public metadata, but the inspection date and sensor condition are useful.
Understood. The inspection was 5 March; the pressure transducer was sound, but debris had shifted the staff-gauge reference slightly.
Does that shift affect the reported levels for the rest of March?
Only by 6 millimetres. I applied the surveyed correction from 6 March onward and documented it in the processing log.
Perfect. I still need the rainfall cross-check for the Enoggera Creek station before I can sign off the quarter.
I asked Liam for the Bureau export yesterday, but he hasn’t sent the CSV yet.
Can you confirm whether we’ll have it before Thursday’s publication cutoff?
The materials order arrived at the depot, but it shipped short: only 8 of the 12 staff-gauge plates and none of the stainless mounting brackets were included.
I checked the packing slip. It lists all 12 plates and 24 brackets as dispatched, so the quantities definitely do not match what arrived.
Were both cartons delivered? The supplier’s notice shows two boxes under the same consignment number.
Only one carton was on the pallet when I collected it. I asked stores to check the receiving bay for a second box.
We need four plates and eight brackets for the Bremer River gauge repair on Thursday. Can the existing brackets be reused?
Two might be salvageable, but the others are badly corroded. I would rather not rely on them with more rain forecast.
I’ll contact the supplier and ask whether the second carton was split in transit. Please send me photos of the carton label and contents.
Sending the contents photo now. The carton label is torn across the lower barcode, but the consignment number is still readable.
Could we borrow brackets from the Oxley depot if the missing carton does not turn up today?
Possibly. Their stock sheet showed ten last week, though I need Ben to confirm they have not been allocated.
I can collect from Oxley tomorrow morning before heading to the river, provided someone confirms by 7:30.
I’ve emailed Ben and marked it urgent. I also noticed the supplier invoice was for the full order, not the reduced shipment.
The supplier is tracing the second carton and will call back this afternoon. They also asked for a signed delivery docket.
Stores have not sent me the signed docket yet. Do either of you know who accepted the delivery?
Have you seen the arborist survey for the east avenue? Three figs are marked for removal.
Yes, trees 12, 14 and 15. The report says root damage and storm risk.
Tree 14 is beside the river-gauge access gate. Removal could block our maintenance vehicle.
I’ll flag that. Did the water authority give you any access dates?
We’re due to service the gauge next Thursday morning, but the crew time isn’t confirmed.
The arborist proposed starting Thursday at 7 am, so that may clash.
Could they begin at the northern end and leave tree 14 until later?
Possibly. They also want the rescue training trailer moved from beneath tree 12.
I can move it after Saturday’s swift-water session at Wivenhoe.
Good. The survey’s appendix mentions nesting habitat, but my copy is missing page 18.
Mine too. We shouldn’t approve removal until we see the habitat recommendation.
Agreed. I’ll ask the arborist for the complete PDF and a revised work sequence.
Please also check whether the east avenue will remain open to pedestrians.
Will do. What time should I tell them the gauge crew expects access on Thursday?
The materials order arrived at the depot, but it’s short by six stainless mounting brackets and two cable glands.
That matches the packing slip, though the supplier invoice shows the full quantity.
I need four brackets for the Logan River gauge service on Thursday. Did they mention a second carton?
No second tracking number. The courier marked the consignment complete at Eagle Farm this morning.
Could the missing pieces be tucked inside the conduit bundle? I only checked the main crate.
I opened the bundle with Sam. It had the conduit, anchors and junction boxes, nothing loose inside.
Right. I’ll hold two spare brackets from the Pine River kit, but that still leaves us short.
I’ve emailed the supplier photos of the crate label and counted contents. They’re checking dispatch records.
Thanks. Please ask whether they can send the cable glands by express; the old seals are badly cracked.
Will do. Do you need IP68 M20 glands, or were these the M25 ones for the telemetry enclosure?
M20 for Logan. The M25 pair can wait until next week if they split the replacement shipment.
Understood. The invoice also lists ten chemical anchors, but I counted only eight. Did you take any?
No, I haven’t removed anything. Add the two anchors to the shortage claim and send me the revised count.
I’ll update it, but I’m still waiting for the supplier to confirm whether a second carton left their warehouse.
Are we still looking at the West End apartment this Saturday?
Yes, the agent offered 10:30 am, but I haven’t confirmed it yet.
That should work. I finish checking the river gauges by nine.
Great. Can you meet me outside the building on Vulture Street?
Sure. Is there visitor parking, or should I take the bus?
The listing mentions one car space, but nothing about visitor parking.
I’ll bus over, then. Did the agent send a floor plan?
Only the photos and rental application. I’ve asked for the floor plan.
Thanks. I want to check whether the spare room fits my rescue-training gear.
I also want to ask how noisy the balcony gets on weekends.
Good point. We should check the water pressure and signs of flood damage too.
Definitely, especially that low storage area shown in the photos.
Can you forward me the application before Saturday?
I will once the agent replies. Should I confirm 10:30 am?
Have you checked the seed-bank accession list I shared?
Yes. Three Brisbane River entries are missing collection dates.
Are those BR-117, BR-121 and BR-124?
Exactly. BR-121 also lists Oxley Creek instead of Enoggera Creek.
Good catch. I copied that location from the old field sheet.
I can verify the gauge coordinates when I’m at Enoggera tomorrow.
Thanks. The list also marks BR-124 as Melaleuca quinquenervia.
That may be wrong; my sample bag notes say Casuarina cunninghamiana.
Do you still have a photo of the label?
Possibly on the rescue-training tablet. I’ll check after Saturday’s session.
Could you send it before I submit the accession list Monday?
I should manage Sunday evening, but I can’t promise a time.
I’ll leave BR-124 flagged and update BR-121’s location meanwhile.
Great. Who has the missing collection-date sheet for those three?
Starting review of the quarterly hydrology dataset.
North Pine gauge has a gap on 18 June.
Field log says the pressure sensor was fouled.
I’ll flag those readings as provisional.
Brisbane River levels otherwise match telemetry.
Need to add the manual Enoggera Creek reading.
Rainfall totals are imported through 30 June.
Rating curve version needs checking for Oxley Creek.
I think the May adjustment was v4.2.
Ask Priya before publishing the derived discharge values.
Metadata still needs the sensor swap date.
Draft QA summary saved in the quarterly folder.
I can submit after weekend rescue training.
Did Liam upload the signed calibration sheet?
Did the organ tuner confirm Tuesday at St Luke’s?
Not yet. He offered Tuesday morning or Thursday after 2.
Tuesday is difficult; I’m checking the river gauges upstream.
Would Thursday at 3 suit you?
Probably, unless the rain pushes me onto flood-response duty.
I’ll pencil in Thursday at 3 with the church office.
Thanks. Did they mention how long the tuning will take?
About three hours, longer if the sticking swell pedal needs repair.
I can meet him and explain which notes have been drifting.
Great. I noted the sharp middle D and the soft bass stop.
Also ask him to check the cipher in the second manual.
Will do. He needs the organ’s last service report too.
I think Helen has it, but I haven’t seen the file.
Shall I confirm Thursday at 3 now, or wait until your flood roster is settled?
The ginger beer batch overshot overnight—34°C instead of the 24–27°C target.
How long was it that hot? The yeast may have produced some harsh flavours.
Logger shows it climbed after 1 am and stayed above 30°C for nearly four hours.
Is the airlock still active, and does it smell solvent-like or just extra yeasty?
Still bubbling. It smells strongly of banana, but I’m not getting nail-polish remover.
That’s encouraging. Move it somewhere cooler, but don’t crash the temperature suddenly.
I’ve put it in the laundry sink with cool water. It’s down to 28.5°C now.

contact_0128.description: The anchor persona's long-term partner, sharing their rented townhouse in Brisbane's 4069 area and caring for their elderly kelpie together. Morgan handles the dog's weekday medication, while they split rent, groceries and the Sunday river-walk routine.

They meet each Monday at the Brisbane operations depot to review gauge faults, flood-response rosters and upcoming field visits, and share responsibility for keeping the Brisbane River monitoring network operational.

contact_user.description: A hydrology technician who maintains river gauges for a regional water authority and volunteers as a swift-water rescue trainer at weekends. Household: Lives with a partner and their elderly kelpie in a rented townhouse. Routine: Works Monday to Friday for the regional water authority, usually leaving home at 06:30. Mondays begin at the depot with equipment checks and route planning, followed by gauge inspections along the Brisbane River catchment. Tuesday through Thursday are mostly field days servicing telemetry units, taking flow measurements and documenting site conditions; wet-weather callouts can extend into the evening. Fridays combine a short inspection run with data review, maintenance reports and vehicle restocking. Trains with the volunteer swift-water rescue unit on Wednesday evenings from 18:30 to 21:00 and leads practical rescue sessions most Saturdays from 08:00 to 13:00. Sundays are normally reserved for errands, dog walks and rest, unless flooding triggers an emergency deployment.

emails.content:
Hi Mara,

I’ve gone through the landlord’s 28 April letter, the attached Form 4 and our tenancy agreement again. The notice says the rent for 16 Millbank Terrace will rise from £1,180 to £1,345 per month from 1 July—an increase of £165, or just under 14%. That is the same figure Hawthorn Lettings quoted in their email of 2 May, so at least the paperwork and their message now match. The first version they slipped under the door on 26 April said £1,375, which is why I think we should keep all three documents.

I spoke to Priya at the tenants’ advice line this morning. She said the key issue is not simply whether the increase is steep, but whether the Form 4 was served correctly and whether £1,345 reflects the local market. Our fixed term ended on 31 January and the tenancy became monthly periodic on 1 February, so the landlord can propose an increase under section 13. However, Priya noticed that the form is dated 28 April but states it was served on 30 April. She thinks that probably still gives the required month’s notice for a 1 July start, although she wants to see the envelope and the complete form before confirming.

Could you photograph the envelope when you get home? I put it on the hall table beside the blue folder. Please include the postmark and both sides. I’ve already scanned “Rent Increase Notice – 28 April,” “Form 4 – Proposed New Rent” and the signed tenancy dated 18 January last year. I’ll forward those to Priya this afternoon along with Hawthorn’s 2 May email.

On comparable rents, I found three two-bedroom places within half a mile advertised at £1,250, £1,275 and £1,295. None has the damp patch in the back bedroom or the recurring boiler-pressure fault we reported on 12 February and again on 19 March. I’ve saved the listings as PDFs before they disappear. That should help if we negotiate or refer the proposed rent to the tribunal.

My preference is still to write to Elaine Porter before filing anything. We could offer £1,260 from 1 July, conditional on the bedroom damp being treated and the boiler repair being completed by 15 June. If they refuse, Priya says we must submit the tribunal application before the new rent is due; we should not simply pay the old amount without taking formal action. She also stressed that we should continue paying the current £1,180 in full and on time meanwhile.

I’ve drafted a response headed “Without Prejudice – Proposed Rent Increase at 16 Millbank Terrace,” but I won’t send it until you’ve checked it. I left the draft in the shared folder. Can you read it after your gauge round tomorrow? If you’re on the late callout again, just add comments and I’ll send the final version by noon on Friday, 10 May.

I know this is the last thing you need alongside the river work and Saturday’s rescue training, but we do have grounds to push back calmly. Please don’t ring Elaine from the depot; keeping everything in writing is safer.

Love,
Morgan

Hi Mara,

Thanks for sending the clearer scan of the landlord’s 14 September notice and the tenancy agreement you signed on 1 April 2022. I have compared them with the rent schedule attached to your message from Monday.

As we discussed, the notice says the monthly rent for 18 Mill Lane will rise from £925 to £1,075 with effect from 1 November. That is an increase of £150 a month, or just over 16%. However, clause 7.2 of the tenancy agreement says the rent may be reviewed once in any twelve-month period and that you must receive at least two full calendar months’ written notice. The previous increase, from £875 to £925, took effect on 1 February this year, so the proposed 1 November date appears inconsistent with both parts of that clause.

There is also a discrepancy between the figures in the documents. The covering letter headed “Annual Rent Review 2024” gives the new rent as £1,075, while the attached standing-order slip says £1,050 from 1 November. I would not amend your standing order until the landlord confirms in writing which amount is actually being proposed and provides a valid effective date. Continue paying the current £925 on the first of each month in the meantime, and keep the funds for any disputed difference aside.

I have drafted a response below for you to send to Mr Pritchard or Greenbank Lettings:

“Dear Mr Pritchard,

I acknowledge receipt of your rent increase notice dated 14 September 2024. The notice proposes increasing the rent for 18 Mill Lane from £925 to £1,075 per calendar month from 1 November 2024. The accompanying standing-order instruction instead states £1,050.

Please clarify the intended amount. I also draw your attention to clause 7.2 of the tenancy agreement dated 1 April 2022, which provides for no more than one review in a twelve-month period and requires at least two full calendar months’ written notice. As the last increase took effect on 1 February 2024, I do not agree that the proposed increase can take effect on 1 November 2024.

Until this is resolved and a compliant notice is served, I will continue paying the contractual rent of £925 per calendar month. This should not be taken as agreement to the proposed increase.

Yours sincerely,
Mara Ellis”

If the landlord intended to use the statutory procedure rather than the contractual review clause, ask Greenbank to send the prescribed Form 4; the two-page letter you received is not that form. A valid statutory notice would ordinarily need to allow at least one month and could not take effect before the end of the fixed or contractual restriction that applies. I would avoid stating an alternative acceptable figure for now, as that could muddy your position.

Please also save the original envelope showing the 18 September postmark, along with the PDF named “Rent Review Notice - Mill Lane.pdf.” If they telephone, make a brief note of the date, time and what was said, then ask them to confirm it by email. Do not feel pressured to agree during a call.

Send me their reply when it arrives. If they insist that £1,075 is due on 1 November or threaten arrears action, I can help you put the papers in order for the council’s tenancy-relations officer.

Best,
Helen

Hi,

I have now reconciled the logger export with the handwritten readings for Batch F-0614, the 120 L elderflower-and-ginger ferment that overshot temperature on 16 June. The corrected timeline is in “F-0614_Temperature_Excursion_v7.pdf,” which replaces v6 from Tuesday.

The vessel was pitched at 18.4°C at 19:20 on 14 June. It remained between 18.1°C and 19.6°C until 22:40 on 15 June, then rose steadily after the cooling-loop valve stuck. The probe recorded 24.0°C at 01:50 on 16 June, 27.8°C at 04:10, and a maximum of 29.3°C at 05:35. Your 05:42 manual reading of 29.1°C confirms that the logger was not simply drifting. Once you freed the valve and circulated the two 10 L ice-water containers, the batch fell below 24°C at 08:25 and reached 20.2°C by 13:10. Total time above our 24°C limit was 6 hours 35 minutes, including 2 hours 20 minutes above 27°C.

I also corrected the earlier note about the sugar addition. We added 8.6 kg, not 9.0 kg, giving an original gravity of 1.046. Yesterday’s final gravity was 1.008 in both samples after temperature correction, so attenuation is about 83%. The retained bottle opened normally: no gush, rope, film, or solvent aroma. There is a little more pear/banana ester than in Batch F-0524, but the panel of four did not identify harsh fusel alcohol. pH moved from 4.18 at pitching to 3.36 on 21 June, which is consistent with the previous batches.

Micro results from Northbank came back this morning. The report “NB-24-1887_F0614.pdf” shows no detectable coliforms or enteric organisms, and the yeast morphology is consistent with the production culture. The low-level Lactobacillus signal was also present in the control blank, so the lab has marked it as probable handling contamination rather than evidence of spoilage. I have attached their amended certificate, dated 27 June, along with “F-0614_Sensory_Scores.xlsx.”

On that basis, I agree with your proposal not to dump the full 112 L remaining after sampling. Please keep it quarantined and clearly tagged until we complete the 72-hour package check. I filled twelve 330 mL test bottles at 15:00 today: six will stay at 20°C and six at 30°C. I’ll check pressure, pH, aroma, and visible growth at 24, 48, and 72 hours. If there is no abnormal pressure rise and pH remains within 0.10 of today’s value, we can release it for the volunteer event, but not before Monday, 1 July.

For the root cause, I have changed the wording from “operator failed to monitor” to “cooling valve mechanical seizure compounded by alarm-routing failure.” The alarm did trigger at 24°C, but it went only to the retired tablet in the store room. That matches the notification log you sent. Please confirm that the replacement valve installed on 22 June is the stainless V2 unit, serial CV-4471, and that the high-temperature alert now reaches both your phone and mine. Once confirmed, I’ll close actions 3 and 4 in “CAPA_F-0614_revC.docx.”

Thanks again for getting there at 05:40 after your gauge round. Without the manual check and rapid cooling, we would almost certainly have lost the batch.

Best,
Mara

I’ve finished checking the 18 May saison batch against the Tilt export and your notes from the shed controller. You were right about the timing: the 62 L batch rose from 23.8°C at 21:10 on 19 May to a peak of 31.6°C at 03:42 on 20 May. It stayed above 30°C for approximately 2 hours 25 minutes, rather than the four hours I estimated in my last message. The probe started reporting normally again after you reseated it at 06:15, so I have not discarded the later readings.

I’ve attached the corrected files as “Saison_18May_Temperature_Log_v3.csv” and “Batch_24-05_Deviation_Report_v2.pdf”. The report now records the actual pitching amount (two 11.5 g packets of BE-134), the starting gravity of 1.052, and the 58 L transferred after trub loss. I also amended the cooling-water entry from 20 L to 27 L, based on the marks in your brew-day notebook.

The good news is that yesterday’s samples from bottles 3 and 11 were consistent. Both finished at 1.006, with pH readings of 4.18 and 4.21. I picked up a little extra pear/banana aroma, but no solvent character, sourness or obvious contamination. Carbonation in bottle 11 was lively, although it had been at room temperature for longer. I agree with your suggestion that we keep the batch quarantined until the next check rather than tipping it solely because of the temperature excursion.

Could you bring one unopened 500 ml bottle from the warmest crate and one from the lower shelf when you come over on Saturday, 8 June? I’ll chill both for 24 hours, then we can compare them at the 16:30 tasting. I’ve added a line for each sample to “Saison_18May_Sensory_Sheet.docx”. If either shows pressure, phenolic notes beyond the expected saison character, or a pH below 4.0, we’ll stop and dispose of the remaining 41 bottles.

On the controller fault, I tested the Inkbird with the spare probe in a water bath this morning. The relay opened correctly at 24.5°C three times, which makes your loose-probe theory more likely than a failed controller. For the next batch I suggest taping the probe firmly to the fermenter under insulation, setting the high alarm to 26°C, and using the separate blue logger as an independent check. I’ve put those steps into “Fermentation_Setup_Checklist_v4.pdf”.

Please don’t leave the bottles in the gauge van while you’re on the Friday route; even a mild afternoon could warm them enough to muddy the comparison. If Saturday changes because of rescue training, just text me and I’ll collect them from your porch in the insulated box.

Thanks again for catching the discrepancy in the log.

Hi Mara,

I’ve finished reviewing the logger export and your notes for the 17 May ginger saison batch. You were right that the temperature overshoot was shorter than the first graph suggested. The probe climbed above the 22.0°C set point at 01:42 on 19 May, peaked at 28.6°C at 03:18, and was back below 24.0°C by 06:51. The flat section in the screenshot you sent on Monday was a charting artefact, not another four hours at peak temperature.

I’ve attached the corrected “Batch_17May_TempLog_v3.csv” and updated the incident sheet as “Fermentation_Deviation_17May_revB.pdf”. I also added your observation that the cooling jacket outlet hose had kinked behind the crate. On the evidence we have, the controller relay operated normally; the restricted return flow is still the most likely cause. The 26 L batch started at an original gravity of 1.054, and yesterday’s reading of 1.011 is consistent with the expected attenuation rather than an uncontrolled secondary fermentation.

The samples tell much the same story. Bottle A, drawn before the temperature rise, was clean but still quite sweet. Bottle B, drawn at 18:30 on 19 May after cooling, had a stronger pear/banana note but no solvent character, sourness or visible pellicle. The pH moved from 4.62 at pitching to 4.08 on 20 May and 3.96 on 23 May. I don’t see a safety reason to dump it, although the warmer interval will probably make it fruitier than the April trial.

My suggestion is to leave it at 20°C until the gravity is unchanged for two consecutive days, then cold-crash as planned. Please don’t package on the strength of the single 1.011 reading. If Friday morning’s result is still 1.011 (or within one point), the original 5.5 g/L priming rate should remain suitable. That works out to 143 g for the full 26 L, but recalculate against the actual volume after transfer rather than adding the whole amount automatically.

I’ve also revised the checklist we discussed. The new version includes a hose-clearance check, a high-temperature alarm at 24.5°C, and a separate independent probe taped to the vessel under insulation. For the next run, I’d test the alarm with water before pitching rather than discovering another notification problem overnight. The missed alert was traced to the old email rule, so I’ve replaced your obsolete work address with mara.ellis@example.org in the controller account.

Could you confirm whether the backup probe was sitting against the stainless wall or hanging free in the chamber? Its maximum was only 25.1°C, and that placement detail will help us explain the 3.5°C difference in the close-out note.

I can collect Bottle C after my Hawthorn culvert inspection on Thursday, probably around 16:45. If you’re still out servicing the upstream gauges, leave it in the labelled box in the shed fridge and I’ll message before I come through. No need to interrupt your rescue-training preparation on Saturday.

Regards,
Priya Nair
Riverland Civil

Hi Mara,

I’ve compared your latest readings with the photos and the log sheet you sent. For the 14 February chickpea-miso batch, the key excursion still appears to be the period between 22:40 on 15 February and 04:20 on 16 February. The centre probe rose from 31.8°C to a recorded maximum of 41.6°C, while the shelf probe reached 38.9°C. That fits with your note that the 2.4 kg tray was still covered with the folded towel and pushed close to the heat mat overnight.

The good news is that nothing in the 16 February photos suggests obvious contamination. The growth was evenly white, the beans were knitting together, and I couldn’t see the green, black or pink patches we discussed. Your pH readings—5.9 before incubation, 5.1 after the overshoot and 4.7 when you mixed in the brine on 17 February—also moved in the expected direction. The smell you described as “sweet chestnut with a sharp pear note” is less concerning than ammonia, rotten meat or a strongly solvent-like odour would be.

That said, photographs and pH strips cannot establish that a batch is safe. As agreed, please don’t taste it or give any to the dogs. Keep the three 750 ml jars labelled “14FEB-CM-A/B/C” sealed in the utility-room fridge until the culture result is back. I dropped your 25 g sample from jar B at the lab yesterday morning; their receipt is attached as “WSV_LabReceipt_1847_21Feb.pdf”. They expect the mould identification and basic bacterial screen by Tuesday, 27 February.

I also reviewed “Koji_Temp_Log_v4.xlsx”. Your correction of the 03:10 entry from 46.1°C to 41.6°C makes sense given the probe photo and the adjacent readings. Please retain the original file as well as v4, just so we have an unaltered record. In the incident note, I’d phrase it as a five-hour-forty-minute excursion above 35°C, not as six hours above 40°C; only the 02:30 and 03:10 centre readings exceeded 40°C.

For the replacement batch, your proposed changes look sensible: divide the 2.4 kg into two shallow trays, leave at least 8 cm between them, remove the towel once the centre reaches 30°C, and set the controller alarm at 33°C. I’d also move the independent probe into the middle of the bean layer rather than taping it under the tray. Since you’ll be at the Mill Weir rescue-training day on Saturday, I would wait until Sunday evening to inoculate rather than leave the first active phase unattended. The river-gauge alarm is enough to have on your phone without adding a ferment alarm too.

One small correction to my previous message: the salt calculation for 3.6 kg finished mix should be 396 g at 11%, not 360 g. Your actual addition was 398 g, so no action is needed; please just amend the figure in “Chickpea_Miso_Batch_Record_14Feb.docx”.

I’ll message as soon as the lab report arrives. If any jar lid domes, leaks, or develops a markedly foul smell before then, don’t open it—bag the whole jar and let me know.

Best,

Priya

Priya Nair, BVetMed MRCVS
Westside Veterinary Practice

I’ve now reviewed the renewal pack against the Harbour Master’s checklist dated 14 August. We are nearly there, but two items still need attention before I lodge the application for your harbour pilot certification renewal, which expires on 30 September.

First, the medical certificate you sent on Monday is the general AMSA seafarer medical form. The Port Authority has confirmed that it also requires the signed “Pilot Medical Declaration – Form HP-12”, even where the AMSA certificate remains current. Dr Chen only needs to complete sections 4 and 6; your examination does not need to be repeated. I’ve attached the HP-12 version issued in July 2025, as the older March 2023 form in the original pack will no longer be accepted after 1 September.

Second, the sea-service statement currently records 18 supervised harbour movements between 3 October and 22 November last year. Your log extract shows another four movements aboard Southern Kestrel on 6 and 7 December, but Captain Rowe’s signature is missing from page 3. If he signs that page, the total will be 22 movements and will satisfy the renewal requirement. Otherwise, the Authority may ask for a separate statutory declaration.

The application fee remains $685, not the $720 quoted in my earlier email. Finance confirmed yesterday that the higher amount applies only to an initial issue. Riverland Civil can pay the fee with the lodgement and invoice you afterward under reference RLC-HP-4471, as we did for your 2022 renewal. Please let me know if you would prefer to pay the Authority directly instead.

I have retained the following documents on file:

• Harbour Pilot Renewal Application HP-R1, signed 12 August;
• colour scan of your passport, certified by Leon Briggs on 9 August;
• current First Aid and CPR certificates;
• Marine Radio Operator’s Certificate; and
• the CPD record showing 16 hours completed, including the 18 May bridge-resource-management session.

Your swift-water rescue training on 24 August can count toward professional development only if the provider issues a certificate identifying the risk assessment and emergency coordination components. It is not needed to reach the 12-hour minimum this cycle, so there is no need to delay lodgement for it.

If you can return the completed HP-12 and the signed Southern Kestrel log page by 4:00 pm on Tuesday, 27 August, I can submit the full pack on Wednesday morning. That leaves more than four weeks for processing before the 30 September expiry. The Authority advised that its current turnaround is 10–15 business days, although it will not guarantee approval until the originals have been sighted.

I’ll keep the original sea-service statement in the blue document wallet you left at our Docklands office. You can collect it after lodgement, or I can send it by registered post to the regional water authority office if that is easier while you are out servicing gauges.

Kind regards,

Priya Nair

I’ve finished the second-pass review of the April–June 2025 quarterly hydrology dataset and uploaded my marked copy as “Q2_2025_HydrologyDataset_review2.xlsx” in the shared Quarterly Returns folder. This is the version based on the export you sent on 14 July, with the 18 July corrections to the Mill Weir and East Bracken records incorporated.

Most of the dataset is now ready for submission, but I found four items that still need your confirmation before I lock the figures:

1. Mill Weir (MW-04): the stage record for 06:15–09:00 on 23 May is still flagged as observed rather than infilled. Your maintenance note says the pressure transducer was disconnected while you replaced the desiccant and vent tube. I’ve highlighted the 12 affected 15-minute values in orange. Should these be coded “M” and infilled from the downstream correlation, or did you take manual staff-gauge readings during that visit?

2. East Bracken (EB-02): the revised discharge total for June is 18.742 million m³, not 18.724 million m³. The difference appears to come from the updated rating table RT-EB02-2025-03 taking effect at 00:00 on 11 June. I have applied the new rating from that timestamp, which matches the approval note Priya circulated on 9 July.

3. Alder Footbridge (AF-07): there is a 42 mm stage jump at 02:30 on 4 April, followed by an immediate return at 02:45. It looks like debris interference rather than a genuine pulse, especially since North Alder showed no corresponding rise. I’ve proposed removing that single value and interpolating between the adjacent readings.

4. Rain gauge RG-12: the monthly total shown on the summary tab is 63.8 mm for May, while the daily sheet sums to 64.3 mm. The 0.5 mm difference is the manual catch recorded on 31 May. Please confirm whether that catch should remain included; I recall from our 2 July exchange that the gauge was being used for comparison only while the tipping-bucket calibration was outstanding.

For completeness, the quarter currently contains 26 stations, 224,640 stage observations, 8,736 rainfall observations and 17 manual discharge measurements. Data completeness is 98.7% before infilling and 99.4% after the approved short-gap fills. I also checked the three spot gaugings from 12 June against “Q2_2025_GaugingSheets_signed.pdf”; all three values agree with the field sheets.

Could you send me your decisions on the four points above by noon on Thursday, 24 July? If I have them by then, I can generate “Q2_2025_HydrologyDataset_FINAL.csv,” refresh the station completeness table and submit the package to Regional Data Services before Friday’s 16:00 deadline. No need to resend the whole workbook—an email response with the relevant codes and values will be enough.

Thanks again for tracking down the East Bracken logger offset. That correction removed the only remaining unexplained drift in the quarterly series.

Best,

Morgan Reilly
Data Quality Coordinator
Regional Water Authority

emails.content:
Hi,

I’ve finished checking the records for the fermentation batch started on 14 May and have updated the attached document, “Batch F-24-0514 Temperature Excursion Review v3.” The short version is that the vessel held at the 22.0°C set point until 01:35 on 16 May, then rose steadily and peaked at 31.7°C at 04:18. It remained above our 26.0°C upper limit for 2 hours 43 minutes, rather than the 90 minutes I estimated in my last message.

The most likely cause is still the combination of the active fermentation phase and the failed cooling-water solenoid. The controller was calling for cooling from 01:42 onward, but the valve-position trace stayed at 4–6%. When I tested solenoid SV-3 on 17 May, the coil was receiving 24 V but the plunger was sticking. I’ve added those readings, along with the controller export, to “F-24-0514 Sensor and Alarm Log.csv.” The independent probe was within 0.3°C of the vessel sensor, so this does not appear to have been a bad temperature reading.

For completeness, the batch contained 118 L at the start, made with 24.5 kg of substrate and inoculated with 2.4 L of starter. We lost approximately 3 L during sampling and transfer, leaving 115 L currently held in the cold room at 4.2°C. The 18 May sample showed pH 3.61, compared with 3.74 before the excursion. Aroma is sharper than normal but there is no visible contamination, film, or unexpected gas production. I’ve labelled all six retained 250 mL samples “HOLD — TEMP EXCURSION” and recorded their shelf positions in the review.

I agree with your suggestion not to discard anything until the laboratory results are back. The yeast and bacterial screens were delivered this morning under chain-of-custody form COC-1846; the lab expects preliminary results by Thursday, 23 May, and the full panel by 27 May. Please don’t use Batch F-24-0514 for the planned 25 May blending trial unless we both sign off after those results.

I’ve also revised the corrective-action section. Before the next run, I propose that we replace SV-3, test the high-temperature alarm at 25.5°C, and add a second alert if the cooling demand remains above 80% for more than ten minutes without a corresponding valve response. I can fit the replacement solenoid on Wednesday afternoon. The quoted part is £68.40, plus the new gasket at £6.75.

Could you review sections 4 and 6 of the excursion report, particularly the disposition criteria? If you’re comfortable with the wording, I’ll issue the final version after the lab report arrives. I’ve kept the original 16 May log and v2 of the review in the batch folder so the audit trail is intact.

Thanks for catching the discrepancy in the alarm duration. Your reconstruction from the five-minute logger data was right; I had initially used the dashboard summary, which omitted the first 37 minutes above 26.0°C.

Best,
Mara Ellis

Hi Mara,

I’ve now compared your gauge-logger export with my notes for the saison batch that overshot on 14 May. Your reconstruction was right: the fermenter did not sit at 31°C all night, as I first feared. According to “Batch-24-05-14_TempLog.csv,” the probe crossed our 22.5°C upper limit at 21:42, reached a maximum of 30.8°C at 23:17, and fell below 25°C again at 01:06 after we moved the vessel into the utility-room bath. Total time above 25°C was 2 hours 49 minutes.

The important correction is that I pitched at 18:35, not 19:10. I found the original entry on the paper brew sheet; the later time in “Saison_Batch_Record_v3.docx” was when I fitted the airlock. That means the temperature rise started about three hours after pitching, which makes active fermentation a more plausible contributor than the heater alone. Could you amend the timeline table before we circulate it to Ben?

I also tested the controller yesterday using your suggested jug-and-ice-bath check. At 0.4°C on the reference thermometer, the controller displayed 2.1°C; at 20.0°C it displayed 21.6°C. The separate blue probe was within 0.3°C at both points. More worryingly, the relay remained energised until the displayed temperature reached 24.7°C even though the set point was 21.5°C with a 0.5°C differential. I’ve labelled that controller “DO NOT USE” and removed it from the cupboard.

For completeness, the batch volume was 23 litres, not 25, and we added 11 g of Belle Saison yeast. Gravity has gone from 1.052 to 1.006. The sample this morning had a strong pear aroma but no solvent or burnt-plastic note, so I don’t think we need to discard it yet. I propose leaving it at 20°C until 21 May, then taking another gravity reading and a small tasting sample. I won’t bottle anything unless the reading is unchanged for three days.

I’ve attached my revised incident note, “Fermentation_Temp_Excursion_14May_v4.pdf,” plus photographs of the controller display and probe positions. In section 3 I retained your observation that the stainless thermowell lagged the taped external probe by roughly 18 minutes during cooling. Please check that I have described your method accurately; I know you were adapting the same sort of sanity-check you use when a river-gauge logger starts drifting, but I don’t want to overstate the precision.

One remaining question: your graph shows a brief drop from 27.4°C to 24.9°C at 22:31, then an immediate return to 27.2°C. Do you think that is when I lifted the probe while adding the wet towels, or should we flag it as a missing/invalid reading? My handwritten note says “wrap on 22:28,” so the timing fits. I’d rather annotate it than silently smooth it out.

If you can send the corrected timeline by Friday afternoon, I’ll add the sensory notes and forward the complete record to Ben. There’s no hurry tonight, especially if you’re out checking the upstream gauges after the rain.

Thanks again for turning my rather panicked messages into something usable.

Best,
Natalie
