product_00127.name: Swift-Water Rescue Clinical Reference Card Set

options.copy: A waterproof, field-ready clinical reference designed for swift-water rescue trainers, gauge technicians and remote crews working around rivers, floodwater and wet environments. The quick-reference cards summarise primary surveys, drowning response, hypothermia staging, cold-water shock, trauma checks, oxygen guidance, patient handover prompts and Australian emergency contact procedures. High-contrast diagrams and tabbed sections are readable in rain, with glove-friendly rounded corners and a lanyard attachment for use beside a personal flotation device or first-aid kit. In the box: 18 double-sided synthetic reference cards, a corrosion-resistant split ring, detachable lanyard, compact protective pouch and contents index. This set is an aide-memoire only; it does not replace accredited rescue or clinical training, local water-authority procedures, medical direction or current ANZCOR guidelines.

options.copy: Protect vegetable, native grass and riparian restoration seed from Brisbane’s humidity, summer storms and accidental splashes with this rugged waterproof storage vault. Designed for home seed collections, field revegetation kits and keeping replacement seed organised between river-gauge maintenance trips, it has a gasket-sealed polypropylene shell, pressure-equalisation valve and removable dividers for packets of different sizes. The bright orange case is easy to spot in a vehicle, shed or rescue-equipment store, while the carry handle and dual latches suit transport to remote planting sites. In the box: one seed vault, six adjustable dividers, 24 write-on seed envelopes, 12 reusable silica-gel sachets, a humidity indicator card and a waterproof label sheet. Limitation: the vault resists temporary immersion when correctly latched, but it is not intended for prolonged underwater storage and does not replace refrigeration for seed requiring cold preservation.

product_00129.name: RiverTrack R50 Waterproof Handheld GPS Navigator

options.copy: Built for river-gauge inspections, flood-response work and swift-water rescue training, the RiverTrack R50 provides dependable position, track and waypoint navigation from a compact, glove-friendly handheld unit. Its IPX7 waterproof housing, high-visibility colour display and physical controls suit wet boats, muddy banks and heavy rain, while GPS, Galileo and GLONASS reception helps maintain a fix in steep or tree-lined waterways. Mark gauge sites, ramps, access tracks and hazards, then transfer GPX routes and field data by USB-C. The replaceable AA battery system is practical for long shifts away from mains power, and the integrated compass and barometric altimeter assist with orientation and changing-weather awareness. In the box: R50 navigator, Brisbane and South East Queensland river basemap, USB-C data cable, wrist lanyard, belt clip, quick-start guide and two alkaline AA batteries. Limitation: the included basemap is intended for general navigation and does not replace official nautical charts, flood intelligence or rescue-agency procedures.

product_00130.name: RiverTrack Portable Electromagnetic Flow Meter Kit

options.copy: Measure stream velocity and calculate discharge during river-gauge inspections, rating runs and swift-water training site assessments. The waterproof handheld meter provides live, average, minimum and maximum velocity readings, while the low-profile electromagnetic sensor works in shallow, silty or weed-prone channels without a moving propeller. A backlit display, glove-friendly controls and internal logging suit long field days around Brisbane’s creeks and floodways. The kit includes the handheld display/logger, velocity sensor with selected cable length, graduated 1.5 m wading rod, adjustable sensor mount, USB data cable, rechargeable battery, mains charger, field lanyard, cleaning brush, quick-start guide, calibration certificate and padded hard case. Limitation: this is a wading-deployment instrument and is not rated for unattended submersion or use from a moving boat; measurements in unsafe flood flows require an appropriate remote gauging method.

A backlit display, glove-friendly controls and internal logging suit long field days around Brisbane’s creeks and floodways. The kit includes the handheld display/logger, velocity sensor with selected cable length, graduated 1.5 m wading rod, adjustable sensor mount, USB data cable, rechargeable battery, mains charger, field lanyard, cleaning brush, quick-start guide, calibration certificate and padded hard case. Limitation: this is a wading-deployment instrument and is not rated for unattended submersion or use from a moving boat; measurements in unsafe flood flows require an appropriate remote gauging method.
options.label: 10 m sensor cable

product_00131.name: RiverSafe Archival Textile Drying & Support Mesh

options.copy: A conservation-grade polyester mesh for supporting flood-wet uniforms, rescue-training textiles, field satchels and historic fabric items during rinsing, draining and flat drying. The open, non-absorbent weave allows water and air to pass through while reducing stretching, snagging and handling stress—useful when stabilising mud- or silt-affected textiles after fieldwork around Brisbane waterways. It can be cut to line wash trays, create lifting slings or separate layers on a drying rack, and the smooth edges resist fraying after trimming. Each box contains one roll of white inert polyester support mesh, two reusable fastening clips, an archival label pencil and a quick guide to handling water-affected textiles. Rinse and air-dry the mesh between uses; no conservation chemicals are applied. Limitation: this product provides physical support only and will not disinfect, remove stains or make contaminated rescue PPE safe for operational reuse; sewage-affected or chemically exposed items require specialist assessment.

product_00132.name: RiverTrack Rugged Digital Brewing Refractometer Kit

options.copy: Built for brewers who appreciate field-ready instruments, the RiverTrack Digital Refractometer quickly checks wort or must sugar concentration in Brix and estimated specific gravity. Its splash-resistant housing, bright backlit display and pocket-sized format suit brew-day benches, crowded sheds and weekends away from Brisbane. Apply a few cooled drops to the stainless-steel sample well for a reading without filling a test jar. The box includes the digital refractometer, protective hard case, sampling pipettes, calibration dropper, microfibre cloth, wrist lanyard, two AAA batteries and a quick-reference conversion card. Automatic temperature compensation helps manage warm Queensland conditions. Limitation: once fermentation begins, alcohol distorts direct specific-gravity readings, so fermented samples require a correction calculator or conventional hydrometer confirmation; the unit is splash-resistant but not waterproof or suitable for immersion.
options.label: Standard Kit

product_00133.name: RiverTrack 32-Bit Wireless Field Audio & Caption Kit

options.copy: Capture clear spoken notes during river-gauge inspections, record training commentary from the bank and produce accurately timed audio for safety-video subtitles. Each compact transmitter records a 32-bit float backup, while the receiver feeds a camera, phone or laptop and generates timecode markers that simplify transcript and caption alignment. Intelligent gain control helps with rushing-water noise, and the supplied furry windscreens reduce wind rumble during exposed field work. In the box: two clip-on recorder/transmitters, dual-channel receiver, two lavalier microphones, two furry windscreens, magnetic clips, camera and USB-C audio cables, charging case, hard-shell field pouch and quick-start guide. The 4-Person variant adds a second paired kit and larger pouch. Limitation: the components are splash-resistant only, not waterproof or suitable for immersion; keep them inside a waterproof pouch when working from boats or near swift water.

product_00134.name: GME MT610G GPS Personal Locator Beacon

options.copy: A compact 406 MHz personal locator beacon for offshore passages, remote river-gauge inspections and swift-water training where mobile coverage cannot be relied upon. When activated, the MT610G transmits a distress alert with GNSS coordinates through the Cospas-Sarsat satellite network, while its 121.5 MHz homing signal and high-intensity strobe assist rescue crews during the final approach. The IP68-rated housing is designed for harsh, wet conditions and can be secured to a PFD, work vest or equipment bag using the supplied attachment gear. In the box: MT610G beacon with sealed long-life battery, mounting pouch, lanyard, belt clip, reflective tape, registration instructions and user guide. Limitation: this PLB does not provide two-way messaging or confirmation that rescuers are responding, and it must be registered to the owner and manually activated with a clear view of the sky. It is not a substitute for an EPIRB where maritime regulations require one.
options.label: Yellow

product_00135.name: RiverReach Fibreglass Telescopic Pole Saw & Pruner

options.copy: Maintain access around river gauges, monitoring stations and rescue-training sites without hauling a ladder onto steep or waterlogged banks. The RiverReach combines a curved 330 mm impulse-hardened saw blade with a rope-operated bypass pruner for trimming overhanging branches and cutting green stems up to 30 mm thick. Its oval fibreglass pole offers a secure, corrosion-resistant grip in humid riverside conditions, while positive-lock extension collars help keep the selected reach stable. The removable head and compact collapsed length make it practical to carry in a field vehicle alongside gauging equipment. In the box: telescopic fibreglass pole, bypass-pruner head, 330 mm saw blade, blade guard, pull rope with handle, shoulder carry strap, adjustment spanner and instructions. Limitation: the fibreglass shaft is not certified as electrically insulated; never use this tool near overhead powerlines, and do not use it for storm-damaged or tensioned limbs.

product_00137.name: Swift-Water Casualty Field Reference Card Set

options.copy: A waterproof clinical reference set for swift-water rescue training, river-gauge fieldwork and first-response support in wet, remote environments. The colour-coded cards summarise primary surveys, drowning and aspiration care, hypothermia staging, cold-shock risks, spinal precautions, bleeding control, oxygen guidance, CPR prompts, patient observations and structured handover using Australian terminology. Durable synthetic stock, rounded corners and a stainless split ring allow the set to be clipped inside a rescue pack or field vest. The box contains 18 double-sided reference cards, a compact casualty-observation card, a permanent wet-surface pencil, split ring, snap hook and protective storage sleeve. Limitation: this is a quick-reference aid only; it does not replace accredited clinical training, current Queensland Ambulance Service guidance, local rescue protocols or advice from a registered health professional.

product_00139.name: Garmin GPSMAP 67i Rugged Handheld GPS & Satellite Communicator

options.copy: Navigate remote river corridors, record gauge locations and maintain contact beyond mobile coverage with the Garmin GPSMAP 67i. Built for wet fieldwork and swift-water operations, this IPX7-rated handheld combines multi-band GNSS positioning, preloaded TopoActive Australia and New Zealand maps, an electronic compass, barometric altimeter and inReach two-way satellite messaging. Long battery life supports multi-day inspections, while physical buttons remain practical with wet hands or gloves. The standard box includes the GPSMAP 67i handheld, rechargeable lithium-ion battery, USB-C charging/data cable, carabiner clip and documentation. Available bundles add a protective case or powered vehicle mount for authority utes and rescue equipment caches. Limitation: inReach messaging, tracking and SOS functions require an active satellite subscription, and satellite reception may be reduced in deep gorges, beneath dense canopy or indoors.

product_00141.name: RiverReady Archival Textile Drying Mesh Kit

options.copy: A conservation-grade drying support designed for stabilising wet or recently cleaned textiles, including flood-affected uniforms, rescue-training equipment covers, field satchels, flags and fabric gauge-station records. The inert polyester mesh promotes airflow while supporting fibres evenly, helping reduce distortion during air drying after rinsing or emergency salvage. It can be laid across a clean table or raised on blocks for ventilation from both sides—useful in Brisbane’s humid conditions. Each box contains one reusable polyester drying mesh, four polypropylene corner clips, two acid-free blotting sheets, a soft handling spatula and illustrated cleaning and drying instructions. Choose a size suited to the item and use multiple meshes for larger collections. Limitation: this kit is not suitable for load-bearing drying of ropes, harnesses or other safety-critical swift-water rescue equipment, and it does not replace controlled dehumidification or specialist treatment for mould, dyes that bleed, or severely degraded fibres.

options.copy: A compact emergency beacon for hydrology field crews, boat operators and swift-water rescue trainers working around remote rivers, estuaries and offshore waters. When activated, it transmits a 406 MHz distress alert with GNSS position through the Cospas-Sarsat satellite network, while a 121.5 MHz homing signal and high-intensity strobe help rescuers close in. The buoyant, waterproof housing clips securely to a PFD or equipment harness, and the protected controls reduce accidental activation while climbing gauge structures or handling rescue lines. Registration with the Australian Maritime Safety Authority is free and links the beacon to your emergency contacts. In the box: RiverWatch beacon with sealed battery, PFD mounting clip, detachable lanyard, reflective identification labels, registration instructions and quick-start guide. Limitation: it is a manually activated personal locator beacon and does not replace an EPIRB where one is legally required for a vessel.

product_00146.name: RiverTrack Waterproof Sequential Cable Tags – 100 Pack

options.copy: Keep river-gauge cases, rescue ropes, throw bags, dry boxes and field instruments identifiable through wet transport, deployment and storage. These flexible logistics tags are made from water-resistant synthetic stock with pre-printed sequential numbers and a writable panel for asset IDs, inspection dates or destination codes. Rounded edges help prevent snagging, while the self-locking tails fit case handles, rope bags, cage mesh and equipment loops without separate fasteners. Permanent marker remains legible during rain, spray and muddy fieldwork. Each box contains 100 sequentially numbered tags, one fine-tip permanent marker and a resealable storage pouch suitable for a vehicle kit or depot shelf. Choose a high-visibility colour to separate calibrated instruments, quarantine items, rescue-training gear or equipment awaiting return. Limitation: these tags are intended for identification and stock control only; they are not load-rated, tamper-evident or suitable as life-safety equipment, and prolonged UV exposure may cause fading.

options.copy: Built for river-gauge inspections, boat-based fieldwork and swift-water rescue training, the Garmin GPSMAP 79s provides dependable handheld navigation on Brisbane’s rivers, creeks and coastal approaches. Its sunlight-readable colour display, high-sensitivity multi-GNSS receiver, three-axis electronic compass and barometric altimeter help crews record sites, follow routes and relocate access or recovery points. The rugged, IPX7-rated housing floats if dropped overboard, while glove-friendly buttons suit wet working conditions. options.copy: Measure point velocity in rivers, creeks, culverts and open channels when verifying rating curves, checking gauge sites or assessing current strength for swift-water training. The compact electromagnetic probe reads flow from 0.02 to 5.0 m/s in either direction, while the splash-resistant handheld display records average, minimum and maximum velocity with date and time. A threaded probe mount suits standard wading rods, and high-visibility cable markings simplify deployment from banks, bridges or shallow crossings. In the box: velocity probe with selected cable length, handheld display unit, rechargeable battery, USB charging lead, wading-rod adaptor, lanyard, calibration certificate, quick-start guide and padded field case. Limitation: the meter measures water velocity only and does not calculate discharge without separate depth and cross-section measurements; it is also not rated for use in explosive atmospheres.

options.copy: A portable conservation kit for air-drying waterlogged fabric items after fieldwork, flood response or swift-water training. A hooked blade tip keeps the saw in the kerf and assists with retrieving small cut branches, while the high-visibility locking collars are easy to check in shaded vegetation. In the box: telescopic pole assembly, replaceable pruning blade, branch hook, blade guard, shoulder carry strap, hex key and care guide. Choose the reach that suits vehicle-based gauge rounds or longer walk-in approaches. Limitation: intended for pruning small to medium branches only; it is not insulated, must not be used near powerlines, and is unsuitable for cutting while standing in flowing water or on unstable banks.

options.copy: A waterproof, wipe-clean clinical reference set designed for swift-water rescue training, river-gauge fieldwork and first-response use in wet environments. Limitation: this set is a quick-reference aid only; it does not replace accredited clinical training, current Queensland service protocols, medical direction or equipment-specific instructions.

product_00159.name: Garmin GPSMAP 79s Rugged Floating Handheld GPS

options.copy: Built for river-gauge inspections, flood-response crews and swift-water rescue training, the GPSMAP 79s provides reliable handheld navigation when spray, rain and fast-moving water make phones impractical. Its high-contrast colour display is readable outdoors, while large glove-friendly buttons simplify waypoint marking and route checks from a boat or riverbank. The buoyant, IPX7-rated housing helps prevent loss during accidental drops, and multi-band GNSS support improves positioning near steep banks, bridges and tree cover. Use it to record gauge locations, navigate back to access points and share field coordinates with a response team. In the box: GPSMAP 79s handheld, preloaded worldwide basemap, USB cable, wrist lanyard and documentation. It runs on two replaceable AA batteries, sold separately. Limitation: detailed Australian marine charts and topographic maps are not included and may require a separate purchase or download; it is a navigation aid, not a substitute for official flood intelligence or rescue procedures.

product_00160.name: Heron Little Dipper 2 Electronic Water Level Meter

options.copy: A compact electronic dip meter for checking water levels in monitoring bores, piezometers and river-gauge stilling wells. The corrosion-resistant stainless-steel probe gives bright LED and audible indications on contact with water, while the permanently marked polyethylene tape allows repeatable depth-to-water readings in metres and centimetres. Its lightweight reel is easy to carry along riverbanks and includes a brake, winding handle and probe holder for tidy deployment between sites. In the box: Little Dipper 2 meter with selected tape length, 16 mm probe, fitted battery, reel and frame, vinyl carry bag, operating guide and test certificate. Limitation: this is a manual point-reading instrument rather than a logging sensor, and turbulent, highly conductive or contaminated water may require sensitivity adjustment and careful interpretation.

options.copy: A conservation-grade polyester mesh designed to support wet or freshly washed textiles while they dry flat, reducing stretching, creasing and stress on weakened fibres. Its open weave promotes airflow and allows water to drain, making it useful for stabilising flood-affected uniforms, rescue-training flags, fabric equipment covers, sample bags and historic water-authority textiles after appropriate rinsing. The mesh can be laid over a drying rack or used beneath an item during handling; smooth cut edges help minimise snagging. In the box: one reusable sheet of white, inert polyester drying mesh in the selected size, folded with an acid-free tissue interleaf, plus a concise care and handling guide. Limitation: this mesh is a support surface only—it does not clean, disinfect or remove mould, and fragile, dyed or contaminated textiles should be assessed by a qualified conservator before wet treatment.

options.copy: Monitor beer, cider or mead without repeatedly opening the fermenter. Built for data-minded brewers, RiverTrack floats in the brew and logs specific gravity and temperature to the companion phone app, making it easy to review fermentation curves after a day servicing river gauges or running weekend rescue training. Its sealed, impact-resistant body is easy to sanitise, while Bluetooth syncing suits a Brisbane garage, laundry or temperature-controlled brewing fridge. The box contains one wireless hydrometer, rechargeable battery, USB-C charging cable, calibration weight, spare food-grade silicone O-rings, protective storage tube and quick-start calibration guide. Select a bright shell colour to help separate batches or spot the unit among brewing gear. Limitation: Bluetooth range is reduced by stainless-steel fermenters, insulated fridge walls and solid masonry, so readings may require syncing near the vessel rather than remotely from the field.

options.copy: Capture clear spoken observations at river gauges, record incident debriefs and produce clean dialogue tracks for subtitled swift-water rescue training videos. The H1essential uses 32-bit float recording to handle sudden changes from quiet voice notes to loud water and shouted commands without manual gain adjustment. Its compact stereo microphones suit handheld interviews, site ambience and equipment checks, while the supplied furry windshield helps reduce wind noise on exposed riverbanks. USB microphone operation also supports online briefings and automatic transcription workflows back at the office. In the box: Zoom H1essential recorder, selected-capacity microSD card, furry windshield, foam windscreen, shock-isolating handgrip, USB-C cable, stereo headphones, protective hard case and quick-start guide. Limitation: the recorder is not waterproof and must remain in its case or under suitable rain protection around spray, storms and rescue training.

options.copy: A compact 406 MHz personal locator beacon designed for offshore crews, remote river-gauge technicians and swift-water rescue trainers who need a last-resort distress signal beyond mobile coverage. When manually activated, it transmits an emergency alert with GNSS position data through the international search-and-rescue satellite network; an integrated 121.5 MHz homing signal and high-intensity strobe help responders locate the user. The buoyant, waterproof housing clips to a lifejacket or field vest, while a guarded control reduces accidental activation during boat work and flood deployments. In the box: RiverWatch 406 GPS beacon with sealed battery, flotation pouch, attachment lanyard, belt/PFD clip, registration instructions and quick-reference guide. Limitation: this PLB must be manually activated and registered to its owner; it does not replace a vessel EPIRB or guarantee immediate rescue.

product_00170.name: RiverTrack Pro Portable Electromagnetic Flow Meter Kit

options.copy: Measure stream velocity and calculate discharge during river-gauge inspections, rating-curve surveys and swift-water training exercises. The waterproof electromagnetic sensor delivers stable readings in shallow, silty or weed-affected channels where mechanical impellers can foul, while the handheld display records velocity, depth, site ID, date and time for later CSV transfer. A telescopic wading rod marked in centimetres helps position the sensor consistently through a vertical profile, and the high-visibility case is suited to transport between remote Brisbane catchment sites. The box includes the flow sensor, selected-length sensor cable, IP67 handheld logger, 1.8 m graduated telescopic wading rod, rod mounting bracket, USB data cable, rechargeable battery pack, mains charger, vehicle charger, lanyard, cleaning brush, quick-start guide and foam-lined hard case. Limitation: this contact instrument requires safe wading access and is not suitable for flood flows, deep channels or use from a bridge without a separate suspension system.

product_00171.name: River Recovery Wet Textile Support Kit

options.copy: Stabilise waterlogged uniforms, historic flood records, fabric equipment and other fragile textiles during rinsing, lifting and air-drying. Designed for field stations, rescue training stores and small conservation workspaces, the rigid polypropylene mesh supports saturated material evenly so it can be moved without pulling weakened fibres. Smooth rounded edges reduce snagging, while removable polyester screen liners keep small fragments and detached threads with the object. Each box contains one reusable support tray in the selected size, two washable polyester mesh liners, four soft hook-and-loop securing straps, 20 acid-free identification tags, a graphite pencil and a wet-textile handling guide. The tray and liners can be rinsed after muddy-water recovery and dried for repeat use. Limitation: this kit supports handling and passive air-drying only; it does not disinfect contaminated textiles or replace specialist treatment for mould, sewage exposure, dyes that bleed, or culturally sensitive material.

options.copy: Brew beer, cider or sparkling water at home with a lightweight pressure-capable fermenter that suits busy rosters and compact storage. The clear PET vessel lets you check fermentation and sediment without opening the lid, while the wide neck simplifies cleaning after long days in the field. Pressure-rated hardware supports closed transfers and natural carbonation, helping reduce oxygen exposure when moving a finished brew into a keg. The box includes one PET fermenter vessel, screw lid, pressure-rated stainless-steel carbonation cap, floating dip tube with filter, liquid and gas ball-lock posts, adjustable pressure-relief valve with gauge, stick-on temperature strip, silicone seals and a cleaning brush. Choose the capacity that matches your batch size. Limitation: this kit does not include a CO₂ cylinder, regulator, keg or temperature-control system, and the PET vessel must not be filled with liquid above 50°C.

options.copy: Capture clear field notes, river-gauge commentary, interviews and rescue-training dialogue in rain, spray and windy conditions. This rugged dual-channel recorder pairs two clip-on wireless microphones with automatic timecode and speech-focused WAV recording, making footage easier to synchronise and prepare for subtitles back at the office. The recorder and transmitters are IP67-rated when their sealed covers are fitted, while included furry windshields help control gust noise beside rivers and weirs. Each transmitter also stores a safety recording in case the wireless signal drops. In the box: one recorder/receiver, two wireless microphone transmitters, two lavalier microphones, three furry windshields, locking clips, USB-C charging and data cable, 3.5 mm camera cable, USB-C phone adaptor, weatherproof carry case and quick-start guide. Limitation: the kit withstands temporary accidental immersion but is not designed for underwater recording or use during a swimmer deployment.

options.copy: A compact personal locator beacon for offshore fieldwork, remote river-gauge visits and swift-water rescue training around Brisbane and beyond. When activated, it transmits a 406 MHz distress alert with GNSS position through the international Cospas-Sarsat satellite network, while a 121.5 MHz homing signal and high-intensity strobe assist search crews at close range. The buoyant, waterproof housing clips to a PFD or equipment harness, and the protected controls help prevent accidental activation in boats, rain and turbulent water. In the box: RiverWatch 406 GPS beacon with sealed long-life battery, PFD mounting clip, retention lanyard, reflective identification label, registration instructions and user guide. Limitation: this beacon does not provide two-way messaging or confirm that rescuers have received the alert; it must be registered with the Australian Maritime Safety Authority and should only be activated in a genuine emergency.

options.copy: A compact arborist hand saw for trimming small branches and woody growth around river-gauge enclosures, access tracks and training sites. Its impulse-hardened curved blade cuts efficiently on the pull stroke, while the high-visibility handle is easy to locate among wet vegetation. A locking blade and textured, drainage-channel grip support controlled use in Brisbane’s humid conditions, and the reinforced lanyard eye lets you attach an appropriate tool tether when working near water or from a stable platform. In the box: one folding pruning saw, one replaceable steel blade, one adjustable wrist lanyard, one belt holster and a care guide. Rinse and dry the blade after exposure to muddy or brackish water, then apply light oil before storage. Limitation: this is a manual pruning saw for small limbs only; it is not electrically insulated and must not be used near live powerlines, during rope rescue operations, while wading in moving water or for cutting loaded storm-damaged timber.

Its sunlight-readable 3-inch display is easy to check from a tinny or riverbank, while IPX7 waterproofing, glove-friendly buttons and a buoyant housing suit wet field conditions. Record access routes to remote monitoring sites, mark hazards or launch points, and share GPX files with operational mapping software. The rechargeable battery delivers up to 20 hours of tracking, with USB-C charging from a vehicle or power bank. Limitation: detailed Australian marine charts and topographic maps are not included and must be purchased or loaded separately; the unit is also not a substitute for mandated emergency beacons or official navigation equipment.

product_00189.name: RiverTrack R7 Floating Handheld Marine GPS

options.copy: Built for river-gauge inspections, flood-response work and swift-water rescue training, the RiverTrack R7 provides reliable position, track and waypoint navigation in a rugged, buoyant handheld unit. Its glove-friendly controls, sunlight-readable 3.2-inch display and IPX7 waterproof housing suit wet boats, muddy banks and subtropical downpours. Mark monitoring sites, ramps, hazards and rescue access points, then export recorded tracks and field coordinates via USB-C. Multi-constellation GNSS reception supports GPS, Galileo and GLONASS, while an electronic compass and barometric altimeter assist when moving slowly or working beneath partial tree cover. In the box are the R7 GPS, rechargeable battery pack, USB-C cable, wrist lanyard, belt clip, screen protector and quick-start guide. Limitation: this model does not provide satellite messaging or emergency beacon functions, and detailed Australian marine or topographic charts must be purchased separately.

Two compact transmitters feature wind-resistant omnidirectional mics and 32-bit float backup recording, while the USB-C receiver connects to a phone, tablet or laptop for recording, live transcription and subtitle workflows. A 250 m line-of-sight range suits demonstrations conducted from the bank, and the high-visibility cases are easy to locate among wet-weather gear. In the box: two clip-on transmitters, USB-C receiver, charging case, two lavalier microphones, two furry windshields, magnetic clips, 3.5 mm camera cable, USB-C and Lightning adaptor cables, lanyard, storage pouch and quick-start guide. Limitation: the transmitters are splash-resistant only; the receiver and charging case are not waterproof and must be protected around spray or immersion.

product_00194.name: RiverWatch 406 MHz GPS Personal Locator Beacon

options.copy: A compact personal locator beacon for hydrology field crews, rescue trainers and offshore users who need a last-resort distress signal when mobile coverage is unavailable. Once activated, it transmits a 406 MHz alert and encoded GPS position through the international Cospas-Sarsat satellite network, while a 121.5 MHz homing signal helps search teams close in. The buoyant, high-visibility housing clips to a PFD or field vest and includes a protective activation flap, strobe light, self-test function and replace-by battery indicator. In the box: one RiverWatch GPS beacon with sealed long-life battery, PFD mounting clip, reflective lanyard, registration guide and quick-start card. Australian beacon registration is free but must be completed before use. Limitation: this beacon is for grave and imminent danger only; it does not provide two-way messaging, and buoyancy does not guarantee that the antenna will remain correctly oriented if activated while floating unattended.

options.copy: Set accurate access lines in riverside trees, gauge-station approaches and training-site canopies with this high-visibility arborist throwline kit. The low-stretch, slick-braid line runs smoothly through forks, while the weighted throw bag has a bright body that is easy to track against dense subtropical foliage. A ventilated folding cube keeps the line flaked and ready between inspections, helping reduce tangles when working on muddy banks or in humid Brisbane conditions. The kit is intended for positioning a rated climbing or work line before pruning, inspection or canopy access. In the box: one 50 m high-visibility throwline, one reinforced throw bag in the selected weight, one collapsible storage cube, one mini attachment carabiner and a printed quick-start guide. Limitation: the throwline, throw bag and accessory carabiner are not life-support equipment and must never be used for climbing, fall arrest, hauling people or swift-water rescue.

product_00196.name: RiverTrack Tamper-Evident Waterproof Field Transport Bags

options.copy: Keep water samples, gauge downloads, inspection sheets and small wet-weather spares organised between remote river sites, the depot and the laboratory. RiverTrack bags use a tough, clear polyethylene body with a write-on identification panel and individually numbered tamper-evident seal, helping maintain chain-of-custody records during hydrology rounds. The leak-resistant closure and secondary document pocket separate paperwork from damp sample containers, while the high-visibility blue strip is easy to spot in a field crate or rescue-training equipment cache. Each box contains 100 single-use transport bags with sequential security numbers, write-on panels and detachable receipt stubs. Choose a capacity suited to data loggers, water-sample bottles or grouped consumables. Limitation: these bags are splash- and leak-resistant but are not certified for dangerous goods, biological specimens or prolonged submersion, and they cannot be resealed after opening.

product_00197.name: Swift-Water & Drowning Care Waterproof Clinical Field Guide

options.copy: A splash-proof clinical reference designed for swift-water rescue trainers, river-gauge crews and first responders working around floods, weirs and fast-moving waterways. The colour-coded pages summarise drowning assessment, hypothermia care, oxygen and ventilation priorities, spinal precautions, casualty monitoring, handover prompts and Australian resuscitation guidance. Durable synthetic pages can be wiped clean after muddy field exercises, while tabbed sections and high-contrast diagrams support quick consultation in rain or low light. In the box: one spiral-bound waterproof field guide, a removable adult and paediatric observation card, a grease pencil and a lanyard clip for securing the guide inside a rescue pack. Limitation: this is a quick-reference aid only; it does not replace accredited clinical training, local water-authority procedures, current ANZCOR guidelines or direction from ambulance and medical personnel.

options.copy: A rugged, weather-sealed storage case for carrying native riparian, wetland and erosion-control seed between the nursery, gauge sites and volunteer planting days. The crush-resistant shell, silicone gasket and stainless-steel latch help protect seed packets from rain, spray, mud and accidental drops in the ute, while removable dividers keep species and collection lots separated. A writable inventory card supports recording provenance, harvest date and treatment notes, and the bright orange finish is easy to locate among field gear. The box contains one seed vault, six adjustable dividers, twelve reusable paper seed envelopes, twelve waterproof labels, a permanent marker and an inventory card. Capacity variants suit anything from a compact day kit to a larger revegetation programme. Limitation: the case is not designed for prolonged submersion, and it does not control temperature or humidity, so thoroughly dried seed and desiccant may still be required for long-term storage in Brisbane conditions.

options.copy: Built for river-gauge inspections, small-boat work and swift-water rescue training, the RiverTrack IPX7 Handheld GPS Navigator provides reliable position, track and waypoint data without relying on mobile reception. Its high-contrast 3-inch sunlight-readable display is easy to check from a tinny or riverbank, while glove-friendly buttons, a buoyant high-visibility shell and IPX7 waterproofing suit Brisbane’s wet, muddy field conditions. Mark gauge sites, boat ramps, hazards and training points, then transfer GPX routes and logs by USB. The replaceable AA battery system is practical for long shifts away from charging facilities. In the box are the handheld GPS unit, wrist lanyard, belt clip, USB data cable, two alkaline AA batteries, quick-start guide and protective screen film. Limitation: detailed marine charts and live traffic or weather data are not included; this unit must not replace official charts, local warnings or required safety equipment.

product_00200.name: RiverPulse Pro Handheld Electromagnetic Flow Meter

options.copy: Measure stream velocity during gauging runs, rating-curve checks and culvert assessments with a rugged electromagnetic sensor designed for Brisbane creeks, rivers and flood channels. The backlit handheld displays live, minimum, maximum and averaged velocity in m/s, while IP67 construction, glove-friendly controls and internal logging support wet-weather fieldwork. Selectable averaging intervals help smooth turbulent readings, and stored datasets can be transferred to a computer by USB-C. In the box: RiverPulse Pro meter, velocity sensor with 3 m cable, graduated wading rod in the selected length, adjustable sensor mount, rechargeable battery, USB-C charging/data cable, wrist lanyard, hard carry case, quick-start guide and calibration certificate. Limitation: the sensor must remain fully submerged and correctly aligned with the flow, so it is unsuitable for non-contact flood measurement or deployment where wading conditions are unsafe.

options.copy: A field-ready conservation kit for stabilising waterlogged uniforms, fabric logbook covers, rescue-training textiles and other small woven items after flood, river or storm exposure. Designed for controlled blotting, flat support and transport from remote gauge stations to a suitable drying area, it helps reduce distortion and prevents fragile wet fibres from being lifted unsupported. The box contains 25 sheets of acid-free unprinted blotting paper, 10 polyester spunbond support sheets, 5 archival corrugated-plastic support boards, 20 reusable polyethylene interleaving sheets, 10 soft cotton tying tapes, nitrile gloves, pencil labels and a waterproof handling guide. Choose the kit capacity to match routine vehicle storage or larger incident-response caches. Limitation: this kit is for temporary stabilisation only; it does not disinfect sewage-contaminated textiles, remove stains or replace treatment by a qualified textile conservator.

options.copy: Brew clean beer, cider or sparkling water around an unpredictable field roster with this tough, transparent pressure fermenter. The wide opening makes ingredient loading and cleaning straightforward, while the pressure-rated vessel lets you ferment, carbonate and transfer into a keg with minimal oxygen exposure. Its moulded volume marks are easy to read after long days servicing river gauges, and the compact footprint suits a Brisbane garage or utility room. In the box: PET fermenter vessel, screw-on lid, pressure-relief valve, adjustable spunding valve with gauge, floating dip tube, stainless sampling tap, collection cup, carry handles, seals and cleaning brush. Choose the capacity that matches your batch size; all variants use replaceable standard seals. Limitation: PET can scratch and retain microbes, so use only soft cleaning tools, and do not expose the vessel to boiling liquid, direct Queensland sun or pressure above the marked working limit.

options.copy: Capture clear spoken notes beside river gauges, under bridges or during swift-water rescue training with this compact bodypack recorder. Its 32-bit float recording handles sudden changes from quiet technical commentary to shouted instructions without constant gain adjustment, while Bluetooth control and wireless timecode support help align audio with inspection video for accurate captions and training subtitles. A low-cut filter reduces traffic rumble and wind noise, and the locking lavalier connector helps prevent accidental disconnection while moving through the field. In the box are the F2-BT recorder, LMF-2 omnidirectional lavalier microphone, locking mic clip, foam windscreen, belt clip, two AAA batteries and quick-start documentation. Recordings are saved to a separately purchased microSD card. Limitation: the recorder and supplied microphone are not waterproof, so they must remain in a suitable dry pouch around spray, rain or rescue operations.

options.copy: A compact 165N automatic inflatable lifejacket for gauge-boat inspections, estuary crossings and offshore work where dependable flotation and all-day mobility matter. Its ergonomic bladder is designed to rotate an unconscious wearer face-up, while the adjustable waist belt, crotch strap, lifting becket, whistle and reflective detailing support recovery in low light. The automatic firing head inflates on water entry, with a manual pull toggle and oral inflation tube as backups. In the box: one adult inflatable PFD with fitted 33 g CO₂ cylinder and activation cartridge, integrated crotch strap, whistle, protective cover and user/maintenance guide. Check the status indicator before each deployment and service the jacket at the specified interval. Limitation: this is not a high-buoyancy swift-water rescue PFD and has no tether points for technical river rescue; automatic inflation may also be unsuitable where repeated immersion is expected.

options.copy: Maintain clear sightlines and safe access around river gauges, telemetry stations and riparian tracks without carrying a chainsaw into wet, remote terrain. The RiverReach manual pole saw uses a lightweight oval-section fibreglass shaft, positive-lock telescopic clamps and a 390 mm impulse-hardened curved blade for controlled cutting of overhanging branches. A hooked blade tip helps retain the cut, while the replaceable lower sickle is useful for vines and small growth around gauge structures. The tool collapses for transport in a field vehicle or rescue-equipment trailer, and its high-visibility grip is easy to spot beside dense riverbank vegetation. Limitation: intended for manual pruning of branches up to 100 mm diameter only; it is not electrically insulated and must not be used near powerlines or while standing in flowing water.

product_00209.name: Garmin GPSMAP 79s Rugged Floating Handheld Navigator

options.copy: Built for river-gauge servicing, flood inspections and swift-water rescue training, the GPSMAP 79s provides dependable handheld navigation from a high-visibility, water-resistant housing that floats if dropped overboard. Its button-operated interface remains practical with wet or gloved hands, while multi-band GNSS support helps maintain position beneath tree cover, beside steep banks and around urban structures. Record tracks to remote monitoring sites, mark gauge stations and boat ramps, or use TracBack routing to retrace an approach after conditions change. Wireless connectivity supports compatible Garmin Explore planning and location sharing, and the sunlight-readable colour display is suited to open boats and bright Queensland conditions. In the box are the GPSMAP 79s handheld navigator, preloaded worldwide basemap, wrist strap, USB cable and documentation. Limitation: detailed Australian marine charts and inland-water mapping are not included and may require a separately purchased compatible chart or map download.

product_00210.name: RiverTrack Pro Handheld Electromagnetic Current Meter

options.copy: Measure stream velocity during gauging runs, discharge surveys and post-flood channel inspections with a rugged electromagnetic current meter designed for Australian field conditions. The compact sensor has no moving parts, making it suitable for shallow waterways, silty channels and weed-prone sites where propeller meters can foul. A backlit handheld display provides live velocity, averaging and minimum/maximum readings, while internal logging stores survey points for later transfer to a computer. The IP67 enclosure, high-visibility controls and replaceable batteries support long days beside remote gauges. In the box: velocity sensor with selected cable length, handheld display/logger, wading rod mounting bracket, USB data cable, four AA batteries, protective carry case, calibration certificate and quick-start guide. Limitation: the sensor requires full submersion and stable positioning, so it is not intended for measuring aerated whitewater or use from an unsecured rescuer in swift flow.

product_00214.name: Ocean Signal rescueME PLB1 Personal Locator Beacon

options.copy: A compact 406 MHz personal locator beacon for offshore passages, remote river-gauge inspections and swift-water rescue operations where mobile coverage cannot be relied upon. Once activated, the waterproof PLB transmits a distress alert and GPS position through the global Cospas-Sarsat satellite network, while its 121.5 MHz homing signal and high-intensity strobe help search crews close in. The unit is designed for one-handed deployment and is small enough to secure to a PFD, equipment vest or field pack without obstructing movement. In the box: rescueME PLB1 beacon with long-life battery, flotation pouch, mounting clip, lanyard, registration information and user guide. Australian beacon registration with AMSA is required before use. Limitation: this PLB provides distress signalling only—it does not offer two-way messaging or confirmation from rescuers, and it must be carried in the supplied flotation pouch to float.

A waterproof handheld display provides live velocity, timed averaging, minimum/maximum readings and USB-C data export, while the graduated telescopic wading rod helps position the sensor at standard depth intervals. The box includes the velocity sensor with selected cable length, IP67 display/logger, 0.5–2.0 m stainless wading rod, USB-C cable, mains charger, spare sensor guard, lanyard, quick-start guide, calibration certificate and padded carry case. Limitation: this is a contact instrument intended for safely wadeable sites; it must not be deployed by a person standing in swift, deep or floodwater, and it does not calculate total discharge without a measured cross-section.

options.copy: A portable conservation-grade drying system for stabilising wet uniforms, rescue webbing, fabric equipment pouches and small heritage textiles after flooding or field exposure. The rigid, stackable screens promote airflow above and below saturated material, while the smooth inert mesh supports fibres without transferring dyes or leaving a coarse imprint. It is suitable for a gauge-station workshop, equipment shed or volunteer rescue training store and packs flat between incidents. The box includes two powder-coated aluminium screen frames, removable polyester conservation mesh, four stacking spacers, eight securing clips, a soft sediment-removal brush, twenty acid-free blotting sheets and illustrated wet-textile triage instructions. Choose the screen size to suit available bench space and typical items. Limitation: this kit is intended for air-drying colourfast textiles only; it cannot prevent mould in persistently humid conditions and should not be used on chemically contaminated, badly degraded or dye-bleeding material without advice from a professional conservator.

product_00223.name: RØDE Wireless PRO Dual-Channel Field Audio Kit

options.copy: Capture clear commentary, equipment checks and training dialogue beside noisy rivers with the RØDE Wireless PRO, a compact dual-channel wireless microphone system suited to hydrology field reports, gauge-maintenance videos and swift-water rescue debriefs. Two clip-on transmitters record 32-bit float backup audio internally, while intelligent GainAssist helps manage sudden changes in voice level. Timecode support simplifies synchronising speech with action-camera footage for accurate subtitles, and the included lavalier microphones can be positioned beneath protective clothing. The kit works with cameras, phones and computers and stores neatly in its charging case between site visits. In the box: two transmitters, one receiver, smart charging case, two Lavalier II microphones, three furry windshields, magnetic clips, camera and mobile connection cables, USB-C cable and accessory case. Limitation: the units are not waterproof and must remain inside a dry pouch or protected clothing around spray, rain and swift water.

product_00224.name: RiverReach Pro Floating Rescue Throw Bag

options.copy: Built for swift-water training, river-gauge fieldwork and near-shore vessel emergencies, the RiverReach Pro deploys a high-visibility floating line to a conscious casualty without requiring the rescuer to enter the water. The tough, self-draining bag has reflective panels, a foam flotation insert, a wide throw handle and a corrosion-resistant attachment ring. Its low-stretch polypropylene rope floats for easy spotting and repacking, while printed distance markers help trainers assess throwing accuracy. In the box: one rescue throw bag, one floating rope in the selected length, one removable waist belt with quick-release buckle, one mesh drying pouch and an inspection guide. Limitation: this is a manually thrown rescue aid, not a personal flotation device, fall-arrest line or rated towing rope; effective range and accuracy depend on operator skill, wind and current.

options.copy: Built for maintaining riverbank vegetation, clearing sightlines around gauge stations and pruning storm-damaged branches from the ground, the RiverReach combines a curved arborist saw with a rope-operated bypass pruner. Its oval fibreglass-and-aluminium pole offers a secure wet-weather grip and extends to reach over fences, steep banks and riparian undergrowth without requiring a ladder. The impulse-hardened blade handles green limbs up to 100 mm thick, while the pruner cuts smaller growth up to 25 mm. In the box: telescopic pole, detachable 330 mm saw blade, bypass pruning head, 4 m pull rope, blade scabbard, shoulder carry strap, adjustment spanner and storage bag. Choose the pole length suited to routine gauge access or broader vegetation work. Limitation: this manually operated tool is not insulated and must never be used near overhead electrical conductors; it is also unsuitable for cutting loaded branches during swift-water or flood operations.

product_00227.name: Waterproof Swift-Water & Drowning Clinical Reference Cards

options.copy: A field-ready clinical reference set for swift-water rescue training, river-gauge callouts and remote first-aid kits. The wipe-clean cards provide concise prompts for scene safety, drowning resuscitation, hypothermia assessment, cold-water shock, spinal precautions, oxygen use, patient monitoring and structured handover to Queensland Ambulance Service. High-contrast tables and flow diagrams remain legible in rain, spray and low light, while rounded corners and a stainless-steel binding ring suit use around boats, throw bags and wet PPE. In the box are 18 double-sided waterproof reference cards, a removable stainless-steel ring, a reflective storage sleeve and a fine-tip chinagraph pencil for temporary notes. Available in pocket, vest and training-board formats. This is a quick-reference training aid only; it does not replace accredited clinical education, local rescue protocols, medical direction or current Australian Resuscitation Council guidelines.

product_00228.name: Riverbank Ready Waterproof Native Seed Vault

options.copy: Keep native grass, sedge and riparian restoration seed organised between field inspections, revegetation days and wet-season call-outs. This rugged seed-storage case uses a gasket-sealed outer shell and removable, labelled vials to protect small seed lots from splash, mud and Brisbane’s humid conditions. It fits easily behind a ute seat or in a field-equipment cabinet, while the clear vials make it simple to separate provenance zones, collection dates and species used for stabilising eroded banks. In the box: one impact-resistant waterproof case, removable seed-storage vials sized to the selected capacity, two reusable silica-gel canisters, 40 write-on labels, a permanent marker and a basic seed-drying and storage guide. Limitation: the case provides short-to-medium-term moisture protection only; seeds must be properly dried before packing, and the vault is not a substitute for temperature-controlled long-term conservation storage.

product_00229.name: RiverTrack Pro Rugged Handheld GPS Navigator

options.copy: Built for river-gauge inspections, flood-response work and swift-water rescue training, the RiverTrack Pro provides reliable position, track and waypoint navigation from a glove-friendly handheld unit. Its IPX7-rated housing withstands rain, spray and brief accidental immersion, while a sunlight-readable colour screen makes coordinates, routes and breadcrumb tracks easy to check from a boat or riverbank. Mark gauge sites, access points, hazards and rescue staging areas, then transfer field data by USB. The replaceable AA battery system is practical for long shifts away from vehicle power, and the integrated compass and barometric altimeter assist with orientation and elevation checks. In the box: RiverTrack Pro GPS, preloaded Australia and New Zealand marine basemap, USB cable, wrist lanyard, belt clip, two AA batteries and quick-start guide. Limitation: it is not a certified primary navigation instrument, and detailed inland depth data may be unavailable or outdated after floods and channel changes.

options.copy: Stabilise rain-soaked uniforms, rescue harness webbing, canvas field bags and other washable textiles after river-gauge inspections, flood deployments or training sessions. These conservation-grade, acid-free cotton-linter blotters draw moisture from fabric while it is laid flat, helping reduce tide marks, distortion and slow-drying odours without adding dyes or optical brighteners. They can also be placed between layers when air-drying maps or textile equipment labels. Each box contains 25 white drying blotter sheets, 10 sheets of inert polyester support mesh for lifting delicate items, 20 unprinted archival tissue interleaves and a concise wet-textile handling guide. Blotters may be air-dried and reused when clean, making the kit practical for a workshop or rescue-equipment drying room. options.copy: Capture clear spoken field notes, gauge readings, site interviews and swift-water rescue training debriefs beside noisy waterways. RiverNote combines a compact IP67 recorder with a wind-protected clip microphone and time-stamped WAV recording, making audio easy to match with inspection logs or import into speech-to-text and subtitling software. Physical controls can be operated with work gloves, while selectable low-cut filtering reduces traffic, pump and river rumble. The recorder also works as a USB microphone for office narration or online training sessions. In the box: RiverNote recorder, locking clip-on microphone, foam and furry windscreens, magnetic clothing mount, coiled safety tether, USB-C cable, 32 GB microSD card, monitoring earpiece, hard carry case and quick-start guide. Limitation: although the recorder is IP67-rated with its port cover closed, the external microphone and earpiece are only splash-resistant and must not be submerged.

options.copy: A compact emergency beacon for offshore crews, remote river-gauge technicians and swift-water rescuers who need a last-resort distress signal beyond mobile coverage. When activated, it transmits your registered identity and GNSS position on the global 406 MHz search-and-rescue network, while a 121.5 MHz homing signal and high-intensity strobe help responders close in. The buoyant, waterproof housing can be clipped to a PFD or carried in a field pack, making it suitable for boat inspections, flood deployments and coastal training. In the box: TideSafe 406 GNSS beacon with sealed long-life battery, PFD mounting clip, flotation pouch, wrist lanyard, reflective ID labels, registration guide and quick-start card. The beacon must be registered with AMSA and professionally serviced after activation or battery expiry. Limitation: it does not replace a vessel EPIRB where one is legally required, and it cannot provide two-way communication or confirm that rescuers have received your alert.

options.copy: Maintain clear sightlines around river gauges, access tracks and rescue-training sites with this professional manual pole saw. Its lightweight oval aluminium shaft extends without tools, while the impulse-hardened curved blade cuts overhanging branches, storm-damaged limbs and dense riparian growth from the ground. A hooked blade tip helps retain the kerf and pull down small cut branches, and the textured lower grip remains secure in wet, humid Brisbane conditions. Choose the reach that suits routine gauge rounds or taller vegetation along riverbanks. Limitation: the pole is not electrically insulated and must never be used near powerlines; it is also intended for branches up to 120 mm diameter, not heavy tree felling or powered cutting.

options.copy: A compact clinical reference designed for first responders, river-gauge crews and swift-water rescue trainers working around floods, rivers and remote access sites. Waterproof, mud-resistant pages provide quick guidance on drowning assessment, hypothermia staging, cold-water shock, oxygen use, CPR considerations, trauma checks and structured patient handover. High-contrast flowcharts and Celsius temperature tables remain easy to consult in rain or while wearing gloves. The box contains one spiral-bound field guide, a removable adult and paediatric vital-sign card, a waterproof casualty-observation sheet and a fine-tip marking pencil with tether. Choose Pocket size for a PFD or field-pack pocket, or A5 for larger training diagrams. This guide is a memory aid only: it does not replace accredited clinical training, local Queensland Ambulance Service protocols, medical direction or current ANZCOR guidelines.

options.copy: Built for river-gauge inspections, small-boat navigation and swift-water rescue training, the RiverTrack Pro provides glove-friendly waypoint marking, track recording, compass guidance and tide information in a buoyant, IPX7-rated handheld unit. High-sensitivity multi-constellation GNSS helps maintain a position fix in steep valleys and beneath partial tree cover, while MOB and backtrack functions support rapid return to an access point, casualty location or monitoring station. The bright 3.2-inch sunlight-readable display can show compatible marine charts and user-loaded survey waypoints. In the box: RiverTrack Pro GPS, rechargeable battery pack, USB-C charging/data cable, flotation lanyard, belt clip, screen protector and quick-start guide. Limitation: detailed Australian marine and inland-waterway charts are included only with mapped variants, and the device is a navigation aid rather than a substitute for official charts, local river knowledge or rescue procedures.

options.copy: Measure point velocity in streams, culverts and open channels when rating river gauges or checking discharge after high-flow events. The RiverTrack EM-1 uses a shrouded electromagnetic sensor with no moving parts, making it well suited to shallow, silty and weed-affected Brisbane waterways where propeller meters can foul. Its sunlight-readable handset displays live, minimum, maximum and averaged velocity in m/s, while internal memory stores time-stamped readings for later USB-C export. The IP67 enclosure, glove-friendly controls and graduated 1.5 m sectional wading rod support routine field work and rescue-training site assessments. In the box: EM velocity sensor with selected cable length, handheld display/logger, four-section wading rod, mounting bracket, rechargeable battery, USB-C charging and data cable, calibration certificate, quick-start guide and padded carry case. Limitation: it is intended for wading or fixed-position measurements only and must not be used from a moving boat.

options.copy: Check wort and must sugar levels quickly at home, at the brew shed or between field call-outs. Automatic temperature compensation helps stabilise readings across typical Brisbane brewing conditions, while the rubber-armoured grip and battery-free design suit a hydrology technician accustomed to dependable field instruments. The box includes one calibrated optical refractometer, sampling pipette, calibration screwdriver, lens cloth, protective hard case and quick-start guide. Choose the standard range for most beer and cider recipes or the high-range model for concentrated musts and syrups. Limitation: once fermentation produces alcohol, the raw Brix reading is not a direct final-gravity result and must be entered into a refractometer correction calculator using the original reading.

options.copy: Capture clear spoken audio for river-gauge inspection notes, flood-site briefings and swift-water rescue training videos without running cables to the camera. The compact 2.4 GHz wireless system pairs automatically, while built-in microphones in both the transmitter and receiver can record an instructor and the person behind the camera. options.copy: A compact emergency beacon for offshore crews, solo gauge inspections and rescue trainers working beyond reliable mobile coverage. The buoyant, high-visibility housing is waterproof to 10 m for 1 hour and has a five-year sealed battery designed for at least 24 hours of emergency transmission. Limitation: this is a one-way distress device, not a satellite messenger; it cannot receive replies, and it must be registered with the Australian Maritime Safety Authority before use.

options.copy: Maintain clear sightlines around river gauges, access tracks and training sites without climbing a ladder. The RiverTrack combines a hardened 330 mm pruning blade with a bypass lopper for cutting overhanging branches and storm-damaged growth from the ground. Its oval fibreglass pole resists twisting, while the insulated construction provides added protection when working in wet riparian corridors. A quick-lock telescopic system packs down for transport in a utility vehicle and extends to suit high branches; the high-visibility grip is easy to locate among field gear. Limitation: the pole is not electrically rated and must never be used near powerlines; it is intended for branches up to 30 mm with the lopper or 120 mm with the saw, not heavy felling.

product_00249.name: RiverTrack HX7 Rugged Handheld Marine GPS

options.copy: Built for river-gauge maintenance runs, flood reconnaissance and swift-water rescue training, the RiverTrack HX7 provides reliable position, track and waypoint navigation from a boat, bank or rescue raft. Its sunlight-readable 3.5-inch display, glove-friendly controls and IPX7-rated housing suit Brisbane’s glare, rain and muddy field conditions. Record access points, gauge stations, hazards and search patterns, then transfer GPX files by USB. The unit includes Australian coastal and major inland-water basemaps, a high-sensitivity GNSS receiver, electronic compass, barometric altimeter and man-overboard shortcut. In the box: HX7 handheld GPS, removable rechargeable battery, USB-C charging/data cable, lanyard, belt clip, screen protector and quick-start guide. Limitation: detailed river depths, temporary obstructions and flood-driven channel changes may not appear on the supplied maps, so it must not replace local observations, official warnings or approved rescue procedures.

product_00250.name: RiverTrack Pro Electromagnetic Wading Flow Meter

options.copy: Measure point velocity in rivers, creeks, culverts and open channels without a moving propeller. The RiverTrack Pro uses an electromagnetic sensor suited to routine stream gauging, discharge surveys and training exercises where weeds, silt or low flow can interfere with mechanical meters. Its backlit handheld display shows live velocity, average velocity, sample duration and water temperature, while internal logging stores up to 10,000 readings for USB-C export. The IP68 sensor and graduated sectional wading rod are designed for field deployment in Queensland conditions. In the box: electromagnetic velocity sensor with selected cable length, handheld logger, four-section 1.5 m stainless wading rod, mounting bracket, USB-C data cable, rechargeable battery pack, mains charger, padded carry case, quick-start guide and calibration certificate. Limitation: this meter must remain stationary and fully submerged during sampling; it is not intended for flood measurements from bridges or use in hazardous swift water where wading is unsafe.

product_00257.name: AquaMedic Waterproof Swift-Water Clinical Reference Cards

options.copy: A compact, waterproof clinical reference designed for swift-water rescue trainers, river-gauge crews and first responders working around floods and fast-moving waterways. The colour-coded cards provide quick prompts for primary assessment, drowning response, hypothermia and cold-shock recognition, trauma checks, oxygen guidance, patient monitoring, handover notes and Australian emergency contacts. Rounded corners, high-contrast type and a glove-friendly layout make the set practical beside a river or in a wet training environment. In the box: 24 double-sided synthetic reference cards, a stainless-steel locking ring, detachable lanyard, waterproof field-notes card and fine-tip wet-surface pencil. Limitation: this is a memory aid only, not a substitute for accredited clinical training, current Queensland Ambulance Service protocols, medical direction or local rescue procedures; medication and resuscitation guidance must be checked against the user’s current scope of practice.

options.copy: Keep native revegetation seed dry, organised and ready for field planting in Brisbane’s humid climate. This rugged seed-storage kit suits river-gauge technicians, catchment crews and rescue volunteers carrying grass, sedge and riparian-tree seed between the depot, vehicle and waterside sites. A gasketed outer case helps protect contents from rain, spray and accidental splashes, while individually labelled foil pouches reduce moisture exposure when only one seed lot is needed. The high-visibility case is easy to locate among monitoring or rescue gear. In the box: one impact-resistant storage case, removable compartment tray, resealable foil seed pouches, two rechargeable silica-gel canisters, humidity indicator card, waterproof labels and permanent marker. Limitation: the case is weather-resistant but not certified for prolonged submersion, and stored seed still requires species-appropriate temperature and viability checks.

product_00259.name: RiverTrack M7 Rugged Handheld GNSS Navigator

options.copy: Built for river-gauge rounds, boat-based inspections and swift-water rescue training, the RiverTrack M7 is a waterproof handheld navigator with a sunlight-readable 4-inch display, glove-friendly controls and multi-constellation GNSS positioning. Load marine charts, topographic maps, waypoints, gauge locations and pre-planned access routes, then record tracks for field reports or guide crews back to a launch point after dark. An IPX7 housing, replaceable rechargeable battery and high-visibility casing suit wet subtropical fieldwork around Brisbane’s rivers and estuaries. In the box: RiverTrack M7 navigator, 3200 mAh battery, USB-C charging/data cable, marine cradle, rail mount, wrist lanyard, screen protector and quick-start guide. Limitation: detailed charts are sold separately, and the unit has no built-in sonar or satellite messaging; it should not replace approved charts, local warnings or professional navigation judgement.

product_00260.name: RiverTrack Pro Handheld Current Meter Kit

options.copy: Measure stream velocity and calculate discharge during routine gauging, rating-curve checks and post-flood surveys with the RiverTrack Pro handheld electromagnetic current meter. Its sealed sensor has no moving parts to foul on weeds or fine sediment, while the backlit controller displays live, average, minimum and maximum velocity in metric units. The rugged wading rod features graduated depth markings and quick-adjust sensor positioning for repeatable cross-section measurements. Each kit includes the electromagnetic velocity sensor, selected-length sensor cable, IP67 handheld display, three-section 1.8 m stainless-steel wading rod, rechargeable battery, USB-C charger, lanyard, cleaning brush, calibration certificate and padded hard case. Suitable for freshwater velocities from 0.03 to 5 m/s. Limitation: it is intended for technician-held wading measurements and must not be used from a boat, in unsafe floodwater or as an unattended logging gauge.

options.copy: A reusable polyester support mesh for air-drying waterlogged textiles, field notebooks, fabric maps, rescue-training flags and other flat heritage items after flood or river exposure. The inert, non-rusting mesh allows airflow above and below an object while reducing strain during handling, making it useful for conservation work in Brisbane’s humid conditions or for stabilising wet material brought back from gauge stations. Smooth heat-sealed edges help prevent snagging, and the mesh can be rinsed between recovery jobs. Each box contains one white conservation-grade polyester drying mesh in the selected size, four removable polypropylene corner clips and a printed wet-textile handling guide. The mesh is supplied rolled for transport and will settle flat under light weights. Limitation: it is intended only as a drying support and does not remove mud, salts, mould or chemical contamination; fragile, dyed or historically significant textiles should be assessed by a qualified conservator before cleaning.

options.copy: Brew clean beer, cider or hard ginger in Brisbane’s warm climate with this lightweight pressure-rated fermenter. Pressure fermentation can suppress unwanted esters at moderate ambient temperatures, and the ball-lock posts support oxygen-reducing transfers into a keg. The box includes one PET fermenter vessel, screw-on pressure lid, stainless ball-lock gas and liquid posts, floating dip tube with filter, adjustable pressure-relief valve and gauge, carry harness, stick-on temperature strip, spare seals and cleaning guide. Choose a capacity to match test batches or full keg fills. Limitation: a PET vessel must not be filled with hot wort or scrubbed with abrasive tools, and operating pressure must remain below the marked 2.4-bar limit.

product_00263.name: RiverComms Waterproof Field Audio Recorder Kit

options.copy: Capture clear voice notes, gauge-site observations, incident debriefs and training audio beside rivers without risking a phone. RiverComms combines a compact IP67-rated recorder with a wind-protected lapel microphone, making it practical for hydrology rounds, noisy weir inspections and shore-based swift-water rescue instruction. One-touch recording works with wet or gloved hands, while automatic level control helps balance speech against pumps, wind and flowing water. Time-stamped WAV and MP3 files transfer by USB-C for reports, transcription or subtitle production, and the built-in speaker supports quick checks in the field. In the box: waterproof audio recorder, clip-on omnidirectional microphone, foam and faux-fur windshields, coiled safety tether, mounting clip, USB-C cable, 32 GB microSD card, protective hard case and quick-start guide. Limitation: although the recorder is IP67-rated with its port cover secured, the external microphone and connectors are not submersible and should not be used during in-water rescue drills.

product_00269.name: RiverTrack R7 Rugged Handheld GPS Navigator

options.copy: Built for river-gauge rounds, flood inspections and swift-water rescue training, the RiverTrack R7 is a waterproof handheld navigator that keeps essential waypoints, tracks and bearings close at hand. Its sunlight-readable 7-inch display supports Australian marine charts and user-loaded topographic maps, while glove-friendly controls make it practical in rain, spray and muddy field conditions. Mark gauge stations, boat ramps, hazards and rescue access points, then export recorded tracks for reporting or training review. The rechargeable battery provides up to 14 hours of typical use, and an emergency strobe helps locate the unit after dark. In the box: RiverTrack R7 navigator, Australia coastal-and-inland waterways chart card, rechargeable battery, USB-C charging cable, 12V vessel power lead, RAM-compatible cradle, wrist lanyard and quick-start guide. Limitation: it is a navigation aid only and does not replace official charts, local notices, depth soundings or professional river-condition assessment.

Record gauge locations, mark hazards, follow pre-planned routes and retrace a track when visibility deteriorates. options.copy: Measure point velocity in rivers, creeks, culverts and open channels when checking rating curves, verifying gauge sites or assessing swift-water training locations. Readings are shown in m/s or ft/s, while the marked wading rod helps position the sensor consistently through a vertical. Its rugged cable and high-visibility controls suit routine fieldwork in wet, muddy conditions around South East Queensland. The box includes the handheld display, velocity sensor with selected cable length, three-section 1.5 m graduated wading rod, sensor mounting bracket, four AA batteries, USB data cable, protective carry case and quick-start guide. Limitation: it is intended for wading or bank-side measurements and must not be deployed from a person working in dangerously swift or floodwater conditions.

product_00281.name: RiverSafe Wet Textile Recovery Support Mesh Kit

options.copy: A field-ready conservation kit for lifting, rinsing and drying flood-soaked textiles without placing strain on weakened fibres. Ideal for stabilising water-damaged uniforms, rescue-training flags, equipment bags and community collection fabrics after river flooding or muddy-water exposure. The inert polyester mesh supports an item across its full area while allowing silt and rinse water to drain, and the reusable identification tags help maintain provenance from collection through drying. The box contains one roll of conservation-grade polyester support mesh in the selected width, two smaller mesh cover sheets, 12 archival waterproof ID tags, a graphite marking pencil, 10 soft cotton tying tapes, four nitrile glove pairs and an illustrated flood-recovery guide. The mesh can be washed, air-dried and cut with ordinary shears. Limitation: this is a textile-handling aid only; it is not load-rated, must not be used for swift-water rescue or hauling equipment, and is unsuitable for textiles with active mould until appropriate remediation advice is obtained.

options.copy: Keep beer, cider or ginger beer fermenting steadily through Brisbane’s warm days and cooler nights. A gasketed lid, airlock and bottling tap support clean, low-fuss fermentation, while moulded carry handles help move the vessel safely when full. In the box: one graduated HDPE fermenter, screw lid with silicone seal, three-piece airlock, bung, digital probe thermometer, insulated zip jacket, bottling tap, sediment reducer and cleaning brush. Choose capacity to suit compact test batches or a standard home-brew run. Limitation: the jacket only buffers temperature changes; it does not actively heat or cool, so Brisbane summer brewing may still require a fermentation fridge or ice packs.

options.copy: Capture clear spoken notes at river gauges, site briefings and swift-water rescue training sessions for later transcription, subtitling or incident-review videos. The compact F2-BT records 32-bit float WAV audio, reducing the risk of clipped dialogue when voices suddenly rise, while its locking lavalier connector helps prevent accidental unplugging in the field. Bluetooth control allows basic monitoring and settings changes from a compatible phone, and wireless timecode synchronisation is available with supported external devices. In the box are the F2-BT recorder, LMF-2 omnidirectional lavalier microphone, mic clip, foam windscreen, belt clip, two AAA batteries and a quick-start guide. Its lightweight body slips easily onto a radio harness or shirt pocket. Limitation: the recorder and microphone are not waterproof, so they must be kept in a sealed protective pouch around rain, spray or boat operations.

options.copy: A compact Level 150 inflatable lifejacket for offshore passages, estuary fieldwork and river-gauge servicing from powered boats. A high-visibility bladder, reflective panels, whistle, stainless-steel D-ring and adjustable waist strap support rapid location and recovery in rough water. The low-profile yoke leaves room for rainwear, tool belts and routine movement around gauge structures. In the box: one Riverwatch Pro 150N PFD, fitted 33 g CO₂ cylinder, automatic activation cartridge, whistle, protective storage bag, inspection tag and user guide. One limitation: this inflatable PFD is not suitable for swift-water or whitewater rescue, where impact, debris and immediate buoyancy require a purpose-built foam rescue PFD. The cylinder and activation cartridge must also be replaced after inflation and inspected before each deployment.
