options.copy: Clear overhanging branches around river gauges, access tracks and training sites without hauling a chainsaw into wet, uneven terrain. The Riverbank Pro combines a corrosion-resistant curved pruning blade with a lightweight oval-section fibreglass pole for controlled cutting from the ground. A hooked blade tip helps keep the saw in the kerf, while the lower bark cutter reduces tearing on live limbs. Tool-free lever locks make length changes quick when moving between dense riparian scrub and elevated branches, and high-visibility grips are easy to spot beside muddy water. In the box: one telescopic pole, one 390 mm impulse-hardened saw blade, protective blade scabbard, shoulder carry strap and printed care guide. Choose the reach that suits routine gauge maintenance or broader vegetation work. Limitation: this manual saw is intended for branches up to 120 mm diameter and must not be used near powerlines, from a boat, or while standing in flowing water.

options.copy: Keep river-gauge components, water-sampling kits, rescue PPE and wet field equipment clearly identified while they move between depots, vehicles and worksites. Limitation: the tags are water-resistant but not suitable for permanent underwater identification, and handwritten details may fade after prolonged UV exposure.

product_00287.name: River Rescue Clinical Field Reference – Australia & New Zealand

options.copy: A weather-resistant clinical reference for swift-water rescuers, river-gauge crews and remote field teams working around floods, weirs and fast-moving waterways. The quick-access pages cover primary survey prompts, drowning and aspiration, hypothermia, crush injury, bleeding control, spinal precautions, waterborne exposure, evacuation priorities and concise handover using Australian terminology. High-contrast tables and glove-friendly tabs make key information easier to find beside a river or inside a response vehicle. In the box: one spiral-bound synthetic-paper reference guide, a removable casualty-observation card, a waterproof pencil and a clear zip storage sleeve with attachment loop. Choose the compact pocket edition for a PFD or the larger field edition for a first-aid kit or gauge-service vehicle. Limitation: this is a prompt guide only, not a substitute for accredited clinical or rescue training, local water-authority procedures, medical direction or current ambulance-service protocols.

The gasket-sealed outer case resists rain, mud and brief splashes, while removable amber vials help protect seed from light and allow batches to be separated by species, collection site or season. Limitation: the case is not certified for prolonged submersion, and moisture-sensitive seed may still require refrigerated or controlled-atmosphere storage for long-term viability.

product_00290.name: RiverTrack Vented Water Level & Temperature Logger Kit

options.copy: Designed for river-gauge maintenance, stream surveys and flood-monitoring deployments, the RiverTrack logger records water level and temperature at user-set intervals. Its vented pressure sensor automatically compensates for atmospheric pressure, while the 316 stainless-steel body suits prolonged immersion in fresh water. Connect it to a field laptop to download data, check live readings and export records for rating-curve or hydrograph analysis. The box includes one water-level logger with the selected cable length and measurement range, a desiccant-protected vent tube, USB interface lead, stainless mounting bracket, protective nose cone, configuration software download card and quick-start guide. Limitation: the vent connection and desiccant must remain dry and be inspected regularly; flooding or condensation inside the vent tube can cause inaccurate readings and is not covered as normal sensor drift.

options.copy: Track fermentation gravity and temperature from your phone without repeatedly opening the fermenter—ideal for monitoring a brew around gauge-maintenance shifts or weekend rescue training. The box includes one wireless hydrometer, a fitted long-life battery, calibration tube, protective storage case, quick-start guide and access instructions for the free app. The smooth housing can be sanitised with standard no-rinse brewing sanitiser. Limitation: Bluetooth range is reduced by stainless-steel fermenters, thick fridge walls and distance, so remote checking may require a nearby compatible phone or separate gateway; readings should also be calibrated against a standard hydrometer before first use.

options.copy: Record clear spoken updates at river gauges, rescue-training briefings and field interviews with this compact dual-channel wireless microphone system. Two clip-on transmitters capture separate speakers, while 32-bit float onboard recording provides a safety copy when water noise, radio traffic or sudden level changes overwhelm the camera track. Timecode support helps align audio with video for faster transcription, captioning and incident-review edits. The kit connects to cameras, phones and computers and stores neatly in its charging case between call-outs. In the box: two transmitters with built-in microphones, receiver, smart charging case, two Lavalier II microphones, three furry windshields, two MagClip GO mounts, locking 3.5 mm camera cable, USB-C and Lightning leads, accessory case and quick-start guide. Limitation: the components are not waterproof and require protected placement or a suitable dry bag around spray, rain and swift-water operations.

product_00294.name: Ocean Signal rescueME PLB1 Personal Locator Beacon

options.copy: A compact 406 MHz personal locator beacon for lone river-gauge visits, remote boat access and offshore fieldwork around Brisbane and Moreton Bay. When activated, it sends your registered distress identity and GNSS position through the COSPAS-SARSAT satellite network to search-and-rescue authorities; a 121.5 MHz homing signal and high-intensity strobe assist final location. Its small body clips to a PFD or field vest, while the seven-year battery life suits seldom-used emergency kits. In the box: rescueME PLB1 beacon, flotation pouch, belt clip, lanyard, protective cover, registration guidance and user manual. Australian users must register the beacon with AMSA and keep contact and trip details current. Limitation: the PLB provides no two-way messaging or confirmation that rescuers are coming, and it will not float upright without its supplied pouch; it is an emergency alerting aid, not a substitute for a marine radio, trip plan or swift-water PPE.

options.copy: Trim overhanging branches and woody regrowth around river gauges, access tracks and rescue-training sites without carrying a chainsaw into steep or muddy terrain. The lightweight oval aluminium pole locks securely at multiple lengths, while the 390 mm impulse-hardened curved blade cuts efficiently on the pull stroke. A hooked blade tip helps retain contact with wet limbs and draw down small cut branches; the lower grip remains easy to control when wearing work gloves. In the box: telescopic pole assembly, 390 mm replaceable pruning blade, branch hook, rigid blade scabbard, shoulder carry strap, adjustment tool and care guide. Rinse and dry the blade after use near silty or brackish water. Limitation: the aluminium pole is not electrically insulated and must never be used near overhead powerlines; it is intended for pruning from firm ground, not while wading, climbing or operating from a moving boat.

options.copy: Keep water-sampling coolers, gauge-tool cases, rescue equipment tubs and vehicle first-aid kits visibly secured in transit with RiverTrack single-use cable seals. product_00297.name: Swift-Water Rescue Clinical Reference Card Set

options.copy: A waterproof, field-ready clinical reference designed for swift-water rescue trainers, river-gauge crews and first responders working around floods and waterways. The colour-coded cards provide concise prompts for primary assessment, drowning and aspiration response, hypothermia staging, cold-water shock, trauma checks, spinal precautions, oxygen guidance and structured handover to Queensland Ambulance Service. Large type and wipe-clean synthetic pages make the set practical in rain, spray and muddy conditions. The box contains one spiral-bound reference card set, a detachable casualty-assessment card, a waterproof marker, a retractable lanyard and a protective zip pouch. This is a quick-reference aid only: it does not replace accredited clinical training, current workplace protocols or medical direction, and medication guidance must be checked against local scope-of-practice requirements.

High-visibility latches make it easy to find among monitoring and rescue gear, while adjustable dividers separate species, collection dates or catchment zones. Limitation: the case is splash-resistant rather than certified for prolonged submersion, and it does not replace refrigerated storage for seeds requiring controlled temperature or long-term conservation conditions.

product_00299.name: CurrentPath IPX7 Handheld Marine GPS Navigator

options.copy: Built for river-gauge inspections, small-boat navigation and swift-water rescue training, the CurrentPath handheld navigator provides position, speed, bearing, track logging and waypoint guidance on a sunlight-readable 3.5-inch display. Large glove-friendly buttons and a high-visibility floating housing suit wet launches, muddy banks and fast-moving water, while IPX7 protection handles rain, spray and brief accidental immersion. Load GPX routes, mark gauge sites or rescue access points, and review recorded tracks through the USB-C connection. The replaceable AA battery system is practical for long field shifts where charging is unavailable. In the box are the GPS navigator, removable lanyard, marine mounting cradle, USB-C data cable, two rechargeable AA batteries, quick-start guide and safety information. Limitation: it does not include sonar or live river-depth measurement, so it cannot replace a sounder or site-specific hazard assessment.

product_00300.name: RiverTrack Pro Handheld Electromagnetic Flow Meter

options.copy: Measure stream velocity and verify discharge ratings at river gauges, culverts and flood-warning sites with this portable electromagnetic flow meter. Designed for Australian field conditions, it provides live, minimum, maximum and averaged velocity readings from 0.03 to 5.00 m/s, with no moving impeller to snag on weed or gravel. An IP67 handheld display, backlit screen, rechargeable battery and internal logging for 10,000 readings support routine gauging runs and training-site assessments. The kit includes the velocity sensor, graduated telescopic wading rod, display unit, sensor cable, USB-C charging lead, mains adaptor, lanyard, calibration certificate, quick-start guide and padded hard carry case. Select the rod and cable length to suit shallow creeks or larger channels. Limitation: the sensor must remain fully submerged and correctly aligned with the current, so it is not intended for unattended deployment or use by a wading operator in unsafe flood flows.

options.copy: A compact 406 MHz personal locator beacon for technicians, boat crews and rescue trainers working around remote rivers, estuaries and offshore waters. The buoyant, waterproof housing clips to a lifejacket or field vest, making it practical for isolated gauge inspections, flood deployments and small-craft trips from Brisbane. The box contains one GPS personal locator beacon with sealed long-life battery, flotation pouch, belt clip, wrist lanyard, reflective ID labels, registration instructions and user guide. Limitation: this PLB must be activated by hand and is intended for personal carriage; it does not replace a vessel EPIRB where maritime regulations require one.

options.copy: Built for clearing woody growth around river gauges, access tracks and rescue-training sites, the RiverReach pruning saw combines an aggressive curved blade with a secure, wet-weather grip. Triple-ground teeth cut efficiently on both green and seasoned branches, while the hard-chromed steel blade resists sap and corrosion in humid Brisbane conditions. A high-visibility handle makes the saw easier to locate among riparian vegetation, and the locking sheath can be mounted on a work belt or arborist harness for hands-free movement along steep banks. Rinse and dry the tool after exposure to muddy or brackish water. Limitation: this is a hand-pruning tool for branches within safe reach; it is not electrically insulated, suitable for felling large trees, or rated as load-bearing swift-water rescue equipment.

product_00306.name: RiverTrack Waterproof Equipment Transfer Labels – 100 Pack

options.copy: Keep river-gauge components, sampling cases and swift-water rescue gear identifiable while they move between depots, vehicles and field sites. RiverTrack transfer labels use a waterproof synthetic face stock with permanent acrylic adhesive, allowing technicians to record asset IDs, destinations, inspection dates and handling notes in pencil, ballpoint pen or permanent marker. A high-visibility border makes labelled cases easier to sort in wet, low-light loading areas, while the split backing supports quick application with gloved hands. Each box contains 100 pre-cut labels, a fine-tip permanent marker and an application guide. Choose the label size and colour that best suits small instrument cases, larger transport tubs or urgent quarantine loads. Apply only to clean, dry, smooth surfaces and press firmly around the edges. Limitation: the labels are water-resistant but are not intended for prolonged submersion or reliable adhesion to muddy, oily, textured or flexible fabric surfaces.

product_00307.name: River Rescue Clinical Reference – Waterproof Field Cards

options.copy: A rugged quick-reference set for first-aid assessment during river-gauge fieldwork, flood response and swift-water rescue training. The colour-coded cards summarise primary survey steps, drowning and aspiration care, hypothermia staging, cold-water shock, trauma checks, spinal precautions, heat illness, envenomation guidance and structured handover prompts, with Australian emergency numbers and metric observations. Printed on tear-resistant, waterproof stock, the cards can be wiped clean after muddy or wet deployments and include large type for use in poor weather. In the box: one selected-size reference card set, a stainless-steel binder ring, a detachable high-visibility lanyard, a fine-tip wet-surface pencil and a protective zip pouch. This is an aide-memoire only; it does not replace accredited clinical training, local water-authority procedures, medical direction or current Queensland Ambulance Service guidance.

product_00308.name: Riverbank Seed Vault Waterproof Storage Case

options.copy: Keep native grass, sedge and riparian revegetation seed organised between field surveys, flood-response callouts and weekend planting days. Designed for humid subtropical conditions and transport in a work ute, this rugged seed-storage case uses a gasketed lid, locking latches and removable dividers to protect labelled packets from rain, splashes, dust and accidental mixing. A pressure-equalisation valve assists when moving between elevations, while the carry handle makes it easy to take restoration seed to remote gauge sites. In the box: one impact-resistant storage case, adjustable compartment dividers, 24 reusable paper seed envelopes, 24 write-on labels, two silica-gel desiccant canisters and a humidity indicator card. Limitation: the case is weatherproof rather than suitable for prolonged submersion, and seeds must be properly dried before storage because the case does not provide refrigeration or active humidity control.

product_00309.name: RiverTrack HX7 Rugged Handheld Marine GPS

options.copy: Built for river-gauge runs, flood-response boats and swift-water rescue training, the RiverTrack HX7 provides glove-friendly GPS navigation in a buoyant, IPX7-rated handheld unit. Its high-contrast 7-inch display shows marine charts, waypoints, tracks, speed and position, while the preloaded Australia and New Zealand coastal and inland-water map pack helps crews navigate unfamiliar reaches around South East Queensland. Record access points, gauge stations, hazards and training routes, then export data by USB-C or microSD. The rechargeable battery supports up to 16 hours of typical use, and a replaceable AA battery tray provides field backup. In the box are the HX7 GPS, regional map card, USB-C charging cable, AA battery tray, wrist lanyard, protective cradle, quick-start guide and mounting hardware. Limitation: it has no built-in sonar and should not replace official charts, local notices or on-water hazard assessment.

product_00310.name: RiverTrack Vented Water-Level Logger Field Kit

options.copy: Monitor river stage, gauge-pool fluctuations and flood-event hydrographs with this rugged vented pressure water-level logger. Designed for routine hydrology fieldwork around Brisbane waterways, it records water level and temperature at user-set intervals, while the vented cable automatically compensates for atmospheric pressure. An IP68 stainless-steel body, replaceable desiccant and USB configuration interface suit repeated deployment in stilling wells, culverts and secured stream installations. The box includes one data logger with selected cable length, vented reference tube, desiccant cartridge, stainless mounting clamp, USB download/configuration lead, protective transport case and quick-start guide. Compatible desktop software is available as a free download. Limitation: this model has no built-in cellular or satellite telemetry, so readings must be collected on site via USB.

product_00312.name: RiverTrack IP67 Brewing pH Meter Kit

options.copy: Built for brewers who appreciate field-grade measurements, the RiverTrack IP67 Brewing pH Meter checks mash, wort, kombucha and ferment acidity from pH 0.00–14.00. Its high-contrast backlit display, automatic temperature compensation and buoyant safety-orange body are easy to handle beside a steaming kettle or in a busy Brisbane brew shed. The replaceable spear-tip electrode reaches into small samples, while two-point calibration helps deliver repeatable readings when refining recipes or diagnosing a sluggish ferment. In the box: waterproof digital pH meter, replaceable electrode, protective cap, lanyard, pH 4.00 and 7.00 calibration sachets, electrode storage solution, sample cup, cleaning brush, AAA batteries and a padded carry case. Limitation: the probe must be rinsed and stored wet in electrode solution; it should not be left in hot wort above 60°C or used without cooling the sample first.

A bypass lopper operated by a pull rope handles smaller shoots, and tool-free extension locks make the saw practical to carry between remote monitoring sites or use during rescue-training site preparation. In the box: telescopic fibreglass pole, detachable 330 mm pruning-saw head, bypass-lopper head, pull rope, blade guard, shoulder carry strap and care guide. Choose the reach suited to your vehicle and work area. Limitation: the pole is not electrically certified or waterproof; never use it near powerlines, from a boat, in flowing water, or on branches exceeding the stated 32 mm lopper capacity.

product_00317.name: River Rescue Clinical Reference Field Cards

options.copy: A waterproof clinical quick-reference set for swift-water rescue training, river-gauge fieldwork and first-response support in wet environments. The colour-coded cards summarise primary assessment, drowning and hypothermia considerations, oxygen and AED prompts, spinal precautions, patient observations, handover structure and Australian emergency contact guidance. High-contrast print, rounded corners and a glove-friendly layout make key information easy to scan beside rivers or during training scenarios. In the box: 18 double-sided synthetic reference cards, a stainless-steel locking ring, breakaway lanyard, protective storage sleeve, fine-tip wet-surface pencil and alcohol wipe for removing field notes. Choose Pocket size for a PFD pocket or A5 for vehicle and training-kit use. Limitation: this is a reference aid only and does not replace accredited clinical training, current Queensland Ambulance Service guidance, local rescue procedures or direction from qualified medical personnel.

options.copy: A rugged, water-resistant seed storage case for keeping native riparian, wetland and garden seed packets organised between nursery work, river-gauge visits and weekend restoration projects. The gasketed hard shell helps protect contents from Brisbane humidity, spray, mud and brief accidental immersion, while removable dividers separate seed lots by catchment, species or sowing date. Each box includes one impact-resistant storage case, six adjustable dividers, 24 write-on seed envelopes, 24 waterproof lot labels, two silica-gel desiccant canisters and a humidity indicator card. A pressure-release latch and carry handle make it practical for transport in a field vehicle or rescue-equipment trailer. Limitation: the case is not intended for prolonged submersion, and moisture-sensitive seeds still require correct drying and temperature-controlled storage for long-term viability.

product_00319.name: RiverTrack M7 Rugged Handheld Marine GPS

options.copy: Built for river-gauge inspections, flood-response boats and swift-water rescue training, the RiverTrack M7 provides reliable position, speed, heading and track-back guidance in a buoyant, IPX7-rated handheld unit. Its glove-friendly controls, sunlight-readable 3.2-inch display and high-sensitivity multi-GNSS receiver suit Brisbane’s tidal reaches, mangrove-lined channels and remote catchments. Load compatible marine charts, mark gauge sites and hazards, record survey tracks, or share GPX waypoints with field teams. The replaceable battery delivers up to 18 hours of typical navigation, while a dedicated man-overboard key quickly creates a return point. In the box are the M7 GPS, preloaded Australia and New Zealand basemap, rechargeable battery pack, USB-C cable, wrist lanyard, belt clip and quick-start guide. Limitation: the basemap is for general orientation only; detailed charts are sold separately, and the unit must not replace official charts, local notices or safe visual navigation.

product_00320.name: RiverTrack Pro Electromagnetic Stream Flow Meter

options.copy: Measure point velocity in rivers, creeks and open channels without moving propellers. The RiverTrack Pro uses an electromagnetic sensor suited to routine gauge inspections, discharge measurements and training exercises where silt, weeds or low flow can hinder mechanical meters. A backlit, weather-resistant handheld display shows live velocity, average velocity, minimum and maximum readings, while internal logging stores survey points for later USB-C export. The wading rod has graduated depth markings and separates into sections for transport between remote sites. In the box: electromagnetic velocity sensor with 3 m cable, handheld display/logger, sectional 1.5 m stainless-steel wading rod, USB-C data cable, rechargeable battery pack, mains charger with Australian plug, protective carry case, wrist strap and quick-start guide. Limitation: intended for wading or fixed-position measurements only; it is not rated for use from a moving boat or by personnel entering swift water above approved wading limits.

product_00321.name: RiverSafe Archival Textile Drying Screen Kit

options.copy: A modular drying screen for supporting wet-cleaned, flood-affected or freshly rinsed textiles while air circulates above and below the fibres. It is particularly useful for drying gauge-station flags, fabric instrument cases, rescue-training bibs and small heritage textiles without hanging, stretching or transferring rust. The inert polyester mesh is tensioned over a lightweight polypropylene frame, with rounded corners that will not snag delicate cloth. In the box: one snap-together frame, one removable conservation-grade polyester mesh panel, four non-slip feet, eight reusable edge clips and a storage sleeve. Components rinse clean after contact with river silt, and the screen can be raised over a tray to collect drips in humid Brisbane conditions. Limitation: it is intended for flat, supported drying only and is not suitable for bearing heavy saturated items such as ropes, PFDs or weighted canvas; fragile or dyed textiles should first be assessed for colourfastness.

options.copy: Brew compact beer, cider or ginger beer batches in a rugged vessel that suits busy weeks on the road and limited storage at home. The wide-mouth 304 stainless-steel keg is easy to carry, resists knocks better than glass and blocks sunlight during fermentation, while etched internal volume marks help with filling. A pressure-capable lid lets you ferment, carbonate and serve from the same vessel, reducing transfers and cleaning after long gauge-maintenance shifts or weekend rescue training. The box includes one stainless fermenter, screw-on pressure lid, adjustable spunding valve with gauge, floating dip tube, liquid and gas ball-lock posts, silicone seal, carry handle and cleaning brush. Choose a capacity for trial recipes or a full home batch. Limitation: the fermenter is rated to a maximum working pressure of 15 psi, so it is not suitable for high-pressure carbonation.

product_00323.name: FieldVoice IP67 Wireless Lavalier Microphone Kit

options.copy: Capture clear spoken notes, river-gauge maintenance reports and swift-water rescue training audio without holding a microphone. The compact 2.4 GHz system includes two IP67-rated clip-on transmitters, allowing an instructor and trainee to be recorded separately, plus automatic gain control and a low-cut mode to reduce wind and engine rumble. Time-stamped recordings can be transferred for transcription or used to create accurate subtitles for training videos. Each transmitter also records a local backup to internal memory, useful when radio interference affects the camera feed. In the box: two transmitters with built-in microphones, dual-channel receiver, USB-C and 3.5 mm camera cables, USB-C phone adaptor, two furry windshields, magnetic clips, charging case, lanyard, USB-C charging cable and hard carry pouch. Limitation: although the transmitters resist rain and brief immersion, the receiver and charging case are not waterproof and must remain protected in wet field conditions.

options.copy: A compact emergency beacon for technicians, boat crews and swift-water trainers working beyond reliable mobile coverage. When activated, it transmits a 406 MHz distress alert and encoded GPS position through the international Cospas-Sarsat satellite network, while a 121.5 MHz homing signal and high-intensity strobe assist search teams during the final approach. The buoyant, high-visibility housing clips to a PFD or equipment harness and is suited to remote gauge inspections, coastal passages and offshore response exercises. The box contains one GPS personal locator beacon with sealed battery, flotation pouch, PFD attachment clip, lanyard, self-test instructions and Australian registration guide. Registration with the Australian Maritime Safety Authority is free and essential before use. Limitation: this PLB does not replace an EPIRB required for a vessel, is not designed to activate automatically, and must be held with its antenna upright and a clear view of the sky for best performance.

A lightweight pruning head and secure cam locks make it practical for repeated field stops around Brisbane’s creeks and riverbanks. NFC connectivity lets you review beacon status and self-test history on a compatible phone. The box includes one PLB3 beacon with sealed battery, multifunction belt/PFD mounting clip, securing lanyard, NFC quick-start guide and Australian registration instructions. The battery has a five-year standby life and is replaceable by an authorised service centre. Limitation: this beacon does not replace a lifejacket, EPIRB or appropriate communications equipment, and it must be manually activated with its antenna clear of obstructions for best performance.

Dedicated buttons remain practical with wet or gloved hands, while tide tables, anchor-drift alarms, compass, barometric altimeter and Australian coastal basemap support work from Brisbane waterways to remote catchments. It runs for up to 18 hours on two replaceable AA batteries and accepts a microSD card for compatible detailed charts. In the box: RiverTrack M7 navigator, wrist lanyard, marine mounting cradle, USB-C data cable, two alkaline AA batteries, quick-start guide and safety leaflet. Limitation: detailed inland-waterway and premium marine charts are not included and must be purchased separately.

product_00340.name: CurrentTrack Pro Handheld River Flow Meter

options.copy: Measure point velocity in streams, channels and around gauging stations with this portable electromagnetic flow meter, designed for discharge surveys, rating-curve checks and swift-water training site assessments. The sealed sensor provides real-time, average, minimum and maximum velocity readings from 0.03 to 5.0 m/s, while the backlit handheld display remains easy to read in rain and low light. A telescopic graduated wading rod helps maintain repeatable sensor depth, and internal logging stores up to 10,000 timestamped measurements for USB export. The box includes the flow sensor and cable, IP67 display unit, telescopic wading rod in the selected length, mounting bracket, USB cable, rechargeable battery pack, mains charger, protective carry case and quick-start guide. Limitation: the sensor requires full submersion and stable positioning, so it is not suitable for measurements in highly aerated water, heavy debris or conditions unsafe for wading.

options.copy: A conservation-grade screening tool for controlled, low-suction vacuum cleaning of textiles affected by dry dust and river silt. It helps protect fibres, stitching and loose insignia while cleaning archived field uniforms, swift-water rescue training flags, fabric equipment labels and other flat textile items. The smooth polyester mesh provides a barrier between the vacuum nozzle and the object, while the soft fabric-bound edge reduces snagging during work at the bench or gauge depot. The box contains one washable polyester mesh screen in the selected size, one adjustable micro-vacuum nozzle adapter, two spare edge-binding strips, a resealable storage sleeve and a cleaning guide. Use only after deposits are fully dry and with a HEPA vacuum set to low suction. Limitation: this screen is not intended for wet cleaning, mould remediation, hazardous flood-contaminated PPE or textiles with actively flaking surfaces unless supervised by a qualified conservator.

options.copy: A rugged, portable optical refractometer for quickly checking wort sugar concentration and tracking fermentation in beer, cider, mead and ginger beer. It needs only a few drops, making it handy for small batches or for taking readings without carrying a fragile hydrometer and full test jar. Automatic temperature compensation helps stabilise readings from 10–30°C, while the dual scale displays both Brix and estimated specific gravity. The water-resistant, rubber-armoured body is easy to grip with wet hands and packs neatly into a field bag. In the box: refractometer, hard storage case, calibration screwdriver, sample pipette, lens cloth, distilled-water calibration vial and quick-reference guide. Limitation: once alcohol is present, the specific-gravity scale is not directly accurate; use the Brix reading with a fermentation correction calculator for reliable results.

options.copy: Capture clear spoken notes, river-gauge maintenance reports, training demonstrations and on-camera interviews without running cables across a boat ramp or rescue staging area. The dual-channel wireless system records two presenters at once, while onboard 32-bit float backup recording helps recover speech affected by sudden level changes, wind gusts or clipped camera audio. Timecode support simplifies syncing footage for captioning and incident-review videos, and the included lavaliers can be secured beneath high-visibility clothing. In the box are two transmitters, one receiver, two Lavalier II microphones, a smart charging case, three furry windshields, magnetic clips, locking 3.5 mm cables, USB-C cables, an accessory case and mounting hardware. Limitation: the components are not waterproof or immersion-rated, so they must remain in a sealed pouch or protected position around spray, rain and swift-water exercises.

options.copy: A compact personal AIS beacon for offshore fieldwork, vessel transfers and rescue-training operations around Brisbane waterways. Clip it to a compatible inflatable lifejacket; when activated, it transmits an AIS man-overboard alert and GPS position to nearby AIS-equipped vessels, while its flashing light aids visual location after dark. The integrated activation tape can be arranged for automatic deployment as the lifejacket inflates, with manual activation also available. Its sealed, waterproof body is suited to spray, rain and repeated work around river gauges or patrol boats. In the box: rescueME MOB1 beacon with battery, mounting clip, lifejacket activation tape, oral-tube bracket, programming/test accessories and user guide. Limitation: this is a short-range AIS locating aid, not a substitute for a registered 406 MHz PLB or EPIRB; alert reception depends on nearby vessels having operational AIS equipment, and professional installation may be needed for some lifejackets.

product_00357.name: Swift-Water Medical Response Waterproof Field Guide

options.copy: A durable clinical quick-reference guide for rescue trainers, gauge crews and first responders working around rivers, floods and remote waterways. Its colour-coded algorithms cover scene safety, drowning resuscitation, hypothermia, cold-water shock, aspiration, trauma assessment, spinal precautions, bleeding control, patient monitoring and structured handover. Tables include adult and paediatric observations, Glasgow Coma Scale prompts and temperature conversion, while waterproof synthetic pages can be wiped clean after muddy field use. The pocket format attaches to a PFD or response pack; the larger format suits vehicle kits and training sessions. In the box: one spiral-bound waterproof guide, a detachable triage card, a permanent fine-tip marker and a locking gear clip. Limitation: this is an aide-memoire only and does not replace accredited clinical training, local Queensland Ambulance Service protocols, medical direction or professional judgement.

product_00359.name: Garmin GPSMAP 79s Rugged Floating Handheld Navigator

options.copy: Built for river-gauge servicing, flood-response work and swift-water rescue training, the GPSMAP 79s provides reliable handheld navigation from a high-sensitivity, multi-band GNSS receiver. Its sunlight-readable 3-inch colour display, physical buttons and buoyant, IPX7-rated housing suit wet gloves, spray and accidental drops into the water. Record gauge locations, navigate to remote access points, follow pre-planned routes and share waypoints with compatible Garmin equipment. It includes a worldwide basemap, 8 GB of memory, a three-axis electronic compass, barometric altimeter and support for downloadable marine and topographic mapping. Two replaceable AA batteries provide up to 19 hours of operation in GPS mode, making field swaps simple. In the box are the GPSMAP 79s handheld, wrist lanyard, USB cable and documentation; AA batteries and detailed Australian charts are not included. Limitation: this unit is a navigation aid only and cannot replace approved charts, local river knowledge or operational rescue procedures.

options.copy: A compact personal man-overboard beacon designed for offshore crews, river-gauge technicians and rescue trainers working around fast or open water. When manually activated, it transmits an AIS distress message and live GPS position to compatible chartplotters and radios nearby, while a high-intensity white strobe helps rescuers locate the wearer after dark or in poor visibility. Its waterproof, high-visibility housing clips to a PFD shoulder strap and can be operated with gloved hands. In the box: AIS MOB beacon, PFD mounting clip, activation pull-cord, protective cover, self-test guide and user manual. The sealed battery provides up to 24 hours of transmission and has a seven-year replacement interval. Limitation: this short-range AIS device depends on nearby AIS-equipped vessels or stations receiving its signal; it does not contact satellites or replace a registered 406 MHz personal locator beacon for remote-area emergencies.

options.copy: Maintain access around river gauges, monitoring stations and rescue-training sites without climbing into unstable trees or working from a ladder. The RiverReach pole saw uses a lightweight fibreglass telescopic shaft for pruning small overhanging branches from firm ground, with a hooked 330 mm impulse-hardened blade that helps retain wet or flexible limbs during the cut. Its collapsed length fits readily in a field vehicle, while the high-visibility grip and corrosion-resistant fittings suit humid Brisbane conditions and work near waterways. In the box: one telescopic fibreglass pole, one 330 mm curved pruning blade, blade cover, branch-pulling hook, shoulder carry strap, adjustment tool and user guide. Limitation: the pole is non-conductive but is not certified for live electrical work; keep well clear of powerlines, and do not use it while standing in flowing water, from a boat or on unstable banks.

options.copy: Keep river-gauge cases, telemetry batteries, sampling kits, throw bags and rescue-training equipment clearly identified while they move between depots, field vehicles and wet sites. These tear-resistant synthetic tags accept permanent marker and feature a write-on panel for asset ID, destination, inspection date, fault status or return instructions. A reinforced eyelet and supplied cable tie allow each tag to attach securely to handles, crates, dry bags and coiled rope without relying on adhesive. Bright colour coding helps separate serviceable gear, quarantined equipment and items awaiting transport, even in a crowded ute tray. Each box contains waterproof tags in the selected colour and size, matching UV-stabilised cable ties, and a fine-tip permanent marker. The tags tolerate rain, splashes and short-term outdoor exposure, but they are not certified for permanent submersion and should not be used as life-safety inspection records or lifting tags.

options.copy: A waterproof, field-ready clinical reference designed for swift-water rescue trainers, river-gauge crews and first responders working around Brisbane’s rivers and flood-prone catchments. The quick-reference cards cover drowning resuscitation, hypothermia, cold-water shock, trauma assessment, spinal precautions, oxygen guidance, casualty monitoring and handover prompts, with high-contrast flowcharts that can be read in rain or low light. The set also includes Australian emergency numbers, vital-sign ranges and a waterproof notes panel for a grease pencil. In the box: one spiral-bound reference card set, a removable lanyard, a mini grease pencil and a protective zip pouch with belt loop. Choose a pocket or A5 format to suit a PFD pocket, response pack or training kit. Limitation: this is an aide-memoire for trained personnel and does not replace accredited clinical training, local water-authority procedures, Queensland Ambulance Service guidance or medical direction.

options.copy: Keep native revegetation seed dry, sorted and ready for fieldwork with this rugged seed-storage vault, designed for humid subtropical sheds, ute trays and days spent around river gauges. A gasketed, impact-resistant case protects individual seed lots from rain, mud and accidental splashes, while removable dividers make it easy to separate riparian grasses, sedges, shrubs and training-site restoration seed. The clear-lid containers accept handwritten labels for species, collection location and date, and included silica packs help control residual humidity. In the box: one latching waterproof outer case, twelve clear screw-cap seed jars, adjustable dividers, twenty-four write-on labels, two permanent markers and six rechargeable silica-gel sachets with indicator beads. Limitation: the case is splashproof and suitable for brief accidental immersion only; it is not certified for prolonged submersion, and seed must be properly dried before storage to prevent mould.

product_00369.name: RiverTrack Pro 7 Rugged Handheld Marine GPS

options.copy: Built for river-gauge rounds, flood-response boats and swift-water rescue training, the RiverTrack Pro 7 provides reliable position, track and waypoint navigation in a waterproof, glove-friendly handheld. Multi-band GPS, Galileo and QZSS reception helps maintain a fix near steep banks and bridges, while dedicated mark, man-overboard and backtrack keys allow fast operation in rain or spray. The sunlight-readable colour display shows marine charts, speed, bearing, distance, tide data and custom gauge-site waypoints. Bluetooth sync exports tracks and coordinates to a phone, and the rechargeable battery delivers up to 24 hours of normal tracking. In the box: RiverTrack Pro 7 GPS, Australia and New Zealand coastal basemap, USB-C charging cable, removable lithium battery, wrist lanyard, belt clip, screen protector and quick-start guide. Limitation: it is IPX7 waterproof but does not float, and inland depth or hazard detail depends on separately sourced compatible charts.
options.label: 16 GB

product_00370.name: RiverTrack Pro Handheld Water Velocity Meter

options.copy: Measure stream velocity and calculate discharge during river-gauge inspections, rating-curve checks and swift-water rescue training. The compact, waterproof meter uses a low-friction impeller sensor to display instantaneous, average and maximum velocity from 0.03 to 7.5 m/s, with selectable metric units and USB-C data export. A telescopic wading rod marked in 10 mm increments helps record depth at each measurement vertical, while the backlit screen remains readable in rain and low light. In the box: IP67 display unit, impeller probe, selected-length sensor cable, 1.5–4.5 m telescopic wading rod, USB-C charging/data lead, spare rotor, wrist lanyard, protective hard case and quick-start guide. Limitation: this contact meter requires safe physical access to the measurement point and is not suitable for use from a bridge, in flood flows beyond approved wading limits, or where debris may foul the impeller.

options.copy: A field-ready drying and support system for stabilising waterlogged uniforms, fabric equipment, flags, sample bags and other valued textiles after flood, river or storm exposure. The inert polyester mesh allows airflow while supporting weakened fibres, making it practical for a gauge-station store, rescue-training facility or conservation workroom. Mesh sheets can be layered with absorbent blotter to move damp textiles without stretching and to separate items during controlled air-drying. The box contains 6 washable polyester mesh sheets, 12 acid-free blotting sheets, 10 unbleached cotton support strips, 20 archival waterproof identification tags, a graphite marking pencil, nitrile gloves and a step-by-step wet-textile triage guide. Supplied in a reusable polypropylene field case. Limitation: this kit is intended for initial stabilisation and air-drying only; it does not disinfect sewage-contaminated material or replace professional treatment for historic, dyed or structurally fragile textiles.

options.copy: Monitor fermentation temperatures from the shed, garage or field with the RiverTrack Rugged Fermentation Temperature Logger. Designed for brewers who need dependable records rather than constant visual checks, it logs temperature at selectable intervals and helps identify heat spikes that can affect beer, cider, mead or kombucha. Its splash-resistant housing, large display and glove-friendly buttons suit Brisbane conditions and users accustomed to working around wet equipment. Attach the food-safe stainless-steel probe to the outside of a fermenter under insulation, or insert it through a compatible thermowell for closer readings. The box includes one digital logger, stainless-steel probe with 2 m cable, elastic fermenter strap, adhesive insulation pad, USB-C cable and quick-start guide. Logged data exports as a CSV file for batch notes. Limitation: the unit is splash-resistant, not submersible, and it does not actively heat or cool the fermenter.
options.label: 16,000-Reading Memory

product_00373.name: RØDE Wireless PRO Field Audio & Captioning Kit

options.copy: Capture clear spoken audio for river-gauge reports, flood-site interviews and swift-water rescue training videos with this compact dual-channel wireless microphone kit. Two clip-on transmitters record presenters or instructors simultaneously, while 32-bit float onboard backup recording helps recover dialogue when water, wind or sudden shouts cause level changes. Timecode support simplifies syncing audio for accurate subtitles and incident-video transcripts. The kit includes two transmitters with built-in microphones, a camera-mount receiver, two Lavalier II microphones, three furry windshields, magnetic and clip mounts, locking 3.5 mm cable, USB-C and Lightning phone cables, USB-C charging hub, accessory pouch and rigid carry case. Compatible with cameras, computers and mobile devices. Limitation: the components are not waterproof and must remain in a sealed pouch or dry location during rain, spray and boat operations.

options.copy: A compact emergency beacon for offshore passages, remote river-gauge inspections and swift-water rescue operations where a mobile signal cannot be relied upon. When activated, it transmits a 406 MHz distress alert with GNSS position to the satellite search-and-rescue network, while AIS and 121.5 MHz homing signals help nearby equipped vessels and rescue teams locate the wearer. The buoyant, high-visibility housing is waterproof and can be clipped to a PFD or equipment harness for rapid access. In the box: RiverTrack personal locator beacon with sealed long-life battery, PFD mounting clip, adjustable retention lanyard, protective storage pouch, self-test guide and Australian registration instructions. Limitation: this is a manually activated distress device and does not replace an EPIRB required for some vessels; it must be registered to the owner, and AIS alerts are visible only to nearby compatible receivers.

product_00379.name: Rivermark R7 Floating Handheld GPS Navigator

options.copy: Built for river-gauge rounds, boat-based inspections and swift-water rescue training, the Rivermark R7 provides glove-friendly GPS navigation without relying on mobile reception. Its high-visibility, buoyant housing is IPX7 waterproof, while physical buttons remain practical in rain, spray and muddy field conditions. Record waypoints for gauge stations, ramps, hazards and training sites, follow GPX routes, review breadcrumb tracks and use the compass and barometric altimeter when working along unfamiliar reaches. The sunlight-readable 3.2-inch display supports compatible Australian marine and topographic map files stored internally or on a microSD card. In the box are the R7 navigator, rechargeable battery pack, USB-C charging cable, wrist lanyard, belt clip, screen protector and quick-start guide. Limitation: detailed charts and topographic maps are not included and must be purchased or loaded separately; the unit is not a substitute for approved emergency communications equipment.

options.copy: Measure stream velocity and estimate discharge during routine gauging, post-rain inspections and swift-water rescue training site assessments. The RiverTrack Pro uses a compact acoustic sensor to display live, average, minimum and maximum water velocity, while the rugged IP67 handset stores timestamped readings for later transfer to a field laptop. Its sectional wading rod has graduated depth markings, making it practical for mid-section velocity measurements in creeks, channels and accessible river reaches. In the box: acoustic velocity sensor, IP67 handheld display/logger, graduated sectional wading rod, sensor mounting bracket, 3 m sensor cable, USB-C data cable, rechargeable battery, mains charger with Australian plug, protective carry case, wrist lanyard and quick-start guide. Limitation: acoustic measurements can become unreliable in highly aerated, debris-laden or extremely shallow water, and the instrument is not intended for use while wading in unsafe flood flows.

Its high-contrast 3-inch colour display, physical buttons and water-resistant, floating housing suit wet gloves, spray and accidental drops overboard. Multi-band GNSS support improves positioning near steep banks and tree cover, while saved waypoints, tracks, routes, compass and barometric altimeter help crews mark gauges, boat ramps, hazards and rendezvous locations. Wireless connectivity allows compatible Garmin devices and phones to exchange data. In the box: GPSMAP 79s handheld navigator, preloaded worldwide basemap, USB cable, wrist lanyard and documentation. Limitation: detailed Australian marine or topographic charts are not included and may require a separately purchased compatible map or subscription; it should not replace official charts, local warnings or rescue navigation procedures.

product_00390.name: RiverTrack Pro Portable Water Velocity Meter

options.copy: Measure stream velocity and calculate discharge during river-gauge maintenance, rating-curve checks and post-flood inspections. The RiverTrack Pro uses a rugged, low-drag impeller sensor with a telescopic wading rod, while the backlit handheld display records average, minimum and maximum velocity in m/s. Its IP67 housing, high-visibility controls and glove-friendly interface suit wet subtropical fieldwork around Brisbane, and stored readings can be exported by USB for station reports and training exercises. The box includes the velocity sensor, graduated telescopic wading rod, 5 m sensor cable, handheld display/logger, USB data cable, rechargeable battery, mains charger with Australian plug, spare impeller, tool kit, wrist lanyard, quick-start guide and hard carry case. Limitation: the impeller requires a minimum water depth of 60 mm and may give unreliable readings in heavily weeded water, dense debris or highly aerated swift-water conditions.

product_00391.name: RiverSafe Undyed Polyester Conservation Support Net

options.copy: A soft, conservation-grade polyester net for stabilising torn, fraying or flood-damaged textiles during inspection, drying, storage and display. Its fine open structure permits airflow and allows loose fibres to be secured with conservation stitching, making it practical for historic water-authority field bags, gauge-station flags, training banners, uniforms and other fabric items exposed to Brisbane’s humid conditions. The net is undyed, low-lint and chemically stable, and can be cut to shape without adding excessive bulk. Each box contains one folded sheet of polyester support net in the selected size, ten stainless-steel entomology pins for temporary positioning, a spool of neutral polyester conservation thread and an illustrated handling guide. Limitation: this material is intended only for textile conservation support; it is not load-bearing and must never be used to repair rescue PPE, throw bags, harnesses, ropes or any item relied upon for swift-water safety.

options.copy: Brew clean beer, cider or hard ginger beer around an irregular field roster with the RiverRun Pressure Fermenter Kit. Its clear, impact-resistant PET vessel lets you check fermentation at a glance, while the pressure-rated lid supports closed transfers that reduce oxygen exposure when moving a batch into a keg. The compact design is easy to carry, clean and store in a Brisbane garage or utility room after long days servicing river gauges or weekend rescue training. In the box: one pressure-rated PET fermenter, screw-on lid, adjustable pressure-relief valve, pressure gauge, floating dip tube with filter, liquid and gas ball-lock posts, collection bottle, stick-on temperature strip, seals and a cleaning brush. Choose a working capacity to suit small trial batches or a full keg fill. Limitation: this kit does not include a CO2 cylinder, regulator, keg or temperature-control system, and the vessel must not be exposed to liquids above 50°C.

product_00393.name: RØDE Wireless PRO Field Interview & Training Audio Kit

options.copy: Capture clear speech for river-gauge field reports, incident debriefs, rescue-training videos and accurately timed subtitles with this compact dual-channel wireless microphone system. Each transmitter provides 32-bit float onboard recording for recovering unexpectedly loud or quiet dialogue, while timecode support helps synchronise audio with compatible cameras and editing software. The weather-resistant carry case keeps the kit organised between vehicle runs, although the components are not waterproof and must be protected from rain, spray and immersion during river work. In the box: two wireless transmitters, one dual-channel receiver, two Lavalier II microphones, three furry windshields, two magnetic clips, three locking 3.5 mm cables, USB-C and Lightning connection leads, accessory pouch, smart charging case and SC22 USB-C cable. Headphones, camera, phone and subtitle software are not included.

options.copy: A compact personal man-overboard beacon for offshore crews, field technicians working beside tidal waterways, and swift-water trainers operating from rescue craft. When manually activated, it transmits an AIS distress target with live GPS position to compatible nearby chartplotters and, when correctly programmed, can send a DSC alert to the vessel’s VHF radio. A high-intensity strobe assists visual location in darkness, spray and poor weather, while the slim housing clips to a lifejacket or safety harness. The box includes one AIS/DSC beacon, lifejacket mounting clip, activation lanyard, antenna guard, programming guide, test instructions and battery-expiry label. Available with a standard clip or an auto-activation pouch for compatible inflatable PFDs. Limitation: this is a short-range local alerting device, not an EPIRB or PLB; reception depends on nearby AIS-equipped vessels, and DSC features require compatible, correctly configured marine radio equipment.

options.copy: Keep river-gauge approaches, sight lines and elevated access tracks clear without hauling a ladder onto unstable banks. The RiverReach combines a rigid oval-section fibreglass pole with a curved, impulse-hardened Japanese-tooth blade for cutting overhanging branches and storm-damaged limbs from ground level. Its non-conductive pole material, positive-lock extension collars and high-visibility grip suit field crews working around wet vegetation, while the removable saw head packs neatly into a utility vehicle or rescue-training trailer. In the box are one telescopic pole, one 390 mm pruning-saw blade, a branch hook, blade guard, shoulder carry strap, hex key and care guide. Choose reach according to the vegetation around your monitoring sites. Limitation: this is a manual pruning tool, not certified electrical-insulation equipment, and it must not be used near powerlines or for cutting while positioned in moving water.

options.copy: Keep field equipment, sample crates and transport bundles clearly identified through rain, mud and rough handling. These tear-resistant synthetic logistics tags suit river-gauge components, calibration tools, rope bags, PPE tubs and equipment awaiting inspection or return to depot. Each tag has a matte writing panel that accepts permanent marker, plus a reinforced eyelet and an individually locking nylon tie for quick attachment to handles, cases, cages or coiled hose. Sequential blank fields provide space for asset ID, destination, date, status and technician initials, making handovers easier when crews are moving between remote sites or weekend rescue training locations. The box contains 50 weatherproof tags and 50 black 200 mm cable ties. Available colours help separate service status or work teams at a glance. Limitation: the tags tolerate wet weather and splashes but are not designed for prolonged underwater immersion.

options.copy: A weather-resistant pocket reference for swift-water rescue trainers, river-gauge crews and first responders managing immersion, drowning, hypothermia and trauma incidents. Designed for quick consultation beside rivers and during training, it summarises primary assessment, airway and oxygen priorities, resuscitation considerations, cold-stress staging, patient packaging, handover prompts and key observations to record for retrieval teams. Colour-coded tabs and high-contrast flowcharts remain easy to scan in rain or low light, while metric values suit Australian field practice. The box contains one spiral-bound synthetic-paper reference, a removable casualty assessment card, a waterproof notepad and a fine-tip field pencil. This guide is an educational prompt only; it does not replace accredited clinical training, current Queensland Ambulance Service protocols, medical direction or organisation-specific rescue procedures.

options.copy: Stabilise mud-soaked uniforms, rescue-training webbing, fabric equipment pouches and heritage textiles during controlled rinsing and flat drying. This conservation-grade support net helps lift weakened material without concentrating strain, making it useful after flood exposure or for routine care at a river-gauge depot. The smooth, undyed polyester mesh is chemically inert, water-permeable and edged with soft polyester tape; corner loops allow two people to transfer larger items between a rinse tray and drying rack. Each box contains one reusable support net, four removable identification tags, a soft cleaning brush and illustrated washing, handling and air-drying instructions. Select a size with enough border to support the entire textile. Limitation: this net provides physical support only and does not remove mould, chemical contamination or sewage hazards; contaminated items require appropriate PPE and specialist assessment before conservation treatment.

options.copy: Capture clear spoken audio for river-gauge inspection notes, incident debriefs, training videos and subtitle-ready rescue demonstrations. The two compact transmitters feature built-in microphones and 32-bit float onboard recording, helping preserve speech when water, wind and sudden changes in level make manual gain control impractical. Timecode support simplifies synchronising audio with action-camera footage, while the supplied lavaliers and furry windshields suit outdoor instruction around Brisbane’s waterways. In the box are two Wireless PRO transmitters, one dual-channel receiver, two Lavalier II microphones, three furry windshields, a charging case, a smart accessory case, USB-C and Lightning cables, a 3.5 mm TRS camera cable, magnetic clips and mounting accessories. Limitation: the units are not waterproof and must be kept in a sealed pouch or protected under clothing during rain, spray or swift-water exercises.

product_00404.name: RiverSafe Pro Floating Rescue Throw Bag

options.copy: Built for boat crews, river-gauge technicians and swift-water rescue trainers, the RiverSafe Pro provides fast, accurate line deployment to a person in the water. The high-visibility floating rope has a grippy sheath for wet hands, while the reinforced Cordura bag features reflective panels, drainage mesh and an adjustable closure. A foam insert keeps the packed bag afloat, and the quick-release belt lets trainers carry it securely while moving along banks, pontoons or vessel decks. In the box: one throw bag, floating polypropylene rescue rope in the selected length, removable foam flotation insert, quick-release waist belt and inspection card. Rinse with fresh water after use and inspect the rope regularly for abrasion, chemical exposure or UV damage. Limitation: this is a reach-and-throw rescue aid, not a personal flotation device, towline or load-rated lifting rope; users should be trained and must not tie it around a casualty.

options.copy: Built for pruning overhanging branches around river gauges, access tracks and training sites, the RiverReach Telescopic Arborist Pole Saw lets field crews manage light vegetation from stable ground. Its oval fibreglass pole provides a secure wet-weather grip and extends without ladders, while the hooked 330 mm impulse-hardened blade helps prevent slipping on green limbs. A bypass lopper head, operated by a low-stretch pull cord, handles smaller shoots and vines. The box includes the telescopic pole in the selected length, curved pruning-saw blade, bypass lopper head, pull cord and handle, blade guard, shoulder carry strap, adjustment tool and illustrated instructions. Components rinse clean after muddy riverside work, and high-visibility fittings are easy to spot in dense riparian growth. Limitation: intended only for branches up to 30 mm with the lopper or 150 mm with the saw; it is not electrically insulated and must never be used near power lines.

options.copy: Keep river-gauge components, field cases, throw bags and training equipment clearly identified through wet, muddy deployments. RiverTrack tags use a tear-resistant synthetic stock with a waterproof write-on surface, making them useful for asset numbers, inspection dates, site codes, destination details and quarantine status. Each tag has a reinforced eyelet and attaches without adhesive, while the bright colours help crews sort equipment for dispatch, return or servicing at a glance. The box contains 100 weatherproof tags and 100 UV-stabilised nylon cable ties, supplied in a resealable storage pouch; pens and other equipment are not included. These tags tolerate rain and short-term splashing but are not certified for prolonged submersion, lifting loads, or life-safety identification, and writing may fade after extended Queensland sun exposure.

product_00407.name: Aquatic Rescue Clinical Reference Card Set

options.copy: A waterproof, pocket-sized clinical reference set for swift-water rescue training, remote river-gauge work and first-aid response around Brisbane waterways. The colour-coded cards provide quick prompts for drowning and aspiration assessment, hypothermia management, CPR and AED sequences, spinal precautions, haemorrhage control, heat illness, snakebite, patient observations and structured handover. Printed on tear-resistant synthetic stock, the set can be rinsed clean after muddy or wet deployments and secured to a PFD, field pack or vehicle kit. In the box: 18 double-sided reference cards, a stainless-steel binding ring, a detachable mini observation chart, a permanent fine-tip marker and a protective storage sleeve. This is a prompt guide for trained personnel, not a substitute for accredited clinical education, local water-authority procedures, Queensland Ambulance Service advice or current ARC guidelines; it does not provide medication dosing or authorise treatment beyond the user’s scope of practice.

product_00409.name: AquaNav R7 Rugged Floating Handheld GPS

options.copy: Built for river-gauge inspections, flood surveys and swift-water training, the AquaNav R7 provides glove-friendly GPS navigation from a waterproof, high-visibility handheld that floats if dropped. Its 7.6 cm sunlight-readable display shows Australian marine and inland-waterway charts, while waypoint averaging helps record gauge sites, access tracks, hazards and rescue staging points. An electronic compass and barometric altimeter support navigation in steep, remote catchments, and replaceable AA batteries make extended field deployments practical. In the box are the R7 GPS unit, preloaded Australia waterways map card, buoyant wrist lanyard, belt clip, USB-C data cable, two lithium AA batteries and a quick-start guide. Limitation: the R7 does not provide satellite messaging or automatic distress alerts, and its chart data must not replace official notices, local hazard assessment or approved rescue procedures.

product_00410.name: RiverTrack Pro Handheld Electromagnetic Flow Meter

options.copy: Measure stream velocity and calculate discharge during river-gauge inspections, rating runs and flood-response surveys. The sealed electromagnetic sensor delivers stable readings in shallow, silty or weed-affected water where mechanical current meters can foul, while the backlit handheld display records velocity, depth and station notes for later CSV export. Selectable averaging and minimum/maximum modes support repeatable transect measurements from banks, bridges or a wading rod. The box includes the flow sensor, graduated sectional wading rod, handheld logger, 5 m sensor cable, USB-C data cable, rechargeable battery pack, mains charger with Australian plug, protective carry case, lanyard and quick-start guide. Limitation: the unit is intended for point-velocity measurements and does not provide live acoustic depth profiling; turbulent, aerated water may require longer averaging and multiple readings.

Its clear PET body lets you check activity at a glance, while the wide opening simplifies cleaning after long days servicing river gauges or running weekend rescue training. Ferment under pressure to reduce ester production in Brisbane’s warmer conditions, then use the floating dip tube for closed transfers with less oxygen exposure. Limitation: PET is not suitable for hot wort or abrasive scrubbing; cool wort below 40°C before filling and use only soft cleaning cloths. Limitation: it has no built-in satellite messaging or AIS receiver and should not replace official charts, local warnings or sound operational judgement.

options.copy: Measure point velocity in streams, culverts and open channels when rating river gauges, checking flood flows or conducting environmental surveys. Limitation: the sensor must remain fully submerged and correctly aligned with the flow, so it is not suitable for non-contact flood measurement or use as a rescue-current safety device.

options.copy: Keep gauge components, water-sample bottles, rescue equipment tubs and field consignments clearly identified through wet, muddy transport. RiverTrack labels use a strong acrylic adhesive and a waterproof, tear-resistant synthetic face suited to ute trays, boats, field cases and Brisbane’s humid subtropical conditions. They can be marked with permanent pen or printed using a compatible laser printer, with space for site code, asset ID, collection time, destination and handling notes. The bright surface remains legible after rain, spray and brief immersion, helping hydrology and swift-water teams sort gear quickly at depots or incident staging areas. The box contains 100 self-adhesive labels on easy-peel backing sheets plus a permanent black field marker. Choose a size and colour to separate samples, service parts or rescue loads. Limitation: the adhesive must be applied to a clean, dry surface and will not bond reliably to wet, oily or heavily textured containers.

product_00427.name: AquaRescue Waterproof Clinical Reference Card Set

options.copy: A field-ready clinical reference designed for swift-water rescue training, river-gauge callouts and other wet-environment incidents. The cards provide concise prompts for primary assessment, drowning response, hypothermia and heat illness, spinal precautions, oxygen use, bleeding control, envenomation, CPR and structured handover. Colour-coded tabs and metric values make key information easy to locate while wearing gloves, and the synthetic waterproof pages can be wiped clean after muddy or saline exposure. In the box: one spiral-bound reference card set, a detachable adult-and-paediatric observation chart, a quick-reference CPR card, a permanent marker and a stainless-steel gear clip. This is an educational aide only; it does not replace accredited training, current Australian Resuscitation Council guidance, local ambulance protocols or advice from a registered clinician, and it is not intended to direct care beyond the user’s authorised scope of practice.

product_00428.name: Riverbank Seed Vault Waterproof Storage Kit

options.copy: Keep native riparian, wetland and revegetation seed organised between field collection, propagation trials and volunteer planting days. Designed for Brisbane’s humid climate and muddy vehicle loads, this rugged IP67 case protects sealed seed packets from rain, spray and brief accidental immersion, while removable dividers separate species or collection sites. A pressure-equalisation valve and carry handle make it practical for gauge runs, boat work and rescue-training weekends. In the box: one impact-resistant waterproof case, adjustable compartment dividers, 24 reusable foil seed envelopes, 24 write-on labels, two silica-gel desiccant canisters and a humidity indicator card. Seeds should be dried to the moisture level recommended for their species before storage. Limitation: the case controls incidental moisture only; it is not a refrigerated seed bank and is unsuitable for long-term storage of recalcitrant seeds that cannot tolerate drying.

product_00430.name: FlowTrack Pro Electromagnetic River Current Meter Kit

options.copy: Measure stream velocity for discharge gauging, rating-curve checks and flood-response surveys with a rugged handheld electromagnetic current meter designed for rivers, creeks and open channels. The compact sensor has no moving parts, making it well suited to silty Brisbane catchments and shallow water where propeller meters can foul. A backlit display provides live velocity, average and minimum/maximum readings, while the graduated wading rod helps position the sensor at repeatable depths. The IP67 console and high-visibility controls are practical for wet fieldwork, and logged readings can be exported by USB for later analysis. In the box: velocity sensor, handheld logger, graduated stainless-steel wading rod, sensor cable in the selected length, USB lead, rechargeable battery pack, mains charger, wrist lanyard, protective carry case and quick-start guide. Limitation: this kit is intended for wading or fixed-line measurements and is not rated for deployment from a moving boat or for use as personal swift-water safety equipment.

product_00431.name: Flood Recovery Textile Support Mesh Kit

options.copy: A conservation-grade support system for lifting, rinsing and drying waterlogged textiles without stretching or tearing them. Ideal for stabilising flood-affected uniforms, equipment pouches, fabric logbook covers and training textiles brought back from river-gauge inspections or swift-water rescue exercises. The inert, non-abrasive polyester mesh allows water and air to pass through while keeping weakened fibres evenly supported, and it can be cut to suit irregular items. Each box contains one roll of white conservation polyester mesh in the selected size, two reusable mesh drying sleeves, six archival polyester identification tags, a soft silicone spatula for positioning folds, cotton tying tape and illustrated flood-salvage instructions. Rinse the mesh with clean water after dirty-field use and allow it to dry before storage. Limitation: this kit is intended for passive support and controlled rinsing only; it is not load-rated rescue equipment and should not be used to lift people, ropes under tension or heavily sedimented textiles without a rigid tray beneath them.

options.copy: Measure point velocity in rivers, creeks, open channels and flood-training sites without relying on a mechanical impeller. It displays live, minimum, maximum and averaged velocity in m/s, with IP67 field protection and internal logging for later CSV transfer. The box includes the electromagnetic velocity sensor, graduated two-piece wading rod, handheld logger, selected-length sensor cable, USB data lead, rechargeable battery pack, mains charger with Australian plug, protective sensor cap, lanyard, quick-start guide and hard carry case. Limitation: this is a contact instrument intended for safe wading or deployment from a stable platform; it must not be hand-held in floodwater or used where depth, velocity or unstable footing makes entry unsafe.

options.copy: A compact 406 MHz personal locator beacon for offshore crews, swift-water trainers and field technicians working around remote waterways. When manually activated, the PLB1 transmits a distress alert and GPS position through the Cospas-Sarsat satellite network, while its 121.5 MHz homing signal and high-intensity strobe assist search teams during the final approach. Its small profile fits a PFD pocket or equipment pouch, making it practical for river-gauge inspections, rescue exercises and coastal passages. In the box: rescueME PLB1 beacon with integrated battery, flotation pouch, belt clip, lanyard, test guide and registration instructions. The battery is rated for long-term standby and user tests can confirm basic readiness between trips. Limitation: this beacon requires manual activation, does not provide two-way messaging and must be registered with the Australian Maritime Safety Authority; the supplied pouch is needed for flotation because the beacon does not float unaided.

product_00451.name: Flood-Recovery Archival Textile Storage Box Kit

options.copy: Protect uniforms, rescue-training tabards, embroidered patches, canvas instrument wraps and other significant textiles after they have been cleaned and fully dried. This conservation-grade kit provides a buffered, acid-free corrugated storage box with a fitted lid, helping shield contents from dust, light and handling while allowing safer layered storage in an office, depot or home collection. The box includes 20 sheets of unbuffered acid-free tissue for interleaving and padding, two pairs of powder-free nitrile gloves, four archival identification cards and a soft graphite pencil. Fold lines allow the box to arrive flat and be assembled without adhesive or metal fasteners. Particularly useful for organising water-authority or swift-water rescue memorabilia in Brisbane’s humid climate. Limitation: the box is not waterproof or airtight and must be stored above known flood levels in a dry, climate-controlled location; do not pack damp, muddy or contaminated textiles.

options.copy: A compact 406 MHz GPS personal locator beacon for technicians, boat crews and rescue trainers working around remote rivers, estuaries and offshore waters. Once manually activated, it sends a distress alert and location through the Cospas-Sarsat satellite network, while a 121.5 MHz homing signal and high-intensity strobe assist search teams nearby. The buoyant, waterproof housing can be clipped to a lifejacket or carried in a field vest, making it suitable for gauge inspections by boat, flood-response training and coastal passages. In the box: RiverWatch beacon with sealed long-life battery, flotation pouch, lifejacket mounting clip, coiled retention lanyard, reflective identification labels, self-test guide and Australian registration instructions. Limitation: this beacon does not provide two-way messaging or confirm that rescuers have received the alert, and it must be manually deployed with a clear view of the sky.

options.copy: A rugged quick-reference set for swift-water rescue trainers, river-gauge crews and remote field teams working around Brisbane waterways. The wipe-clean cards summarise primary assessment, drowning and aspiration response, hypothermia and heat illness, spinal precautions, bleeding control, crush injury, envenomation, CPR prompts and structured handover using Australian terminology. High-contrast tables and glove-friendly tabs support rapid consultation beside a river, in a rescue vehicle or during scenario training. In the box: 24 double-sided waterproof reference cards, a colour-coded index card, stainless-steel binding ring, detachable lanyard and compact protective pouch with belt loop. Select either the pocket format for personal kits or the larger A5 format for vehicles and training stations. Limitation: this is a prompt for appropriately trained personnel, not a substitute for accredited clinical training, local service protocols, medical direction or current Australian Resuscitation Council guidelines.

product_00459.name: RiverTrack Pro 5 Rugged Handheld Marine GPS

options.copy: Built for river-gauge rounds, small-boat navigation and swift-water rescue training, the RiverTrack Pro 5 combines a sunlight-readable 5-inch display with multi-constellation GNSS, waypoint marking, track recording and Australian coastal and inland-water mapping. Its glove-friendly controls, high-visibility housing and IPX7 waterproof construction suit wet fieldwork around Brisbane creeks, tidal reaches and remote gauging stations. Save access points, hazards, gauge locations and training routes, then transfer GPX files by USB-C or Bluetooth. The replaceable battery provides up to 18 hours of typical tracking, while an emergency strobe helps locate the unit after dark. In the box: RiverTrack Pro 5 receiver, Australian marine map card, rechargeable battery pack, USB-C charging cable, lanyard, belt/rail cradle, screen protector and quick-start guide. Limitation: it does not provide sonar, AIS or satellite distress messaging and must not replace official charts, a compass or a registered emergency beacon.

product_00477.name: AquaMedic Waterproof Swift-Water Clinical Reference Cards

options.copy: A compact, waterproof clinical reference set for river-gauge crews, swift-water rescue trainers and remote field responders working around Brisbane’s waterways. The quick-access cards summarise primary assessment, drowning and aspiration management, hypothermia staging, cold-water shock, spinal precautions, crush injury, haemorrhage control, heat illness, snakebite guidance and structured patient handover. High-contrast algorithms and metric values remain readable in rain, spray and low light, while rounded corners and a tether point suit use from a PFD pocket or field pack. In the box are 24 double-sided synthetic reference cards, a stainless-steel binding ring, a breakaway lanyard, a protective storage sleeve and a contents/index card. This is an educational prompt for trained personnel and does not replace current Queensland Ambulance Service protocols, formal clinical training, medical direction or professional judgement; recommendations may require local updates.

product_00479.name: Garmin GPSMAP 67i Rugged Handheld GPS & Satellite Communicator

options.copy: Navigate remote river corridors, record gauge-site coordinates and maintain off-network contact during swift-water rescue training with the Garmin GPSMAP 67i. This waterproof handheld combines multi-band GNSS positioning, topographic mapping, an electronic compass, barometric altimeter and inReach two-way satellite messaging. Its glove-friendly buttons and sunlight-readable colour display suit wet fieldwork around Brisbane’s creeks, estuaries and flood-prone catchments, while long battery life supports multi-day deployments. The 32 GB model stores routes and additional maps; the 64 GB bundle provides more room for detailed mapping and field data. In the box: GPSMAP 67i handset, preloaded TopoActive Australia and New Zealand maps, USB-C charging/data cable, carabiner clip and documentation. Limitation: satellite messaging, tracking and SOS functions require an active inReach subscription, and this unit does not replace a marine chartplotter or approved emergency beacon.
