product_00480.name: RiverTrack Pro Electromagnetic Flow Meter Kit

options.copy: Measure river, creek and open-channel velocity during gauge maintenance, discharge surveys and flood-response assessments with this rugged handheld electromagnetic flow meter. The sealed probe provides real-time velocity, average, minimum and maximum readings without a moving impeller, making it well suited to shallow, silty or weed-affected Queensland waterways. A backlit, glove-friendly display, telescopic wading rod and internal logging memory support repeatable transect work in the field. The kit includes the velocity probe with selected cable length, IP67 display/logger, graduated telescopic wading rod, USB data cable, rechargeable battery pack, mains charger, lanyard, protective carry case, quick-start guide and calibration certificate. Limitation: this is a point-velocity instrument and does not calculate total discharge without a measured cross-section and suitable area-velocity method; it is also not intended for use while personnel are unsupported in swift or flood water.

product_00481.name: RiverSafe Archival Textile Drying Mesh Kit

options.copy: Designed for stabilising and air-drying waterlogged uniforms, rescue webbing, fabric gauge satchels and other washable textiles after river work, flooding or storage leaks. The inert polyester mesh supports wet items while allowing airflow from both sides, helping reduce distortion and avoiding direct contact with dirty benches or abrasive racks. It can be rinsed, dried and rolled for transport between gauge stations, training sheds and conservation workspaces. The box contains one hemmed polyester drying mesh in the selected size, four reusable polypropylene corner clips, two adjustable hanging straps, ten acid-free identification tags and a care guide. Available sizes suit anything from small equipment pouches to laid-flat protective clothing. Limitation: this kit does not clean, disinfect or desalinate textiles, and the mesh must not be used to suspend heavy saturated garments without a rigid support tray underneath.

options.copy: Monitor a brew from the gauge shed, riverbank or rescue-training site with this floating digital hydrometer and thermometer. Designed for beer, cider, mead and other home fermentations, it tracks specific gravity, temperature and estimated alcohol progress, then sends readings to the companion mobile dashboard over 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi. The sealed, food-safe body is easy to sanitise, while configurable alerts help Brisbane brewers catch heat spikes or a stalled fermentation without opening the vessel. In the box are one RiverShift sensor, a weighted calibration sleeve, USB-C charging cable, two spare sealing O-rings, a calibration stand and a quick-start guide. Limitation: remote reporting requires reliable 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi at the fermenter; stainless-steel vessels and thick chamber walls may reduce signal range, although readings remain stored onboard until reconnection.

product_00484.name: RiverTrack Pro Level 150 Auto-Inflatable Offshore PFD

options.copy: A high-visibility Level 150 inflatable lifejacket for boat-based river-gauge servicing, estuary crossings and offshore patrol work around South East Queensland. The low-profile yoke leaves room for tool belts and sampling equipment, while automatic water activation provides backup if the wearer enters the water unexpectedly. Features include a manual pull toggle, oral inflation tube, stainless-steel harness buckle, integrated safety harness, reflective patches, whistle, lifting loop and attachment point for a personal locator light. The removable cover is abrasion-resistant and easy to rinse after muddy or saltwater use. In the box: one AS 4758.1-compliant PFD, fitted 33 g CO₂ cylinder and automatic firing head, crotch strap, whistle, storage bag, inspection card and illustrated instructions. Limitation: this inflatable PFD is not designed for swift-water rescue, whitewater swimming or repeated immersion; use a purpose-built foam rescue PFD for training in fast-flowing rivers. Cylinder and firing head require inspection after activation and scheduled servicing.

options.copy: A waterproof quick-reference set for first aid and clinical decision support during river-gauge fieldwork, swift-water training and flood-response operations. options.copy: Built for remote river-gauge inspections, flood-response fieldwork and swift-water rescue training, the GPSMAP 67i combines a sunlight-readable 3-inch colour display, multi-band GNSS positioning, routable TopoActive Australia and New Zealand maps, and two-way inReach satellite communication. Its IPX7-rated housing, glove-friendly buttons and long battery life suit wet boats, muddy banks and areas beyond mobile coverage. Record tracks, mark gauge sites, share locations with a response team, check weather forecasts and trigger an interactive SOS through the Iridium satellite network. The box includes the GPSMAP 67i handheld navigator, preloaded maps, rechargeable lithium-ion battery, USB-C charging/data cable, carabiner clip and documentation. Limitation: inReach messaging, tracking, weather and SOS functions require an active paid satellite subscription, and IPX7 protection does not make the unit suitable for prolonged submersion or use as a dedicated floating marine chartplotter.

product_00490.name: RiverTrack Pro Handheld Electromagnetic Flow Meter

options.copy: Measure stream velocity and calculate discharge during river-gauge maintenance, rating-curve checks and flood-response surveys. The RiverTrack Pro uses a shrouded electromagnetic sensor with no moving parts, making it well suited to shallow Queensland creeks, silty channels and vegetation-lined gauging sections where propeller meters can foul. Its waterproof handheld display provides live, minimum, maximum and averaged velocity readings, while Bluetooth logging sends geotagged results to a phone or tablet for field records. In the box: electromagnetic velocity sensor, graduated wading rod, selected-length sensor cable, IP67 display/logger, rechargeable battery, USB-C charging lead, Bluetooth data app licence, protective carry case, spare connector caps and quick-start guide. Limitation: this is a wading instrument and is not rated for deployment from a moving boat or for use in water where safe footing and approved swift-water controls cannot be maintained.

product_00491.name: Flood Recovery Textile Support Mesh Kit

options.copy: Designed for stabilising and moving waterlogged uniforms, flags, fabric maps and other flood-affected textiles without concentrating their weight at fragile seams. The inert polyester mesh allows rinse water to drain and air to circulate while the item remains fully supported—useful for depot collections, field-history displays and community flood-recovery work. The box contains one washable conservation-grade polyester support mesh, two colourfast woven handling straps, six reusable archival identification tags, a soft graphite pencil and illustrated rinsing, transfer and drying instructions. Available in three mesh sizes to suit anything from folded garments to large banners. This is a textile-conservation aid only: it is not load-rated for people, rescue equipment or suspended lifting, and it cannot prevent dye migration, mould staining or damage to fabrics that require treatment by a professional conservator.

options.copy: Capture clear maintenance notes at river gauges, document site conditions and add live captions to weekend swift-water rescue briefings. The RiverNote kit combines a compact dual-channel recorder with two clip-on wireless microphones, wind reduction and an offline English caption display, making it practical for noisy weirs, roadside telemetry cabinets and outdoor training areas. Time-stamped recordings and subtitle files save to removable storage and can be transferred by USB-C for reports or training videos. In the box: field recorder/caption display, two wireless microphone transmitters, two lavalier microphones, foam and furry windscreens, charging case, magnetic and clip mounts, USB-C cable, 3.5 mm camera lead, 32 GB microSD card and padded carry pouch. Limitation: the components are splash-resistant only, not waterproof or submersible, so they must remain secured in a dry pouch around boats, floodwater and heavy rain.

product_00494.name: Ocean Signal rescueME PLB3 AIS Personal Locator Beacon

options.copy: Built for offshore crews, remote river-gauge technicians and swift-water rescue teams, the rescueME PLB3 combines 406 MHz distress alerting with local AIS transmission to help both search-and-rescue authorities and nearby equipped vessels locate you. GNSS positioning, Return Link Service confirmation, 121.5 MHz homing and visible plus infrared strobes support faster detection in rough water, low light and isolated catchments. Its compact, buoyant housing clips to a lifejacket or PFD and the sealed battery is designed for long standby storage. In the box: rescueME PLB3 beacon, flotation pouch, belt clip, lanyard, mounting accessories, registration guide and user manual. Limitation: this is a manually activated emergency beacon, not a substitute for an EPIRB where one is legally required, and AIS alerts can only be seen by compatible receivers within local radio range. Australian beacon registration is required before deployment.

product_00495.name: RiverReach Telescopic Pole Saw & Pruner Kit

options.copy: Maintain clear sightlines and safe access around river gauges, telemetry stations, boat ramps and training sites without climbing into unstable riparian trees. The RiverReach combines a triple-lock fibreglass telescopic pole with a curved, impulse-hardened pruning blade for cutting green branches up to 120 mm, plus a rope-operated bypass pruner for smaller growth up to 30 mm. Its corrosion-resistant fittings, high-visibility grip and replaceable blade suit humid Brisbane conditions and regular transport in a field vehicle. The pole collapses for storage, while the supplied blade guard helps protect nearby ropes, dry bags and rescue equipment. In the box: telescopic pole in the selected length, curved saw head and blade, bypass pruner head, 8 m pull rope, blade guard, shoulder carry bag, hex key and care guide. Limitation: the pole is not electrically insulated and must not be used near overhead powerlines or energised equipment.

Preloaded Australian marine charts show channels, navigation aids, hazards and tidal stations, while topographic mapping supports approaches to remote monitoring sites. IPX7 water resistance, glove-friendly buttons, track recording, waypoint averaging and man-overboard marking suit wet field operations around Brisbane’s rivers and Moreton Bay. Bluetooth enables route and waypoint transfer to a compatible phone, and a microSD slot accepts additional mapping. product_00501.name: RiverSafe Archival Textile Drying Mesh Kit

options.copy: A conservation-grade drying support designed for stabilising waterlogged uniforms, flags, fabric maps and other textiles after flood exposure. Particularly useful for field technicians, rescue trainers and local-history volunteers handling muddy or saturated collections, the inert polyester mesh supports fragile fibres while allowing airflow from both sides. It can be laid across a clean table, clipped to a drying rack or used as a sling when transferring wet material, reducing strain on weakened seams. The mesh is washable, quick-drying and suitable for repeated use in humid Brisbane conditions. Each box contains one hemmed polyester drying mesh in the selected size, four polypropylene corner clips, two reusable identification tags and a concise wet-textile handling guide. Limitation: this kit provides physical support only; it does not disinfect, desalinate or remove mould, and badly degraded, dyed or culturally significant textiles should be assessed by a qualified conservator before cleaning.

product_00502.name: RiverShift ATC Brewing Refractometer Field Kit

options.copy: A rugged, pocket-size optical refractometer for checking wort gravity and tracking beer, cider or ginger-beer fermentation with only a few drops of liquid. Ideal for early starts, split shifts and weekends away from the fermenter, it provides quick Brix and specific-gravity readings, while automatic temperature compensation helps in Brisbane’s changing shed temperatures. The water-resistant, rubber-armoured body and high-visibility case suit wet hands and cluttered workbenches. In the box: dual-scale ATC refractometer, shock-resistant zip case, calibration screwdriver, sampling pipette, lens cloth, distilled-water calibration vial, wrist lanyard and quick-reference conversion card. Limitation: once alcohol is present, the direct specific-gravity scale is no longer accurate; fermentation readings must be corrected using the original gravity and a brewing calculator.

options.copy: Capture clear spoken notes at river gauges, record safety briefings and produce cleaner dialogue for training-video subtitles with this dual-channel wireless microphone kit. The compact transmitters can clip to field shirts or accept the included lavalier microphones, and the receiver connects to cameras, phones or computers. product_00504.name: RiverWatch Pro 170N Automatic Inflatable Offshore PFD

options.copy: Built for gauge inspections by boat, estuary crossings and offshore fieldwork, the RiverWatch Pro provides 170N of buoyancy in a compact, high-visibility inflatable lifejacket. Its automatic firing head activates on water immersion, while a manual pull toggle and oral inflation tube provide backup options. A stainless-steel D-ring accepts a compatible safety tether, and the adjustable waist belt fits over wet-weather workwear. Reflective panels, a lifting becket, whistle and water-activated LED light improve visibility during night callouts or rescue training. The removable cover can be rinsed after exposure to salt water, mud and Brisbane’s humid conditions. In the box: one inflatable PFD with CO₂ cylinder and activation cartridge installed, crotch strap, LED distress light, whistle, inspection tag and storage bag. Limitation: this PFD is not suitable for white-water swimming or repeated training entries, and it must be serviced and rearmed after inflation.

product_00505.name: Silky Zubat Professional Curved Pruning Saw

options.copy: A fast-cutting hand saw for pruning trees, clearing storm-damaged limbs and maintaining access around river gauges, monitoring stations and rescue-training sites. The curved Japanese steel blade uses impulse-hardened, non-set teeth to cut efficiently on the pull stroke, while the rubberised handle remains secure in wet or muddy gloves. Its pivoting belt scabbard keeps the saw accessible when moving through steep riparian vegetation or climbing around low branches. Choose the blade length to suit compact field kits or heavier pruning work. In the box: one Silky Zubat curved pruning saw in the selected blade length, one locking polypropylene scabbard with removable belt holder, and care instructions. Limitation: this is a manual pruning saw rather than a felling tool; it is not electrically insulated and must not be used near live power lines. Clean and dry the blade after exposure to floodwater, silt or salt contamination.

product_00506.name: RiverTrack Weatherproof Equipment Tag & Seal Kit

options.copy: Identify, secure and track river-gauge tools, rescue-training gear, sample cases and field freight with tags designed for wet, muddy transport conditions. The tear-resistant synthetic tags accept permanent marker and include a reinforced eyelet, while the single-use numbered pull-tight seals provide visible evidence if a case, cage or equipment bin has been opened in transit. Bright colours make kit groups easy to distinguish at depots, boat ramps and remote monitoring sites. Each box contains 100 waterproof write-on tags, 100 sequentially numbered tamper-evident seals and one permanent industrial marker. Tags can be attached with the supplied seals or with your own cable ties. Suitable for rain exposure and short-term outdoor deployment, but the tags are not intended for permanent underwater use, and the seals are identifiers rather than load-rated restraints or security locks.

options.copy: A compact, waterproof clinical reference designed for swift-water rescue trainers, river-gauge crews and remote field teams working around Brisbane’s waterways. The colour-coded cards provide quick prompts for drowning and hypothermia assessment, CPR and AED sequences, oxygen guidance, spinal precautions, trauma checks, heat illness, envenomation and structured patient handover. Mud-resistant synthetic pages can be wiped clean, while rounded corners and a stainless-steel binding ring suit wet gloves and attachment to a rescue pack or gauge-maintenance kit. The box contains 18 double-sided reference cards, a removable lanyard, stainless-steel split ring, protective storage sleeve and waterproof marker. This is a prompt aid only: it does not replace accredited clinical training, current Queensland Ambulance Service protocols, medical direction or local rescue procedures, and drug doses and guidance must be checked against the user’s authorised scope of practice.

options.copy: A durable stainless steel fermenter for brewing beer, cider or ginger beer around an unpredictable field-work roster. Its wide opening makes ingredient additions and cleaning straightforward, while volume markings help you record repeatable batches. Twin side handles allow easier lifting, and the sealed lid and three-piece airlock help protect the brew from airborne contamination during fermentation. The stainless body is well suited to humid Brisbane conditions and will not retain odours or flavours between batches. In the box: one 304 stainless steel fermenter, fitted lid with silicone gasket, three-piece airlock, drilled stopper, stainless ball tap, removable sediment-reduction pickup, stick-on temperature strip, spare tap seals and cleaning instructions. Limitation: this is not a pressure-rated vessel and must not be sealed without a working airlock; it also provides no active heating or cooling, so Queensland summer brewing may require separate temperature control.

product_00513.name: RiverNote IP67 Field Audio & Caption Recorder Kit

options.copy: Capture clear spoken gauge inspections, river-condition reports and swift-water rescue debriefs for later transcription and subtitling. The compact recorder has glove-friendly controls, selectable low-cut filtering to reduce river rumble, a safety recording track, time-stamped WAV files and USB-C transfer to common captioning software. Its IP67-rated housing suits Brisbane storms, muddy banks and spray around training sites, while the high-visibility shell is easy to find in a field bag. In the box: RiverNote recorder, clip-on wind-resistant lavalier microphone, foam and furry windscreens, locking 3.5 mm lead, coiled monitoring earpiece, USB-C cable, lanyard, belt clip, rechargeable battery and padded carry case. Limitation: the recorder withstands brief accidental immersion when its port covers are sealed, but it is not designed for underwater recording, and the supplied lavalier microphone is only splash-resistant.

product_00514.name: Standard Horizon HX890E Floating GPS DSC Marine VHF Radio

options.copy: Built for offshore crews, river-gauge fieldwork and swift-water rescue training, the HX890E is a rugged handheld marine VHF radio that floats, flashes when dropped in water and carries an IPX8 waterproof rating. Integrated GPS and Class-H DSC support position sharing and distress alerts, while selectable 6 W transmit power, weather channels, waypoint navigation, MOB marking and a loud audio output help maintain communications around noisy boats and fast-moving water. The box includes the HX890E radio, rechargeable lithium-ion battery, charging cradle, mains adaptor, 12 V DC charging lead, antenna, belt clip, wrist strap and operating guide. Limitation: DSC distress functions require a registered MMSI to be programmed, and VHF range remains line-of-sight, so this radio does not replace an EPIRB or PLB for remote offshore emergencies.

options.copy: Designed for pruning overhanging branches around river gauges, access tracks and rescue-training sites, the RiverReach Telescopic Arborist Pole Saw lets ground crews clear light vegetation without carrying a ladder onto steep or waterlogged banks. Its oval fibreglass-and-aluminium shaft adjusts quickly, while the hooked 330 mm impulse-hardened blade helps hold wet limbs during pull cuts. A replaceable bypass lopper head tackles green branches up to 32 mm in diameter, and high-visibility grip sections make the tool easier to locate beside turbid water or dense riparian growth. The box contains one telescopic pole, one pruning-saw head with blade, one bypass-lopper head, pull cord, blade guard, shoulder carry strap, adjustment spanner and instruction guide. This is a manual pruning tool only: it is not electrically insulated and must not be used near live powerlines; maximum practical cutting capacity also depends on branch hardness and operator reach.

product_00516.name: All-Weather Field Equipment Dispatch Labels – 250 Pack

options.copy: Keep river-gauge components, water-sampling kits and swift-water rescue equipment clearly identified while moving between depots, vehicles and field sites. These tough synthetic dispatch labels resist rain, mud, abrasion and Queensland humidity, making them ideal for plastic tubs, hard cases, cartons and sealed instrument bags. Each label has writable fields for asset or consignment number, destination, contents, sender, date and handling notes, plus a high-visibility border for quick sorting in crowded stores or vehicle bays. Permanent acrylic adhesive helps labels stay attached during routine transport, while the matte face accepts permanent marker and ballpoint pen. The box contains 250 peel-and-stick labels on fan-folded backing, packed in a protective dispensing carton. Apply only to a clean, dry surface and press firmly around the edges. Limitation: the labels are splash resistant but not rated for prolonged submersion, and adhesion may be unreliable on wet, oily or heavily textured gear.

product_00517.name: Swift-Water Rescue Clinical Reference Field Cards

options.copy: A waterproof, pocket-sized clinical reference designed for swift-water rescue training, river-gauge fieldwork and remote first-response settings. The quick-reference cards summarise primary assessment, drowning management, hypothermia staging, cold-water shock, trauma priorities, oxygen guidance, CPR prompts, spinal precautions and structured handover using Australian terminology. High-contrast tables and colour-coded tabs are readable in rain and low light, while rounded corners and a lanyard hole suit use around boats, throw bags and wet PPE. The box contains 18 double-sided synthetic reference cards, a stainless binding ring, detachable lanyard, compact casualty-observation card, non-permanent marker and protective storage sleeve. Limitation: this is an aide-memoire for trained responders, not a substitute for accredited clinical training, local Queensland Ambulance Service protocols or medical direction; drug doses and resuscitation guidance must be checked against current authorised guidelines.

options.copy: A rugged, splash-resistant storage case for keeping vegetable, native grass and riparian revegetation seed packets organised through Brisbane’s humid summers. The gasketed shell, desiccant system and internal humidity indicator help protect seeds stored in a shed, work ute or equipment room, while removable dividers separate planting seasons, collection sites or seed lots. A pressure-equalisation valve makes the case practical for regular travel between river-gauge stations and weekend restoration projects. In the box: one impact-resistant seed vault, six adjustable dividers, twenty reusable write-on packet sleeves, two rechargeable silica-gel canisters, one humidity indicator card and a waterproof inventory label sheet. Limitation: the case is splash-resistant rather than submersible and will not preserve seed viability indefinitely; seeds must be properly dried before storage, and the silica canisters require periodic recharging in humid conditions.

options.copy: A rugged handheld GPS and satellite communicator for navigating remote river corridors, locating gauge stations and coordinating swift-water rescue training beyond mobile coverage. Multi-band GNSS delivers dependable positioning in steep valleys and under dense tree cover, while preloaded TopoActive Australia and New Zealand maps support route planning on land and beside waterways. Two-way messaging, location sharing and interactive SOS operate through the Iridium satellite network when paired with an active inReach subscription. The weather-resistant, glove-friendly design includes physical controls, a sunlight-readable colour display, electronic compass, barometric altimeter and rechargeable battery. In the box: GPSMAP 67i navigator, rechargeable lithium-ion battery pack, USB-C charging/data cable, carabiner clip and documentation. Limitation: satellite messaging, tracking and SOS require a separately purchased inReach service plan, and this unit is not a substitute for a chartplotter or approved emergency beacon.
